0.content:
Aaru (also: far side of Eternity, King Deshret's afterlife, Aaru system): Aaru is the unfinished afterlife King Deshret designed for the people of the desert, a "land of dreams" built from celestial technology. For thousands of years it held three of his Seven Pillars (Thoth, Sobek and Heryshaf). Since the destruction of Irminsul in 6.6 it has been reconfigured to store and collect the Ley Lines' information in Irminsul's place. It is not a place a traveler walks into; the entrance is the top of the Mausoleum of King Deshret, Aaru's Shut.

Deshret's aim, as the wiki summarises it, was a new kind of afterlife that would free humans from Teyvat's gods and dangers. It was never completed. The three Pillars sealed inside could leave only by having humans answer three questions to Deshret's satisfaction; that was finally achieved in the Archon Quest, after which Aaru was rebuilt for a very different job. Do not confuse Aaru with Aaru Village, the human settlement built later in the rainforest edge of the desert.

Geography: Aaru is not a place on the map. It is a constructed realm reached through the Mausoleum of King Deshret, whose highest point is called Aaru's Shut. A cyclone that guarded the mausoleum top was permanently switched off in the world quest Dual Evidence (3.1), and Aaru's Shut can be entered afterwards through the Great Hall of Truths. A map description of it says it should have been paradise on earth, the crown jewel of the desert, but now looks very different.

People: Thoth, Sobek (the Crocodile King) and Heryshaf (the Goat King), three of King Deshret's Seven Pillars, were sealed in Aaru by Deshret. Thoth says only he can hear the other two, since all three are inside. Bennu, another Pillar, handed Aaru's mainframe to Kaveh with a warning to use it with great caution. The earlier human visitors who answered Thoth's questions were Goudarz, Makhaira and Nefer.

History: King Deshret created Aaru with celestial technology that the angel Nabu Malikata gave him against Celestia's rules; she was reportedly executed by the Heavenly Principles for this. Because the project was extremely complex, Aaru was never completed. Deshret later locked Thoth, Sobek and Heryshaf inside, and set Thoth three questions (supplied, Thoth says, by the Mistress of Flowers): what causes our rise and fall, what obliterates love and hate, what determines truth and falsehood.

Quests: Quests that touch Aaru: Golden Slumber (3.0) and Dual Evidence (3.1) in the Great Red Sand; Headlong Into the Sands, where Thoth tells the story of the three questions; and the Song of the Welkin Moon Archon Quest act "Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana" (6.6).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Aaru is the active repository of the Ley Lines' information, replacing Irminsul. The sealed Pillars are free and living at the Temple of Silence.

The Heavenly Principles no longer hold direct control over fate through Irminsul, as the wiki reads the 6.6 outcome. Whether Thoth, Sobek and Heryshaf will ever leave the temple is not stated; Thoth and Heryshaf choose to stay for now, and they decline to move their statues into the temple out of respect for Hermanubis's memory.

1.content: Aaru Village is a different place from Aaru: the largest human settlement in the Sumeru desert, home to the followers and descendants of King Deshret and to scholars exiled from the Akademiya. It is built around an old fortress from the Gurabad period, and the wiki notes its name was chosen from the "ancient dream of the gods," the settlers swearing off kings and preserving the embers of their civilisation. Use Aaru only for the afterlife system.

2.content: Aaru's Shut is the highest point of the Mausoleum of King Deshret and the way into Aaru. After Dual Evidence it is reachable through the Great Hall of Truths. The wiki notes that "shut" derives from an ancient Egyptian word for shadow.

3.content: Thoth, Sobek and Heryshaf could be released from Aaru only if humans gave the answer King Deshret intended to three questions: what causes our rise and fall, what obliterates love and hate, what determines truth and falsehood. Goudarz, Makhaira and Nefer each answered one of them over the centuries; the first two answers were rejected, the third person, Nefer, eventually found the intended one, "time", and the Pillars were freed in 6.6.

4.content: After Irminsul was burned in the 6.6 Archon Quest, Aaru took over its role of collecting and storing the Ley Lines' information, shifting from a dead king's unfinished afterlife into the world's record-keeper. The wiki links this to the Akasha System, which resembles Aaru's architecture, and reports that the Heavenly Principles no longer have direct control over fate.

5.content:
Aaru Village: Aaru Village is the largest human settlement in Sumeru's desert, in the Land of Lower Setekh of the Great Red Sand. Its people are the followers and descendants of the desert god King Deshret, and it is also where the Akademiya sends scholars it has exiled, known as Village Keepers. Uncle Anpu is the village chief, and Candace guards it. It is the Traveler's base while the Akademiya's plot against the Dendro Archon unfolds in Chapter III.

Candace says the mountain and lake where the village sits once belonged to King Deshret's territory. The village is built in an old desert style with intricate patterned facades, and sandstorms and Eremite politics shape life around it.

Geography: The village stands in the Land of Lower Setekh, on the desert side of the Wall of Samiel. Houses are stacked in tiers: an upper tier with the Village Chief's House, a middle tier of shops and homes, lower tiers by the water and outskirts beyond. Water comes from a stepwell below the village, supplied by ancient desert-kingdom infrastructure. Caravan Ribat, at the foot of the Wall to the rainforest side, is the usual road in.

Places: The Village Chief's House is the village's meeting place, where Uncle Anpu lives and where visitors shelter from sandstorms. Azalai's shop sells goods and plants; the stepwell and White Lift supply water.

People: Uncle Anpu is the village chief; he says he will help with food, lodging and advice, and urges anyone caught in loose sand or strong wind to take shelter in the village. Candace describes herself as a village guardian with spear and shield, and Dehya, a mercenary, invites friends to visit her in Aaru Village. Residents include Village Keepers such as Khalil (the mad scholar the boy Isak calls "Grandpa"), guards such as Belkacem, Raef and Kazim, and ordinary villagers such as Nermin, Granny Kulsoom, Shani, Azalai and Kazan, Kazim's son.

Governance: Uncle Anpu is chief, with guards on watch day and night. Inscription and weapon text say the village's founders swore off the rule of kings. Candace and Dehya step in when visitors start fighting, as when Cyno and Alhaitham clash.

Culture: The village keeps the faith and traditions of King Deshret's people and, according to weapon and inscription text, its founders awaited the return of Al-Ahmar. Its founders chose the name Aaru for the "ancient dream of the gods". Uncle Anpu refused the Akademiya's request to take the Village Keepers back, and the village looks after them.

History: Candace says the earliest inhabitants were survivors from Akhtamun, the city King Deshret built from golden sand and crimson rock somewhere in the desert. Other text describes refugees from the warring successor cities who, tired of bloodshed, left the desert under a well-educated blind heir from Tulaytullah, swore off kings and named their new home Aaru. At some later time the Akademiya made it a place of exile for scholars.

Atmosphere: Warm, dry and tiered, with patterned facades; when sandstorms rise, the village chief urges everyone to shelter in the village. Inside a village home, Candace says a home is about atmosphere: "Warm, intimate, safe, secure, peaceful...", and that everything she seeks to protect is there.

Dangers: Sandstorms (Uncle Anpu says they, and occasional earthquakes, have recently grown more severe and frequent); rifthounds that come with the storms; Eremite radicals devoted to King Deshret; and, during Chapter III, the Akademiya's agents.

Travel: Reach it from Caravan Ribat, the checkpoint between forest and desert. Dar al-Shifa, the abandoned Eleazar hospital, lies in the desert nearby.

Quests: In the Archon Quest the Traveler arrives with Paimon and Alhaitham; Cyno attacks Alhaitham, Dehya intervenes, and when a sandstorm hits Candace brings everyone into the chief's house. Village Keepers go missing, and the Traveler follows the trail to the desert. Smaller World Quests (Blooming Sands, Desert Bloom, Lost in the Sands) show daily life and the start of the Golden Slumber archaeology line. In the limited-time 3.6 event A Parade of Providence, Tighnari, who passed out from the heat during the Interdarshan Championship's desert round, is brought back to the village to rest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the village still stands, led by Uncle Anpu and defended by Candace. Its missing Village Keepers were recovered in 3.1.

At the end of 6.6's Welkin Moon story Candace and Dehya say they are heading back to Aaru Village to hand out supplies and help people. No later threat to the village is shown in the material checked.

6.comment: Aaru Village: Dreams, Emptiness, Deception at Aaru Village
6.content: When the Traveler reaches Aaru Village with Alhaitham, Cyno (the General Mahamatra, in self-imposed exile) attacks Alhaitham and Dehya intervenes; and a sandstorm drives everyone into the Village Chief's House, where Candace asks them to explain their quarrel. Uncle Anpu then tells them that the Village Keepers, scholars exiled by the Akademiya, have been disappearing. A boy, Isak, asks for help finding the Village Keeper he calls "Grandpa".

7.content: Village Keepers are mad scholars the Akademiya has long exiled to Aaru Village; Cyno says they arrive incoherent but invariably calm down after some time there. Most still seem eccentric or unwell, yet some lucid moments are valuable: a former Kshahrewar Keeper helped build the White Lift. After King Deshret and the Three Magi, Khalil is listed among the village's Keepers.

8.comment: Aaru Village: Uncle Anpu and the Village Chief's House
8.content: Uncle Anpu is the village chief and lives in the Village Chief's House. He is practical and humble, offering food, lodging and warnings about sandstorms; Nahida's All Schemes to Know reveals him privately wondering whether he is fulfilling his obligations as village chief. He appears in the Chapter III Act III and IV quests.

9.comment: Aaru Village: The White Lift and the Stepwell
9.content: Aaru Village's water comes from a stepwell fed by ancient infrastructure below the village. The White Lift, built long ago with the help of a Village Keeper, lowers to the water. Kazim keeps it running, checking it each dawn and dusk, and plans to pass the work to his son Kazan.

10.comment: Aaru Village: Blooming Sands and Daily Life
10.content: In Blooming Sands, the guard Raef asks the Traveler to fetch a flower pot and seeds from Azalai's shop for Nermin, his girlfriend, who is in poor health and convalescing at home. Nermin then cares for the plant with tips from Granny Kulsoom, and the daily commission Desert Bloom has the Traveler fetching water for her from the distant stepwell, chasing a kitten that chews leaves, or making a drink with Zaytun Peach for Raef.

11.comment: Aaru Village: Competition on the Sands
11.content: During the limited-time event A Parade of Providence (3.6), the second round of the Interdarshan Championship takes place in the desert around Aaru Village. Tighnari runs out of water and passes out from the heat, dizzy from the disturbed ley lines. The Wanderer hands the Traveler water to give him, and Tighnari withdraws from the round; Cyno and the Traveler escort him back towards the village to rest.

12.content:
Aaru's Shut (also: Aaru's Reflection): Aaru's Shut is the highest point of the Mausoleum of King Deshret in the Hypostyle Desert of Sumeru. The Traveler and Paimon first come here in the world quest Dual Evidence, lifted up from the Great Hall of Truths, and it can be visited freely afterwards.

Its name plays on Aaru, the dream-afterlife of the desert dwellers; the second word comes from an Egyptian word for shadow. The Scarlet Sand Slate says this place should have been paradise on earth, the jewel of the desert, but that today it looks very different.

Geography: The summit of the whole Mausoleum complex, above Duat Hall and the Great Hall of Truths. After Dual Evidence it is permanently reachable by entering the central section of the Great Hall of Truths. Before the quest, a cyclone turned at the top of the pyramid and could not be approached.

History: In Dual Evidence the slate sends the party through Duat Hall and the three trial chambers, then through the Great Hall of Truths. Lighting three primal torches there wakes a device that carries them to the summit. The Primal Construct they defeat, billed in the game as Field Annihilation Array: The Evincing Shadow, is followed by a precious chest holding a stone slate, the Record of Aaru's Shut.

Quests: Dual Evidence, the first quest of Old Notes and New Friends (begins after Golden Slumber). Completing it permanently turns off the cyclone over the Mausoleum.

Status as of 7.1: Open and safe to visit as of Version 7.1.

Nothing in the sources up to Version 7.1 changes the summit. The real Aaru is a separate matter handled in its own entry and in the Sumeru Archon Quest.

13.content:
Abdju Pit (also: Abdju Road): Abdju Pit is a deep sinkhole at the edge of the Great Red Sand in Sumeru's Land of Lower Setekh. Before the quest Lost in the Sands the spot was an ordinary stretch called Abdju Road; afterwards the ground has opened into a pit leading down into ruins of King Deshret's ancient civilisation. Its name echoes Abydos, an ancient Egyptian city.

The pit is where the Traveler finds the archaeology team of the Akademiya researcher Tirzad, trapped with their guides and a merchant's Sumpter Beasts, in the first part of the Golden Slumber quest series.

Geography: The pit lies where the desert's edge meets the road toward the sands' heart, in the Land of Lower Setekh within the Great Red Sand. Down in the hole are broken temple structures, long corridors, torch-lit chambers, sealed doors and an exit cavern through which a dry wind blows out to the open desert. Official map text says that at the desert's very edge stands a palace whose main form is entombed beneath the sands, and that King Deshret's realm lies ahead.

Places: Red Desert Threshold, a one-time domain, lies in the pit. Its description says the wise once debated here in a corner of the ancient city of Gurabad and outlined the desert king's dream; after the dream burst, the place became a secret holding cell, and it is now infested with monsters though old treasures remain.

History: The pit belongs to the ruins of King Deshret's civilisation, which the Great Red Sand still hides. Canon gives no date for the collapse of Abdju Road into a pit, and the pit itself is a recent development within the story: it appears only after Lost in the Sands.

Dangers: Ancient guardian constructs (the quest names Primal Construct Prospectors and Reshapers), scorpions and lizards in the buried passage, sunstroke and thirst for anyone stranded, and the risk of being stuck with no way back to the surface. Treat the pit as a trap that is easy to fall into and hard to climb out of.

Quests: Lost in the Sands (3.1), the first part of Golden Slumber. The merchant Bonifaz, a Mondstadter in Aaru Village, hires the Traveler to find a missing associate, Nachtigal, and the Sumpter Beasts leased to Tirzad's team. Footprints lead to the pit; below, the Traveler finds the stranded party. The team leaves together, guided by the wind, after the Traveler finds a strange friendly machine that Jeht names Benben.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Abdju Pit is an explorable ruin in the Great Red Sand and nothing later has changed it.

The pit remains open in the world after Lost in the Sands, and its domain Red Desert Threshold is available to players who have started Golden Slumber.

14.content: Tirzad's archaeology team fell into the pit while working on his research, the Scarlet Sand Slate. They are Tirzad, the Eremite Jebrael and his daughter Jeht, with Mirsad and Omid; the merchant Nachtigal and the leased Sumpter Beasts are in another part of the ruins. Jeht befriends a small guardian machine she names Benben; it reacts to the slate, hinting that the slate commands devices in King Deshret's ruins.

15.content:
Alhaitham's Home: Alhaitham's Home is the house where Alhaitham lives with Kaveh, whom he calls only his roommate. It sits near Treasures Street in Sumeru City. Its interior is closed to players except in a few quests. It was first an Akademiya research center and became a home after Kaveh gave up his claim to it.

Kaveh pays rent to Alhaitham and handles the housework; the two bicker over the furniture, which Kaveh finds ugly. The arrangement is a secret Kaveh tries to keep from visitors.

Places: Inside are a central living room, a study to the right, and hallways with a painting, a broom, a red floor cushion and a shelf of books. Two further doors cannot be opened.

People: Alhaitham, who bought the furnishings, and Kaveh, who has his own room. Kaveh retreats to his room when Alhaitham has guests and avoids answering the door when Alhaitham is out, to avoid being discovered living there.

History: The Akademiya first provided the building as a research center for the joint research of Alhaitham and Kaveh. It fell into disuse for lack of a shared vision and manpower, was allotted to the two, and became a home after Kaveh forfeited his rights. Kaveh later sold his own home and possessions to fund the second construction of the Palace of Alcazarzaray and went bankrupt, drinking at Lambad's Tavern until Alhaitham met him there and offered a room on condition that he pay rent.

Quests: Enterable in Alhaitham's Story Quest "Pride and Prejudice" (Vultur Volans Chapter, 3.4) and in Kaveh's hangout quest "Past Mementos". It also appears in the limited-time event quest "Suspicions Aroused", part of the 3.6 event A Parade of Providence.

Atmosphere: A lived-in, slightly cluttered scholar's house, with books piled up waiting to be sorted and a running quarrel over decor between two men who would never call themselves friends.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 both men still live here as far as the pages consulted show.

16.content:
Amrita Pool: The Amrita Pool is a small clear spring in a cave near Vourukasha Oasis in Sumeru. It is an overflow of the Amrita that surrounds the oasis, and the Pari say it is where they were granted life.

Fedhri, a Pari, looks after the pool. Memories belonging to the Khvarena are said to flow back through it to the Harvisptokhm, the great structure beneath the oasis. Players unlock it with the world quest Heart of Amrita, available after The Splendorous Sky That Day.

Geography: A pool in a cave beside Vourukasha Oasis, in the Realm of Farakhkert in the Girdle of the Sands. It is only a spring that overflows from the larger Amrita around the oasis.

People: Fedhri, a Pari, says she is in charge of looking after the pool and has not left the place since Lady Zurvan sealed the oasis. She addresses the Traveler as the outlander offerer, a human bonded to a Pari.

History: Item text records that the Amrita was created in the cataclysm five hundred years ago, when Egeria, the previous Hydro Archon, was killed at Tunigi Hollow fighting the monsters and corruption pouring into Teyvat. Greater Lord Rukkhadevata grew the Harvisptokhm from it, which anchored Egeria's consciousness to the mortal realm and let her act as a seal over the dark hollow.

Quests: Heart of Amrita (3.6): Fedhri explains the pool and introduces the offering system, The Gift of Amrita, in which Plumes of Purifying Light are offered to the pool for rewards. That system is a gameplay mechanic.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the pool remains a spring in Vourukasha Oasis, tended by Fedhri. No later changes were found.

17.content: Fedhri is the Pari keeper of the Amrita Pool, who has stayed at the pool since Lady Zurvan sealed the oasis. She treasures memories of the age when Pari and humans lived side by side in the oasis.

18.content:
Apam Woods (also: Apam Forest): Apam Woods is a huge rainforest in Sumeru's Dharma Forest, within the Ashavan Realm. Giant trees reach for the sky and, in the official description, the rain beneath their canopy has never ceased. The rain is not natural: it comes from the Varunastra, a pillar of water raised by an old device, the Varuna Contraption, which the Traveler helps the Aranara repair.

The area is home to fungi, ruin machines, Eremites and tigers, and its name comes from the Sanskrit word for "of the waters."

Geography: A dense, wet jungle of towering trees with an underground layer. The Varunastra, a column of water, stands in the southern part, at The Rain's End, where the main contraption is found. Between 00:00 and 06:00 and between 12:00 and 18:00 (late night or late day) it rains and the water level is low; from 06:00 to 12:00 and 18:00 to 00:00 (early night or early day) it is dry and the water is high, flooding lower ground. After the quest the Traveler can fix either state.

Places: The Rain's End, where the Varuna Contraption sits. The Grove of Dreams, a cavern with a real and a dream version that the Traveler switches between with the Rhythm of the Great Dream played on a vintage lyre at a Silapna. The Tower of Abject Pride, a weapon-material domain whose description recalls three sage-kings of the desert, one of whom (Hermanubis) stayed wise and lovely to the end, and says the tower was the temporary home of one of them while building an earthly paradise, and earlier a small shrine against wind and sand.

History: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata built the Varuna Contraption to summon timely rains in part of the desert; the forest that now covers the area grew from that rain. Item text adds that after the forest labyrinth was made, the forest's lord Viaghara was born from the moon's reflection on the water. In the present, the original makers are long dead and the Nara Varuna is gone, so the contraption has gone unmaintained.

Dangers: Rishboland tigers, spinocrocodiles, shaggy sumpter beasts, floating and stretchy fungi, Eremite axe vanguards and sword-dancers, and Ruin Guards. The rain and the shifting water level change which routes are flooded; the Traveler is warned the air is off before the repair.

Quests: Varuna Gatha (3.0): after The World of Aranara, the Traveler and Paimon rescue Arapandu from fungi and learn the contraption is failing; three smaller quests (Memory of Stone, Irate Iron Chunk, Slumbering Roots) lead to A Prayer for Rain on the Fecund Land, the climax. Arapandu then teaches the Rhythm of the Source Water for controlling the device, and the Aranara head to Vanarana for a festival.

Status as of 7.1: Apam Woods is a repaired rainforest as of 7.1, with its rain regulated by the Varuna Contraption.

Nothing later than 3.0 has changed the area.

19.content: A device made by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata that raises the Varunastra, a giant pillar of water, to bring a constant cycle of rain to a former desert. It runs on a twelve-hour cycle and its water draw lowers the surrounding water level. Its energy sources, the branches and leaves, were misaligned until the Traveler corrected them; the Aranara maintain it and know its tune, played on a vintage lyre.

20.content: An underground cavern that connects to the Ruins of Dahri to the west. According to Arapandu it is a place where one may enter dreams, and it, like Vanarana, exists in a real and a dream form.

21.content:
Apep's Resort (also: The Lost Hermitage): Apep's Resort is a large, mysterious cavern in the far north of the Desert of Hadramaveth, under the Great Red Sand in Sumeru. A glowing tunnel inside it is the entrance to the Realm of Beginnings, the domain tied to the Dendro Dragon Sovereign Apep.

In-game viewpoint text says a friend of King Deshret once built a court in a great cavern beneath the dunes, with Wenut as court officials and flying serpents as companions, and that both creatures have since lost their wit and vigour. The wiki links that friend to Apep.

Geography: A great cavern in the northernmost part of the Desert of Hadramaveth, in the Great Red Sand region. The desert above is the result of a Celestial Nail that fell long ago and turned lush forest to sand. The cavern's glowing tunnel opens onto the Realm of Beginnings.

People: No living community is established here. The viewpoint text recalls Wenut as courtiers and flying serpents as companions in an earlier age. Elsewhere in the 3.x desert story, Liloupar, a jinni from King Deshret's era, calls the Wenut the children of Apep.

History: Apep ruled Sumeru before the Heavenly Principles arrived and bore the first elemental lifeforms inside herself. She survived the war against the Heavenly Principles and the desertification of Sumeru. She later agreed that King Deshret could build his civilisation in her domain, in return for the knowledge and elemental power he accumulated after his death.

Travel: Reached overland through the northern Desert of Hadramaveth. The Realm of Beginnings domain unlocks after the Archon Quest chapter What Shape Does the Self Hold.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the cavern is unchanged, and Apep rests in her restored oasis and is not hostile. Nothing found in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content changes the site.

22.comment: Apep's Resort: Apep's Resort and the Realm of Beginnings
22.content: Apep's Resort is the cavern entrance; the Realm of Beginnings is the domain reached through it, where the player relives the fight with the Guardian of Apep's Oasis. The domain text frames it as memory of the battle, recalled in the land where Apep rests.

23.content:
Ardravi Valley: Ardravi Valley is a river valley in the Dharma Forest of Sumeru, named for the great Ardravi river that carved it. Official text calls the river Sumeru's great waterborne mercantile route, and the valley holds the busy harbour of Port Ormos, the quiet fishing hamlet of Vimara Village and the mountain where a huge Khaenri'ahn Ruin Golem lies dormant.

The Forest Watchers (the Forest Rangers) look after the valley's natural life, and the official expedition text says many lovely creatures live there. The name echoes Ardravi in the title of the Iranian water goddess Anahita.

Geography: The valley was formed by erosion from the Ardravi, which cuts through the whole of Sumeru; following the river downstream leads to the southern shore. The river runs from Sumeru City to Port Ormos between two giant trees, and the valley around it is forest and riverbank. Its wild specialties are Nilotpala Lotus and Rukkhashava Mushrooms, and the wiki lists an Aeonblight Drake as the area's boss enemy.

Places: Port Ormos, the largest port in Sumeru, a hub for trade and travel that sits beneath two giant trees with a river running to it from Sumeru City. Vimara Village, a small, tranquil fishing town on the river between Sumeru City and the port, where caravans pass between the two. Devantaka Mountain, home to the Ruin Golem.

People: Port Ormos residents are mostly traders and labourers who grew up there, together with Eremite mercenaries from various factions, merchants of many nationalities, dockworkers and ship crews. Students sometimes come to the port when academic life becomes too stressful, and some consider that lucky. Vimara Village is a village of fishers, hunters, merchants and a few researchers.

Governance: Parts of Port Ormos fall under Akademiya supervision, but smuggling and other illegal activity are more common there than in Sumeru City, and prices are lower. A port master and deputy port master run the harbour day to day.

Culture: The harbour's official blurb has a speaker scoff that the lectures of the sages are boring and propose setting off across the seven seas with wine and floral honey: the port is Sumeru's free-and-easy counterpart to the scholarly capital.

History: Canon does not date the valley's formation. Devantaka Mountain's Ruin Golem is a leftover of Khaenri'ahn machinery; the scholar Pir Kavikavus of Kshahrewar studied it before an accident ended his work, and the Akademiya's later research there is carried on by the Kshahrewar researcher Jazari (see Devantaka Mountain).

Dangers: The Aeonblight Drake, a mechanical beast, and other ruin machines around Devantaka Mountain; wild animals in the forest; Abyss Order mages seeking the Golem's core before it was sealed; smugglers and Eremite mercenaries in the port.

Travel: The Ardravi is the main route between Sumeru City and the sea: caravans stop at Vimara Village, and ships dock at Port Ormos. Vimara Village has a Waverider waypoint for travel on the river.

Quests: Many world quests are tied to the valley, among them Vimana Agama (Ararycan, Jazari and the Ruin Golem), Until Vana is Healed, The World of Aranara, A Refuge in the Sands, Lost in Prosperity and the series about the Port Ormos jeweller Royinjan. These are listed by title in the wiki category; only Vimana Agama and Until Vana is Healed are summarised in the Devantaka Mountain entity.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the valley is open and peaceful, with its trade route functioning and the Ruin Golem idle.

No content from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes the area.

24.content: Sumeru's largest port, under two giant trees, with a river running to it from Sumeru City. The Akademiya supervises parts of it, but smuggling is more common than in the capital and prices are lower. Most long-term residents are traders and labourers; Eremite mercenaries are also present, and stressed students come to escape.

25.content: A small, tranquil fishing town on the river between Sumeru City and Port Ormos. Caravans heading between the two pass through, and the village has fishing spots and a Waverider waypoint.

26.content:
Ashavan Realm: The Ashavan Realm is the southern part of Sumeru's Dharma Forest, a materially rich land of hills, woods and wetlands. Its western edge is defended by mighty ramparts, the Wall of Samiel, which keep out the corroding sandstorms of the desert. Its main places are Apam Woods, the frontier village Caravan Ribat and the Amurta research garden Pardis Dhyai.

Official expedition text says legend holds that many mythical creatures live in Sumeru's woods and that only a lucky few ever see them. The name comes from the Zoroastrian term ashavan, "possessing truth".

Geography: A damp region of hills, woods and wetland. The Wall of Samiel runs along its western edge, separating the rainforest from the Great Red Sand. The Apam Woods rainforest, where it never stops raining unless the Varuna Contraption is told otherwise, takes up much of the interior, and the Ruins of Dahri lie to its west, linked by an underground cavern.

Places: Apam Woods, the rain-soaked forest with the Varuna Contraption. Caravan Ribat, a fortified village at the foot of the Wall of Samiel. Pardis Dhyai, the Garden of Deep Thought, a research site for Amurta scholars. The Ruins of Dahri and the Yasna Monument, two sparsely documented subareas.

People: Caravan Ribat is full of Eremite mercenaries, researchers and merchants; the Amurta scholars work at Pardis Dhyai; Eremites and Forest Rangers also appear around the region. The Aranara, small forest spirits, tend the Varuna Contraption in Apam Woods.

Governance: The Akademiya actively maintains the Wall of Samiel and forbids its destruction. Caravan Ribat functions as the checkpoint between forest and desert.

History: The wall is supposedly the work of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, built to keep sandstorms from ruining the rainforests. The Varuna Contraption, which gives Apam Woods its rain, is also her design; it fell into disrepair until the Aranara and the Traveler repaired it in Varuna Gatha.

Dangers: Fungi that grow when the rain goes unmanaged, Ruin Hunters and Ruin Cruisers in the ruins, Eremites, wild animals such as tigers, and sandstorms at the wall.

Travel: Travel to the desert runs through Caravan Ribat and over or past the Wall of Samiel toward Aaru Village. Travel in the rain-fed woods depends on the contraption's rain cycle.

Quests: Varuna Gatha (3.0) is the region's main storyline: it repairs the Varuna Contraption in Apam Woods. Other world quests listed in the wiki category include Legends of the Stone Lock, Memory of Stone, Pride and Prejudice, Where the Future Stars Fall and Hilichurl Hullaballoo; only their titles were reviewed.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Ashavan Realm is intact, with rain regulated and the wall standing.

Nothing from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes the region.

27.content: A fortified village at the foot of the Wall of Samiel, full of Eremites, and the checkpoint through which people travelling between the forest and the desert, including Aaru Village, must pass. The wall is said to have been made by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata to stop sandstorms from destroying the rainforest, and the Akademiya maintains it.

28.content: A research site for Amurta scholars, described on the official map as the "garden of deep thought" filled with countless flowers. Its local specialty is Padisarah.

29.content:
Asipattravana Swamp (also: Asipatravana Swamp): Asipattravana Swamp is a thorn-filled canyon swamp just north of Vourukasha Oasis in Sumeru's Realm of Farakhkert. It is guarded by Mihir, a Pari called a familiar of thorns. In the quest Asipattravana Itihasa it is smothered by a purple mist of Abyssal origin until the Traveler, Paimon and the Pari Sorush cleanse it.

The name comes from the Sanskrit asipatravana, the forest whose leaves are swords, one of the hells of Naraka.

Geography: A swamp in a canyon thick with thorns, immediately north of the Oasis. Local life includes consecrated horned crocodiles, and the Mourning Flower is the area's local specialty.

History: When the Traveler and Paimon arrive with Sorush, the swamp is blanketed in Abyssal mist. To protect it, Mihir had sealed herself and the source of the Abyssal energy behind a Gray Gate. The Traveler and Sorush awaken Khvarena to disperse the mist, cleanse the defilement and free her.

People: Mihir, a Pari described as a familiar of thorns. After the quest she tells the Traveler that the Oasis's sights are as they always were and says Sorush is dedicated though her methods need refining.

Dangers: Abyssal mist and defilement, consecrated horned crocodiles, and a Gray Gate that blocked the source of the energy until the quest cleared it.

Quests: Asipattravana Itihasa (3.6), part of Khvarena of Good and Evil. Sorush and the Traveler follow floating Khvarena through the swamp, awaken its power to disperse the mist, and free Mihir.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the swamp is clear of the purple mist and Mihir is free.

Mihir stays to rest. Nothing after 3.6 has changed the area.

30.content: A Pari known as a familiar of thorns who guards Asipattravana Swamp. During the Abyssal mist she locked herself and the source of the energy behind a Gray Gate. Freed, she speaks in a formal, measured way.

31.content:
Avidya Forest (also: Avidya): Avidya Forest is the lush rainforest at the heart of Sumeru and the first area the Traveler reaches in the nation. It holds Sumeru City, the "City of Wisdom" built into the Divine Tree and seat of the Sumeru Akademiya, and Gandharva Ville, the base of the Forest Rangers. Rain, mushrooms and glowing lotus fill the woods, and scholars, merchants and rangers share the paths. Nahida, Sumeru's Dendro Archon, lives in the palace at the top of the tree.

The Forest Rangers guard the woods from dangerous wildlife, careless visitors and the creeping Withering. Beyond the forest lie the Lokapala Jungle, the river valley of Ardravi and, beyond the Wall of Samiel, the desert.

Geography: Avidya Forest lies in the Dharma Forest subregion, Sumeru's rainforest. The wiki lists five subareas: Sumeru City, Gandharva Ville, Chinvat Ravine (a ravine below the city, at the base of the Divine Tree), Gandha Hill and Yazadaha Pool. Local specialties include Padisarah, Nilotpala Lotus, Kalpalata Lotus and Rukkhashava Mushrooms; shroomboars and many kinds of mushroom-creatures (Fungi) roam the woods.

Places: Sumeru City (on the Divine Tree), Gandharva Ville (the Forest Rangers' outpost, "The City Above the Forest"), Chinvat Ravine (under the tree), and the quieter Gandha Hill and Yazadaha Pool.

People: Akademiya scholars and students, merchants, farmers and dockworkers, Eremite mercenaries, and the Forest Rangers, whose chief officer Tighnari mentors the ranger Collei. Nahida lives at the top of the Divine Tree; Naphis is Grand Sage.

Governance: Sumeru City is under the jurisdiction of the Sumeru Akademiya, which is both Teyvat's great academy and Sumeru's government. The Corps of Thirty, an Eremite mercenary brigade under contract with the sages, keeps the peace in the city; the Forest Rangers, civil servants, protect the forest.

History: Legend says Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, the original Dendro Archon, built the Varuna Contraption to nurture the rainforest, and the first lord of the forest, the tiger Viaghara, was born from the moon's reflection there. About 500 years ago, in the cataclysm, Rukkhadevata died and the sages of the Akademiya kept her successor, the child-like Lesser Lord Kusanali (Nahida), confined in the Sanctuary of Surasthana. The Traveler's arrival in Avidya Forest opens Chapter III of the Archon Quest (3.0), which ends with the old sages' plot defeated and Nahida free.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Avidya Forest is peaceful, rebuilding after the 6.6 Irminsul crisis.

After Irminsul was burned the people of Sumeru went back to rebuilding and normal life, and Collei was promoted to full Forest Ranger. No 7.0 or 7.1 content touches the forest; the Archon Quest has moved on to Snezhnaya.

32.comment: Avidya Forest: Sumeru City and the Divine Tree
32.content: Sumeru City is known across Teyvat as the "City of Wisdom" and is built on top of the colossal Divine Tree, which holds up the Sumeru Akademiya. It is organised by height: the Grand Bazaar and other everyday buildings at the bottom, the Akademiya (with the House of Daena library) in the middle, and the Sanctuary of Surasthana, Nahida's palace, at the very top. Other places include the Bimarstan hospital, the docks, the Zubayr Theater, Lambad's Tavern, Puspa Cafe and the Corps of Thirty's headquarters, the Citadel of Regzar. Nahida was kept in the sanctuary for 500 years before Chapter III.

33.comment: Avidya Forest: Gandharva Ville and the Forest Rangers
33.content: Gandharva Ville, "The City Above the Forest", is the main outpost of the Forest Rangers (also called Vanara), civil servants who protect Sumeru's forests. Higher-ranking members, the Forest Watchers, wear lighter green. They help travelers in need, suppress Withering Zones, monitor beast populations and report to Pardis Dhyai. Tighnari is the Forest Watcher and chief officer; Collei is a ranger he trained. Merchants, adventurers, Eremite mercenaries and researchers come and go.

34.comment: Avidya Forest: Chinvat Ravine, Gandha Hill and Yazadaha Pool
34.content: Chinvat Ravine lies below Sumeru City at the base of the Divine Tree. In the ancient literary canon of Sumeru, "Chinvat" is the bitter sea of ignorance that a seeker must cross to see the light of truth on the far shore; those who navigate the forests now use the word for the ravine under the tree, perhaps in honour of the elation of finally reaching the city of wisdom. Gandha Hill and Yazadaha Pool are outlying spots in the forest; the pool has ruin torches to light and Eremite, hilichurl and Fungi enemies. The wiki gives little lore for either beyond their names.

35.content:
Ay-Khanoum (also: City of the Moon Maiden, City of Amphitheaters, Amphitheater City, Moon Maiden City): Ay-Khanoum ("City of the Moon Maiden" in the Jinn's ancient tongue) was an ancient city of Sumeru, jointly ruled by Nabu Malikata and King Deshret and built for the Jinn. It is also called the City of Amphitheaters. It is now ruins, probably in the Hypostyle Desert, and only appears in Sumeru through lore.

Later it became one of the desert city-states of the age after Deshret, ruled by a Khagan called Garshasp, who gathered several cities under him before dying; his capital burned afterwards.

History: Item lore says the "Mistress of Flowers and Oases" (Nabu Malikata) and the desert's king (Deshret) built Ay-Khanoum for the Jinn. In the legend of Nabu Malikata, a Seelie survivor of the War of Funerary Flame, her wounds bled into streams that fed gardens, from which water lilies rose and gave birth to the Jinn; at the Jinn's request she stayed in that garden and padisarah flowers bloomed wherever she walked. The wiki presumes the city was founded there. A few generations after Gurabad fell, Ay-Khanoum was ruled by Garshasp.

Status as of 7.1: Only ruins remain. The towers built on the sands may have long collapsed, and the Altar of Mirages in the Hypostyle Desert may mark where the city's remains lie. It is not a place the player can visit as a city.

When Babel first meets Liloupar in The Temple Where Sand Flows Like Tears, he calls her the "eternal prisoner of Ay-Khanoum", a reference to the city she served. Nothing after 3.x changes what is known of it.

36.content:
Bayda Harbor (also: Port Bayda): Bayda Harbor is a Sumeru port on the coast of the Lokapala Jungle in the Dharma Forest, facing Fontaine across the sea. The Sumeru Akademiya runs it, with inspectors who watch the traffic and keep smugglers in check. Its quays are crowded with merchants and stranded foreigners from Liyue, Fontaine and the desert.

Many influential parties cross paths here, and the port's officers say the peace has held because everyone is kept in their own corner. It also serves as the Sumeru end of sea trips from Petrichor.

Geography: The harbor lies on the north coast of Dharma Forest, in the Lokapala Jungle. The Lokapala Jungle runs west of the harbor up a nameless mountain's slope, where it meets the Desert of Hadramaveth. The sea in front of it runs straight to Fontaine.

People: Shajar, the Port Master and an officer of general affairs, is a former Eremite mercenary who took the Akademiya's job offer; she is blunt, wants to be called Shajar or Boss, and disliked being doubted. Adel, a Mahamata of the Akademiya, supervises the Navbed who inspect arrivals and departures; he is an old sailor who once patrolled by boat as far as the Natlan border and likes watching the sea. Boyan, a Liyue merchant, carries goods between Liyue, Fontaine and Sumeru. Zayah is a trader belonging to the Sangemah Bay business group, looking for opportunities in Liyue food. Honorine is a Fontainian engineer stranded when her aquabus project was halted. Anaka is a child whose scholar father has gone to Petrichor.

Governance: The Sumeru Akademiya controls the harbor through its officers: Navbed inspect traffic, a Mahamata (Adel) oversees them, and an officer of general affairs (Shajar) keeps day-to-day order. Entry has strict anti-smuggling rules.

Travel: Ships connect Bayda Harbor with Fontaine, and in the story the Traveler's Waverider and a boat from Petrichor cross to it. By land it lies on the Lokapala Jungle coast of Dharma Forest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Bayda Harbor is an ordinary working port with no major story tied to it. The Archon Quest and later events have not changed it.

Its officers still inspect arrivals and its traders still complain about trade in Fontainian goods.

37.content:
Bayt Al-Hayah (also: The Court of Withered Life): Bayt Al-Hayah is a cavern temple inside Mt. Damavand in Sumeru's Desert of Hadramaveth, beneath Wounded Shin Valley, leading into Deshret's Glass Goblet. It is unlocked in Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part III.

The name is Arabic for House of Life. The map viewpoint calls it the Court of Withered Life. It is on the lower level of the Mt. Damavand ruins.

Geography: Beneath Wounded Shin Valley, on the lower level of the Mt. Damavand map.

History: During Part III, Liloupar describes the tunnels' temple-like stretch as a water supply station and a temple at once, because water was held to be a gift of the Three Gods. She warns that once the sands of time bury this place the Eternal Oasis will inevitably collapse, since even the Master of the Sands could not guarantee its eternity.

Quests: Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part III, the fifth part of The Dirge of Bilqis.

Status as of 7.1: Open to explore as of Version 7.1.

No source up to Version 7.1 that I checked changes this temple.

38.content:
Bayt Al-Muazzam (also: The Temple of Buried Dominion): Bayt Al-Muazzam is a cavern temple inside Mt. Damavand in the Desert of Hadramaveth of Sumeru. It lies beneath Qusayr Al-Inkhida' and leads into Deshret's Glass Goblet. The Traveler unlocks it in Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part I.

The name is Arabic for House of the Glorified. The map viewpoint calls it the Temple of Buried Dominion. It has an upper and a lower level and is the first of three similar caverns found in the Dirge of Bilqis quests, the others being Bayt Al-Sukr and Bayt Al-Hayah.

Geography: In the middle of Mt. Damavand's maze of tunnels, under the ruins of Qusayr Al-Inkhida'. The Mt. Damavand map has two levels for this temple, upper and lower. Paths lead onward to the Goblet.

History: Liloupar, a Jinni who is the Traveler's companion in the quest, explains that the mortal kingdoms of the oasis drew their water from within this mountain, hollowing it and weaving a network of tubes through it. The first water-pumping mechanism the party finds now runs on sand instead of water.

Quests: Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part I, third part of The Dirge of Bilqis, with Jeht, Azariq, Babel and Liloupar.

Status as of 7.1: Open to explore as of Version 7.1.

The Eternal Oasis is reached later in the Dirge of Bilqis. No source up to Version 7.1 that I checked changes this temple.

39.content:
Bayt Al-Sukr (also: The Court of Dried Springs): Bayt Al-Sukr is a cavern temple inside Mt. Damavand in Sumeru's Desert of Hadramaveth, beneath the Sands of Three Canals, leading into Deshret's Glass Goblet. It is unlocked in Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part II.

The name is Arabic for House of Drunkenness. The map viewpoint calls it the Court of Dried Springs. It lies on the upper level of the Mt. Damavand ruins.

Geography: Beneath the Sands of Three Canals, on the upper level of the Mt. Damavand map. It is one of the routes into the central cavern with Deshret's Glass Goblet.

History: During Part II, Liloupar says the oasis honoured the Three Eternal Companion-Gods and that the tunnel was dug in the memory of the slumbering lady of the oasis. She says the Lord charged the mortals' ideal kingdom with guarding his oasis, which is why Gurabad stood on the dune's edge before sinking into the sand.

Quests: Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part II, the fourth part of The Dirge of Bilqis.

Status as of 7.1: Open to explore as of Version 7.1.

No source up to Version 7.1 that I checked changes this temple.

40.content:
Bimarstan: Bimarstan is the hospital of Sumeru City, run by the Akademiya, which gives free healthcare to every resident of Sumeru. It stands just southeast of the city's northwestern Teleport Waypoint. Interns and a doctor staff it, and its name is a variant of the old word for hospitals in the historic Islamic world.

When Eleazar cases rose in Sumeru City, a notice from the mahamatas urged residents with symptoms to go to Bimarstan for treatment. In the Traveler's voice-over, Paimon is amazed that medicine is free.

People: The doctor Zakariya and the intern doctors Golshan and Tamara work at Bimarstan. Patients and their families seen here include Javad (by day), Lila and Tahmina.

Places: A message board nearby, Bimarstan's Proverb Column, displays the sayings of past Akademiya researchers at random, with the stated aim of following the pioneers' trail to the light of wisdom. Behind the building is a medical file that disappears once read.

Governance: Operated by the Akademiya as a public service for all Sumeru residents.

Atmosphere: A calm, clean clinic in the city, with the quiet of waiting families and the cautious optimism of a free-of-charge ward.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains the city's free hospital; the pages consulted record no later change.

key: The Frontier Beneath the High Wall
41.content:
Caravan Ribat (also: The Frontier Beneath the High Wall): Caravan Ribat is a fortified village at the foot of the Wall of Samiel, the great wall that keeps desert sandstorms from the rainforests of Sumeru. It is the checkpoint between the forest and the desert, where travellers going to or from Aaru Village and the Great Red Sand must pass, and it is full of Eremites. Its official tagline calls it the frontier beneath the high wall.

Its name uses the Arabic ribat, a small frontier fortification that later served as a caravanserai defending trade routes. The Ribat sits in the Ashavan Realm of the Dharma Forest, so it feels like a border town that belongs to both worlds.

Geography: Caravan Ribat sits directly under the Wall of Samiel, the barrier between the Dharma Forest and the Great Red Sand. The road through it links the forest side (towards Gandharva Ville and Sumeru City) with the desert side (Aaru Village and the Great Red Sand).

Places: The Caravan Ribat Bulletin Board carries notices such as a recruitment drive for Wall of Samiel maintenance and a reminder that destroying the wall is prohibited. Gilded Journey is a business run by Maryam, with Maziar as an employee.

People: Eremite mercenaries (Aybak, Nasir, Safie, Thiyya) work here alongside merchants (Hawad, Yinjie), an adventurer (Baharak) and researchers (Behnam, Dunya, Juzjani, Ma'asudi, Railah) who monitor the wall. Arshia is also listed.

Governance: No local authority is named. The Akademiya looks after the wall itself; the village is described as the checkpoint between forest and desert.

Culture: Many people here are Eremites, and the village is a place where the desert and the Akademiya's world meet. Dehya says that as she grew up she realised the wall is not only there to keep out sandstorms but also to keep out desert people like her.

History: Collei tells the Traveler that Greater Lord Rukkhadevata created the rainforests and the Wall of Samiel around the desert, to protect the rainforests from sandstorms. Its upkeep has since passed to the Akademiya.

Atmosphere: A frontier stop beneath a towering wall: Eremite mercenaries, merchants, researchers and adventurers gather around a bulletin board, and the village is a way-station between forest and desert.

Dangers: Sandstorms beyond the wall; in Chapter III the Traveler is trailed by Eremites here and needs Alhaitham's help to get away.

Travel: Caravan Ribat is the usual stop for anyone crossing between Gandharva Ville and the forest and Aaru Village and the desert.

Quests: In the Archon Quest the Traveler and Paimon narrowly escape Eremites trailing them at Caravan Ribat, thanks to Alhaitham; he then offers to go with them to Aaru Village. While searching for the missing Village Keepers, Dehya takes the Traveler back to the Ribat to meet her drinking friends.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Caravan Ribat is an operating checkpoint under the Wall of Samiel. Nothing in canon shows it destroyed or abandoned.

It was last shown as a gathering place in the 6.6 Welkin Moon story, with Candace and Dehya saying they have finished escorting people home and are heading back to Aaru Village.

42.comment: Caravan Ribat: The Four at Loggerheads at Caravan Ribat
42.content: In Chapter III Act III the Traveler and Paimon escape Eremites trailing them at Caravan Ribat, thanks to Alhaitham, who says he is still studying the capsule and suspects the Traveler is hiding something. He offers to accompany them to Aaru Village, and they accept. Later, in Act IV, Dehya explains why she resents the wall: she says it serves to keep out desert-dwellers as well as sandstorms, that the sages treat desert people as tools to be used and discarded, and that she would tear the wall down with her own hands if she could.

43.comment: Caravan Ribat: The Wall of Samiel
43.content: The Wall of Samiel separates the Dharma Forest from the Great Red Sand and shields the rainforest from sandstorms. It is said to have been created by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata. The Akademiya maintains it, researchers such as Behnam work on it, and destroying it is forbidden. Caravan Ribat is at its foot.

44.content:
Chatrakam Cave: Chatrakam Cave is a cave system hidden deep in the Lokapala Jungle of Sumeru's Dharma Forest, best known for its huge number of fungi. Humans seldom enter: the damp air suits mushrooms, and apart from the Vanara, for whom mushroom picking is a duty, few people go in. Underground ruins, Eremites, ruin machines and the Realm of Khab are also found there.

The name derives from the Sanskrit chatraka, meaning mushroom. The cave also holds a Battered Notebook tied to the quest Aranakin's Old Friend, and the Realm of Khab opens within it.

Geography: The cave has two mapped levels, a Northern Underground Ruins and a Southern Cavern, with a Dendro Elemental Monument, Clusterleaf of Cultivation, Four-Leaf Sigil, bouncy mushrooms, poisonous mushrooms, Gloomy Path puzzles and Auspicious Branch plants. Outside lies Lokapala Jungle forest where hilichurl berserkers, Dendro samachurls and Eremite Sunfrost are found.

Places: The Realm of Khab, reached from the Northern Underground Ruins, is described as the place where the memories of Nara Varuna and the Aranara converge and where the dreams of the Barsam Flower gather. Khab is a Persian word for sleep.

Dangers: Many fungi: floating Hydro and Dendro fungi, stretchy Geo fungi, grounded Hydroshrooms and winged Dendroshrooms. Eremites (Ravenbeak halberdiers, axe vanguards, linebreakers, crossbowmen and sword-dancers) are also inside. Ruin Destroyers, Cruisers, Defenders and Graders form the elite foes.

People: The Vanara, who treat mushroom picking as a duty, are the only people said to go into the cave in any number. According to the Amurta scholars quoted in the expedition text, the fungi come in a great many varieties.

Quests: Aranakin's Old Friend (3.0) begins at the hill northwest of the cave and ends with a notebook in a tree house; Aranakin has forgotten many of the friends he made. The limited event Fabulous Fungus Frenzy (3.2) placed a Fatui Pyro Agent north of the cave carrying a letter from Second Lieutenant Yurochka that plotted against a rogue Fatui named Elchingen.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Chatrakam Cave is still a fungus-ridden cave that few people enter.

The Fabulous Fungus Frenzy event is over, but the cave and the Realm of Khab remain accessible.

45.content: A dream-like realm said to be the convergence of Nara Varuna's and the Aranara's memories and the gathering place of the Barsam Flower's dreams. It is reached through Chatrakam Cave in the Risen Moon Chapter.

46.content:
Chemin Oublie: Chemin Oublie is a tunnel that connects the Girdle of the Sands in Sumeru to Romaritime Harbor in Fontaine. Its French name means "Forgotten Path". It is a point of interest, not a region.

It was added with Fontaine in version 4.0.

Geography: A cave-like tunnel running from Sumeru's Realm of Farakhkert to the harbor in Fontaine, a large coastal elevator and observation deck beside a waterfall that also provides the passage into Sumeru. Along it are seelie to follow, a Time Trial Challenge, Trishiraite and Mourning Flower to gather, and many sea shells scattered about.

History: Canon does not say who made the tunnel. The wiki infers from the name and the many shells that Oceanids may have used it as a pilgrimage route.

Dangers: Hydro slimes and Hydro hilichurl rogues.

Travel: The tunnel is the walking link between Sumeru and Fontaine at Romaritime Harbor.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tunnel is an open connection between Sumeru and Fontaine.

Nothing after its 4.0 introduction has changed it.

47.comment: Chemin Oublie: Chemin Oublie Name and Shells
47.content: Chemin Oublie ("Forgotten Path") connects the Girdle of the Sands to Fontaine's Romaritime Harbor. The wiki points to the name and the scattered sea shells as a possible sign of an Oceanid pilgrimage route, an inference not confirmed in game text.

48.content:
Chinvat Ravine: Chinvat Ravine is a ravine below Sumeru City, at the base of the Divine Tree, in the Avidya Forest area of Sumeru's Dharma Forest. Forest travellers use the name for the passage beneath the great tree, as an echo of the ancient literary image of crossing a sea of ignorance to reach the light of truth.

The name is a Sumeru-flavoured borrowing of the Chinvat Bridge, the bridge of judgement in Zoroastrian belief.

Geography: The ravine lies below Sumeru City at the foot of the Divine Tree. The expedition text treats it as the last stage of a forest journey before the city of wisdom. It is part of the Avidya Forest.

History: The expedition description explains the name: in Sumeru's ancient literary canon, Chinvat stands for the bitter sea of ignorance that seekers must cross to see the light on the far shore. Those who now navigate the forests apply it to this ravine, perhaps for the elation of finally arriving at the city of wisdom.

Dangers: Eremites (crossbow users, linebreakers and sword-dancers) and shaggy sumpter beasts roam the area. A random encounter called Unscrupulous Dealings can place the Traveler across from Fatui skirmishers, including Anemoboxer and Pyroslinger types, who are in what Paimon calls a dodgy under-the-table deal with Eremites; the Traveler is expected to break it up.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Chinvat Ravine is an ordinary part of Sumeru's open world with no later story change.

The Fatui and Eremites that appear there are random encounters rather than any lasting presence.

49.content: Name lore for the ravine below the Divine Tree: Chinvat is the bitter sea of ignorance in Sumeru's old literature, and travellers use it for the passage into the city of wisdom.

50.content:
Citadel of Regzar: The Citadel of Regzar is the headquarters of the Corps of Thirty, the mercenary brigade that keeps the peace in Sumeru City for the Akademiya. It stands in the middle of the city, near Treasures Street. The name is a Persian word for desert.

The Corps began as thirty Eremite mercenaries hired by the sages; the barracks here fly the Eremite crest and colours on their banners, while members wear teal-green scarves with a petal-like emblem.

People: Rukh Shah, the Parchamdar, commands the Corps and is the youngest ever to hold the post. Asfand is the Consultant (the administrative leader). Others here are the researcher Effendi and the members Sekkura (called "Swallow"), Udad ("Goat") and Yunus ("Bigfish").

Governance: Not a formal army but a permanently hired mercenary brigade working for the Akademiya; the Parchamdar is military commander and the Consultant handles administration.

Atmosphere: Disciplined but not grim, a barracks of hired soldiers in the middle of a scholarly city.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains the Corps' base.

51.content:
Dar al-Shifa (also: Eleazar Hospital, Abandoned hospital near Aaru Village): Dar al-Shifa is an abandoned hospital in the Land of Lower Setekh, not far from Aaru Village. It once specialised in treating patients with Eleazar, the disease that covers the body in scabs and ulcers. Old notes found inside suggest that a doctor there was using patients as test subjects for dangerous treatments. In the Archon Quest the Traveler, Paimon and Alhaitham investigate it after villagers report crying at night.

The name means "house of healing" in Arabic, and the in-game viewpoint says it is named for a prayer for patients. It is now silent, missing both the doctors' bustle and the songs of recovered patients.

Geography: A weathered desert building, half full of sand, with a barrier hiding an older underground wing. A trapdoor leads down to a lower level that looks like a second hospital tucked inside the first. Tunnels beneath hold the remains of dead hilichurls. Eremites roam the surroundings.

History: The hospital treated Eleazar patients, and rooms, labels and patient items such as bowls bearing patients' names remain. A medical file records a farmer called Abbas under a doctor named Amoudi, then continued by a doctor whose name is blacked out. The treatment documents describe replacement of a patient's skin and limb, and a physician's note links high elemental quantities in the body to the disease. The doctor writes of control without elemental power, a possible military use, and sees the patients as specimens.

Status as of 7.1: Abandoned for years. In Cry From the Eleazar Hospital the party learns that the crying heard from the village at night came from here, and finds Razak, an Akademiya scholar and a senior of Alhaitham, in a mindless state.

The people who had been held here were already taken away when the party arrived, leaving drag marks from a cart. The hospital is later used as evidence in Alhaitham's reasoning about the Akademiya.

52.comment: Dar al-Shifa: Razak and the night crying
52.content: In the quest Cry From the Eleazar Hospital, the village girl Shani tells the party she hears faint crying at night coming from far away, and that the guards have heard similar sounds. Alhaitham leads the party to the hospital, where they find Razak, an Akademiya scholar whom Alhaitham says never trained in the forest or reached the Satyavada Life stage, and who now cannot speak and has unfocused eyes. Alhaitham links his state to that of the Eremite Mizri at Port Ormos.

53.content:
Debris of Panjvahe (also: Panjvahe, The Forgotten River Valley, Remnants of Five Oases): The Debris of Panjvahe is a dry river valley and the ruins around it in the Desert of Hadramaveth, Sumeru. Panjvahe was once an irrigated district under Gurabad, where nobles sailed ornate boats on the river and flew hunting falcons. Its water system failed, the district fell into poverty and unrest, and today the valley is quiet and mostly empty, with wild vultures where falcons once flew.

Panjvahe's fate is told in notes and inscriptions: neglected maintenance of the irrigation network fed by the water system at Mt. Damavand, shrinking oases, and a Gurabad council that refused to pay for repairs. The name is read as "five oases" in the Chinese and Japanese versions.

Geography: A broad river valley cut into the desert, with ruins along its sides and a hidden quiet pool in the valley. It lies in the same desert as Gurabad and Mt. Damavand. The nearby Fane of Panjvahe, a domain listed under The Sands of Three Canals, is a separate place: a hermitage that Gurabad's ancestors built for the Lord of the Desert and that now shelters desert dwellers and bandits.

History: In the viewpoint's telling, the great river valley once irrigated Panjvahe, and nobles of Gurabad sailed on it in ornate boats. Records at Mt. Damavand describe the system behind it: Jinn fragments set into machinery regulated the water supply, which was more efficient than older methods. Over time the canal system was clogged by sand. The priests wanted large-scale maintenance but the Jinni Ferigees, who guarded the nearby Orchard of Pairidaeza, refused it because it might disturb the Goddess of Flowers's tomb, and offered some of her own power instead.

Status as of 7.1: Today it is an empty, quiet valley of the Great Red Sand, with the remains of the old district along the dry riverbed.

As of Version 7.1 nothing found changes Panjvahe's status as an abandoned ruin.

54.content:
Desert of Hadramaveth: The Desert of Hadramaveth is the southwestern part of Sumeru's Great Red Sand, opened up in version 3.4. Its dunes and scimitar-shaped ravines hide the ruins of the ancient city of Gurabad, and the nomadic Tanit tribe once lived in its camps. Official text says a lost city lies hidden there, with a wandering tribe seeking refuge in its ruins, and that incessant sandstorms erode all things.

The name blends Hadramaut, a South Arabian region, with the biblical Hazarmaveth ("court of death"). It has eleven subareas, more than any other area in the game. Its main story is the Dirge of Bilqis world-quest series, in which the Traveler accompanies Jeht to the Eternal Oasis.

Geography: A broad desert plain crossed by canyons and wadis, with long sandstorms that the wiki lists as a regular feature. Ruins, obelisks, sandglasses, Jinn shrines and atmospheric vortices dot it, and wenut roam its dunes. The boss enemy is the Setekh Wenut, and the local specialties are Henna Berry and Sand Grease Pupa.

Places: Gurabad, the ruined City of Brass and City of Kings. The Tanit Camps, the tribe's last settlement. Mt. Damavand, the smoking mountain with a tornado at its heart. Safhe Shatranj, the former Temples Forsaken, with a giant chessboard. Deshret's Glass Goblet, the sunken heart where the way to the Eternal Oasis lies.

People: The Tanit are a matrilineal Eremite tribe who revere the Goddess of Flowers and are led by a Matriarch and nine Elders. They value words and knowledge but distrust the Akasha, trade crocodile products, spices and essential oils, and hunt wenut for spice. After the Dirge of Bilqis the Tanit are removed and the Vahumana researcher Tanjiyy takes their camps.

History: Gurabad rose after Nabu Malikata's death and fell before the forbidden-knowledge incident that ended King Deshret's civilisation. According to the wiki, Ormazd ruled until Liloupar engineered his murder; his adopted son Kisra, who took the name Parvezravan and was in fact Liloupar's son, built Jinn-powered machines and was killed by his own son Shiruyeh. Liloupar's use of Abyssal power then sent much of the city into a chasm and a plague killed most of its people, after which Gurabad was abandoned and attempts to revive it failed.

Dangers: Sandstorms; wenut and the Setekh Wenut; Primal Constructs (Repulsors, Reshapers, Prospectors) and Eremites; hilichurls; Fatui camps (reports by a Fatui captain, Zoya Snezhevna, are among the interactables); quicksand; and the desert itself.

Travel: The Temir Mountains link the desert to the rest of the Girdle of the Sands; from the Tanit Camps the Dirge quests use Deshret's old canal tunnels to reach Mt. Damavand and the Glass Goblet. Before taking the quest the game recommends finishing Golden Slumber and accepting The Dirge of Bilqis.

Quests: The Dirge of Bilqis (3.4): Wisdom Has Built Her House, She Has Hewn Out Her Seven Pillars; The Temple Where Sand Flows Like Tears; Dune-Entombed Fecundity Parts I to III; and The Eternal Dream, Ever Lush. Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters... follows it (Behold, the Sign Comes Like A Thief...; Make Bright the Arrows, Gather the Shields...; For Her Judgment Reaches to the Skies...). Memories of Gurabad, The Fallen Falcon, Tadhla the Falcon and the Culling of the Worms series also take place here.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the desert is an open, ruined wilderness without a Tanit tribe.

The Tanit's camps hold only the Vahumana researcher Tanjiyy; nothing from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes the area.

55.content: A nomadic matrilineal Eremite tribe of the Desert of Hadramaveth, led by the Matriarch Babel. In The Dirge of Bilqis the Traveler and Jeht seek the Eternal Oasis; afterwards Babel, who had conspired with the Fatui against the other elders, tries to take the oasis for herself, and the Traveler and Jeht destroy the tribe.

56.content: An ancient desert city in the southwest of the Desert of Hadramaveth that fell before King Deshret's forbidden-knowledge incident. Liloupar, a Jinni, plotted its fall over three generations because Ormazd had not freed its slaves; a revolt, a chasm and a plague ended it.

57.content:
Deshret's Glass Goblet (also: Crystal Goblet of Al-Ahmar, Glass Goblet of King Deshret): Deshret's Glass Goblet is a huge goblet-shaped structure in the depths of Mt. Damavand, in the Desert of Hadramaveth. The platform at its center is the way into the Orchard of Pairidaeza, the Eternal Oasis. It is first seen in the Dirge of Bilqis world quests, and access opens during Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part III.

Desert tales say King Deshret left the cup behind when he bade farewell to joy. The Jinni Liloupar says the visible structure is not the true goblet but a mechanism that holds the oasis in stasis. It was guarded by Ferigees, a Jinni whose spirit lived in a machine on the goblet.

Geography: The Goblet sits inside the cavernous interior of Mt. Damavand, reached by passing ancient pipes and mechanisms, with a platform at its center that leads to the Eternal Oasis. Seen from above it looks like a wide crystal cup. Jeht, a member of the Tanit tribe, described pipes running into the temple inside the mountain.

History: In the account Liloupar gives in the quest, Deshret left the cup as a receptacle for past traumas and memories. Jinn-built machinery under the mountain, powered by gems under the sands according to artifact lore, keeps the oasis in a frozen moment. When the Traveler's party reached the center, Ferigees blocked them; her fall also ended the old arrangement.

Status as of 7.1: Ferigees was destroyed in Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part III, and the Goblet is open to travellers as the way down to the oasis. The quest series continues in The Eternal Dream, Ever Lush.

The Goblet's shape is echoed by a chesspiece in Safhe Shatranj, another subarea of the Desert of Hadramaveth, though canon does not explain the link.

58.comment: Deshret's Glass Goblet: Ferigees at the Goblet
58.content: Ferigees guarded the platform in a machine, bound by what she called shackles, and refused Liloupar entry, calling her a traitor. When the Traveler defeated her mechanical defenders she said the tomb was empty and would crumble, and her spirit faded with the shell.

59.content:
Devantaka Mountain (also: Devantaka): Devantaka Mountain is a mountain in Sumeru's Ardravi Valley, in the Dharma Forest, home to a massive Ruin Golem built in Khaenri'ah's time. The scholar Pir Kavikavus of the Akademiya's Kshahrewar once studied the machine and suffered a terrible accident, and the Akasha System gets no signal on the mountain. The official description calls it the mountain that saw the fall of the demons.

The name probably references Devantaka, a Hindu asura whose name means destroyer of gods. The Ruin Golem was the setting of the Vimana Agama world quests, in which a Kshahrewar researcher called Jazari studies it.

Geography: Valleys and greenery hide a giant machine whose circular holes seem to watch time pass. The Ruin Golem has three levels of rooms and corridors, with energy blocks, large gears and lifts; caves run beneath and behind it, and below it lies Dev's Cavern. Ruin Drakes, Ruin Graders and an Aeonblight Drake are the main hostile machines and beasts.

Places: The Ruin Golem: one of three known in Sumeru, the others being at the Valley of Dahri and the Desert of Hadramaveth. Dev's Cavern: a cavern beneath the mountain where the Golem's core was removed and sealed, now also where the Abyss Order seeks power. The Ruin Golem's top floor and side chambers hold notes from the Akademiya investigation team's Zandik.

History: The Ruin Golem was a Khaenri'ahn war machine whose core was removed and sealed in Dev's Cavern. Hundreds of years on, the Akademiya's Kshahrewar studied it. Pir Kavikavus joined Kshahrewar after the cataclysm of 500 years ago, rose to Herbad before thirty, and became the last person known to enter the Golem for systematic research before an accident erased his work. Kshahrewar's prestige fell, and the Akademiya has not raised its funding since.

Dangers: The Golem's Chaos Core leaked energy and polluted the nearby forest until it was sealed. Monsters gathered at the machine; Abyss Order mages sought the core's power; Eremites, hilichurls, Rishboland tigers and fungi are also present.

Quests: Vimana Agama: Ararycan, an Aranara, investigates a contamination around Devantaka Mountain with the Traveler and meets the Kshahrewar researcher Jazari. Jazari cannot see Ararycan, who explains that humans lose the ability as they grow older. Jazari's chapter has the Traveler reactivate the Ruin Golem enough for its arm to smash the ground and reopen Dev's Cavern; the Golem then breaks down again. In Until Vana is Healed, the Traveler finds Kavikavus's hidden research paper, brings it to Jazari and helps seal the Golem's Chaos Core, weakening the Abyss Order's threat to the forest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Golem still stands idle, its core sealed, and Jazari researches it.

Nothing after 3.2 has changed the mountain, and no later Sumeru or Snezhnaya material in 6.x-7.1 references it.

60.content: Historical Kshahrewar prodigy who became a Herbad before thirty and was the last known person to research the Ruin Golem on Devantaka Mountain. An accident lost his research and he probably died. He was friends with the Aranara Aralohita, who hid some of his work behind puzzles.

61.comment: Devantaka Mountain: Dev's Cavern and the Chaos Core
61.content: Dev's Cavern lies beneath the mountain, where the Ruin Golem's core was sealed. The core leaked and polluted the forest; entrances were blocked, and the Golem's arm blow in Vimana Agama reopened them. The Traveler sealed the core with Kavikavus's method, which weakened the Abyss mages who tried to stop it.

62.content:
Dev's Cavern: Dev's Cavern is a cave in Ardravi Valley, in the Dharma Forest of Sumeru. It is a minor point of interest whose name uses the old Sumeru word for Abyssal monsters.

It is unlocked during the world quest Vimana Agama: Dev Delver Chapter. Its inhabitants are hilichurls and samachurls, with elite Abyss Mages of the Cryo, Electro, Hydro and Pyro varieties.

Geography: A cavern within Ardravi Valley in the Dharma Forest.

History: A Sumeru loading-screen tip says the dark beasts from beneath the earth were once called Dev by the people of Sumeru, and the term also appears in the Oracle Parchment, for the End of Death text. This explains the name in general but not the cave itself.

Dangers: Hilichurls, Electro and Geo samachurls, and elite Abyss Mages (Cryo, Electro, Hydro, Pyro).

Quests: Vimana Agama: Dev Delver Chapter unlocks the location.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no change to the cavern was found.

63.content:
Dharma Forest (also: Sumeru rainforest, Sumeru's rainforest): Dharma Forest is the rainforest half of Sumeru: a green, humid, many-layered country of giant trees, mushrooms, rivers and rain, in the east and centre of the nation. Sumeru City, the "City of Wisdom", is built on a vast tree here and houses the Sumeru Akademiya. Forest Rangers patrol the woods, merchants and students crowd Port Ormos, and the small plant-like Aranara live out of sight in the dreams of children. Its great danger is the Withering, a rot that spreads through the land. The desert lies beyond the Wall of Samiel to the west.

Travellers from Liyue can reach it directly from the Chasm, and Avidya Forest is the first area the Traveler enters in Sumeru. The forest is Dendro country: the nation's Archon, Lesser Lord Kusanali (Nahida), is the God of Wisdom, and the plants, fungi and "dream" magic here all reflect that.

Geography: Seven areas make up the subregion: Avidya Forest (the heart, with Sumeru City and Gandharva Ville), Ardravi Valley (the great river and its trade route), Ashavan Realm (the southern wetlands and hills), Lokapala Jungle (the north coast), Vissudha Field, Vanarana and the small Lost Nursery. The Wall of Samiel separates the forest from the Great Red Sand on the west. The river Ardravi cut the valley that carries Sumeru's main waterborne trade down to the southern shore.

Places: Sumeru City sits on the Divine Tree, with the Akademiya in the middle and upper part of the tree and the Sanctuary of Surasthana, where Nahida lives, on top. Gandharva Ville, "the City Above the Forest", is the Forest Rangers' main outpost. Port Ormos is the largest port in Sumeru, a trade hub under two giant trees; Vimara Village is a quiet fishing town on the river between the two. Caravan Ribat is a fortified village at the foot of the Wall of Samiel, the checkpoint for everyone going to or from the desert and Aaru Village. Apam Woods is a rainforest where the rain never fully ceases; Pardis Dhyai is a garden research site of Amurta scholars.

People: Forest Rangers (the civil-service guardians of the forest; the senior ones are Forest Watchers, among them Tighnari) patrol the woods and report to Pardis Dhyai's researchers. Students and scholars of the Akademiya fill Sumeru City and visit Port Ormos when academic life gets too stressful. Eremite mercenaries from the desert work in Port Ormos and Caravan Ribat. Traders, dockworkers and fishers fill the river towns. Children are the ones who see the Aranara.

History: By the wiki's reconstruction, the forest was once the domain of the Dendro Dragon Apep's court and the cradle of the first fern that grew into the Irminsul. After the Archon War era, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata left her friend King Deshret's desert kingdom, came to the east of the Great Red Sand and used the Varuna Contraption to turn desert into rainforest. She raised the Wall of Samiel against sandstorms, and the forest king Viaghara was born. Her followers became the founders of the Amurta darshan of the Akademiya; Sumeru City was built on the Divine Tree. She also created the Aranara.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Dharma Forest is recovering from the 6.6 Irminsul crisis: the whole rainforest was briefly evacuated, Irminsul was burned away and replaced by the reconfigured Aaru, and Dottore is dead. People have returned and are rebuilding under Nahida's guidance. Old Withering Zones have not gone away.

Collei is now an official Forest Ranger, and the Akademiya works under Naphis and a new council of sages. The 7.0 and 7.1 Archon Quest has moved to Snezhnaya, and no new rainforest areas have been added since.

64.comment: Dharma Forest: Avidya Forest and Sumeru City
64.content: Avidya Forest is the most populous part of Sumeru apart from Ardravi Valley and the first area the Traveler enters. Sumeru City, the "City of Wisdom", is built on a gigantic tree, the Divine Tree, with its Grand Bazaar, Zubayr Theater and Treasures Street below the Akademiya, which occupies the middle and upper part of the tree. On top is the Sanctuary of Surasthana, a treetop palace and the Archon's home. Gandharva Ville, the Rangers' outpost, lies in the forest nearby.

65.content: The Withering is a blight that causes Withering Zones where land and life decay. Within one the party gains Decay, reducing resistances and Max HP, and can fall if it reaches the limit. Dendrograna (Dendro-charged seeds) destroy its Withering Branches, and defeating the enemies from the Tumor of the Withering clears the zone. After clearing one in Chapter III, Tighnari voices concern at how quickly new zones are appearing and how they worsen Eleazar.

66.content: The Aranara are small, plant-like forest spirits created by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata (whom they called Queen Aranyani) to guard the forest. They hide from adult eyes but befriend children; they love memories, fear fire and salt, and when in grave danger turn to seed.
