Their homeland, Vanarana, exists both in reality and as a dream place, Mahavanaranapna. At life's end an Aranara grows into a Vasara Tree.

67.comment: Dharma Forest: Forest Rangers and Gandharva Ville
67.content: The Forest Rangers (also called Vanara) are civil servants who protect the forests of Sumeru: they help travellers, suppress Withering Zones and monitor beast populations. Higher-ranking members are Forest Watchers and wear lighter green. Their main outpost, Gandharva Ville, is "the City Above the Forest". They send regular reports to the researchers of Pardis Dhyai, who supply seeds and nutrients in return.

68.comment: Dharma Forest: Port Ormos and the Ardravi
68.content: Port Ormos is Sumeru's largest port and a hub for trade and travel, beneath two giant trees with a river running to Sumeru City. Parts of it are under Akademiya supervision, yet smuggling and illegal trade are more common here than in the city and prices are lower. Most long-term residents are traders and labourers who grew up there; Eremite mercenaries from several groups work here too, and students come to relax. Kaveh designed its arch bridge.

69.comment: Dharma Forest: Wall of Samiel and Caravan Ribat
69.content: The Wall of Samiel separates the rainforest from the Great Red Sand, supposedly built by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata to keep sandstorms from ruining the forest. The Akademiya maintains it and forbids damaging it. Caravan Ribat, full of Eremites, is a fortified village at its foot and the checkpoint for travel to the desert and Aaru Village.

70.content:
Djafar Tavern (also: Djafar Restaurant): Djafar Tavern is the main place to eat and drink in Port Ormos, Sumeru's big harbour. Its owner Eymen tends the bar, promising the best wine, food and service and treating every customer like family. Merchants, tourists, sailors and former Eremite mercenaries mix here. In the Archon Quest it is where Ayn Al-Ahmar members, devotees of King Deshret, sold false information to would-be buyers.

The staff are Eymen (bartender and owner) and two hostesses, Nesmil and Roshana, who both used to be Eremites.

People: Eymen: bartender and owner. He was a travelling merchant in the desert until he made enough money to open the place. Roshana says he does not want to offend customers and will try to meet any demand. Nesmil: cheerful hostess who talks up the tavern's wine and appetizers; a former Eremite mercenary who says she left them for the tavern because of Roshana, and that she enjoys more freedom here than she would freelancing for the Akademiya. Roshana: dry, unfussy hostess who does not make cocktails or wait on customers ("talk to the bartender"), another ex-Eremite who prefers this to dealing with stiff researchers. Other people seen here include the merchants Abbanes and Behrouz and the researcher Parisa; at night the Mahamata Mahshid and the Eremite mercenary Matari are also present.

Quests: In Lost in Prosperity (Chapter III Act I), Akademiya students in Port Ormos say that the Eremite group Ayn Al-Ahmar likes to set up shop at Djafar Tavern and will sell information on anything for half a million Mora. The Traveler and Paimon go there and Eymen shows them to a table. Ayn Al-Ahmar men (Tariq and Tumart) talk openly about reclaiming King Deshret's power. Tariq takes 500,000 Mora and hands over an address, then explains the group's faith in King Deshret and their grievance against Greater Lord Rukkhadevata. Alhaitham interrupts and calls Tariq a fraud: the address is fake, and the group lures people with promises of information so they can squeeze them for money.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Djafar Tavern is open and unchanged.

71.content: Eymen (owner, bartender), Nesmil (hostess) and Roshana (hostess) run the tavern. Nesmil and Roshana are former Eremite mercenaries; Eymen was a travelling desert merchant whom Eremites once looked after. Nesmil is fond of Roshana; Roshana is blunt and does not wait on tables.

72.content:
Duat Hall (also: The Bottomless Hall): Duat Hall is a vast underground hall in the Mausoleum of King Deshret, in Sumeru's Hypostyle Desert, whose floor falls away into a bottomless void. Its name is the ancient Egyptian realm of the dead, and the Scarlet Sand Slate describes it as the place where the guilty meet their fate.

It is the first stop of the trials in Dual Evidence and joins the Great Hall of Truths on its south side. A side chamber off its east side, the Place of Swallowing, holds one of the slate's clearance trials.

Geography: Reached through an underground teleport waypoint directly south of the Mausoleum. A door to it opens only with the Ferryman's Clearance, a permission the slate grants when Dual Evidence begins. The hall is connected to the Great Hall of Truths at its south end and to the Place of Swallowing off its east side.

History: After Soheil's dismissal in Aaru Village, the slate lights up and points to Duat Hall. On entering, the party finds new writing and three points of light. The text describes the mortal plane as a river between the underworld and Aaru that must not be crossed or coveted, and tells the reader to take a vulture's form, peck at three organs, win Al-Ahmar's consent and cross as a falcon. Paimon connects the three organs to the devices Tirzad found earlier.

Dangers: Falling into the void is the main hazard. In play, falling only returns the traveller to the entrance without penalty; the slate's lines about judging the guilty are symbolic.

Quests: Dual Evidence (Old Notes and New Friends, part 1). The Traveler enters here after Soheil's dismissal in Aaru Village.

Status as of 7.1: Open to explore as of Version 7.1.

No source up to Version 7.1 that I checked changes the hall.

73.content:
Dunes of Steel: The Dunes of Steel are a subarea of the Desert of Hadramaveth in Sumeru's Great Red Sand. Canon describes them only as the stretch of the desert that connects it to Old Vanarana, the former home of the Aranara.

They were added with the Desert of Hadramaveth in version 3.4. Nothing else about their history, inhabitants or purpose is stated.

Geography: Sand dunes at the edge of the Desert of Hadramaveth, on the side that leads toward Old Vanarana in the Dharma Forest's Lost Nursery. The wiki lists no points of interest, enemies or specialties for the subarea itself.

History: Canon gives the dunes no history of their own. Their only stated role is as the link to Old Vanarana, which the Aranara called home for hundreds of years before the cataclysm and which stayed engulfed in the Withering until the Nursery of Lost Dreams quest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the dunes are an open part of the Desert of Hadramaveth.

Nothing after their 3.4 introduction has changed them.

74.comment: Dunes of Steel: Dunes of Steel
74.content: The Dunes of Steel are the part of the Desert of Hadramaveth that connects the desert to Old Vanarana. Canon says nothing more about them; the wiki page is a stub.

75.content:
Fane of Ashvattha: The Fane of Ashvattha is a sacred grove in Vissudha Field, Dharma Forest, that holds the Ashvattha Tree, the first Vasara Tree and the progenitor of the Aranara. It also acts as the seal over the entrance to Old Vanarana, the older, sealed Vanarana. In the Aranyaka quest series the Traveler and Arama come here to make the Bija that will heal Rana.

The tree was weakened by Marana and could not bear the Bija. Arama took its place and planted a new Ashvattha Tree, and the seal at the Fane opened so the party could descend toward Old Vanarana.

Geography: A hidden forest shrine in Vissudha Field, with the Ashvattha Tree at its center and a seal over the passage into Old Vanarana. The body of water over the entrance has to be drained in the quest before the way leads further in. The wiki notes that the area's name is not shown on the map until the quest For Fruits, Seeds, and Trees is done.

People: The Aranara hold it sacred. Arama, a friendly Aranara who guides the Traveler, says it is her first visit. The Ashvattha Tree is the oldest of the Vasara Trees, older than any Aranara and their stories, and all Aranara descend from it.

History: Arama's account is that the first Aranara, Aramuhukunda, sprouted from a seed in a pomegranate the Ashvattha Tree produced after a great singer of the forest called the tree out of Sarva. The tree did this so that the forest's children would grow and befriend the lonely Nara, humans. Later the Aranara spread like leaves on a tree. Aramuhukunda later became a Vasara Tree in Old Vanarana to hold back Marana's avatar, and the tree there withered.

Status as of 7.1: The old Ashvattha Tree in the Fane is spent, though the place remains sacred to the Aranara, and the seal over Old Vanarana was opened in the quest.

The new Ashvattha Tree is Arama in Old Vanarana, so the Fane's tree is a memory of the first. No later change is recorded as of Version 7.1.

76.content: Vasara Trees hold dreams and memories and are usually made when an Aranara chooses to become one. They keep some consciousness, so other Aranara treat a tree as the Aranara it once was. The three Vasara Trees of Araji, Aramaha and Arayama, tended by the concourses, each bear a Vasoma Fruit once the Withering is cleared from their dreams. The Bija is obtained by offering such fruits to the Ashvattha Tree.

77.content:
Gandha Hill: Gandha Hill is a hill in the Avidya Forest of Sumeru's Dharma Forest, the lush rainforest of the north. It has no named settlement or landmark of its own and no stated history; it is simply a stretch of rainforest slope that travellers cross.

It was added with Sumeru in version 3.0. Treat it as a quiet corner of the forest rather than a destination.

Geography: Part of Avidya Forest, the green, populous eastern rainforest that also holds Sumeru City and the Forest Watchers' base at Gandharva Ville. The wiki lists no terrain features, points of interest or local specialties for the hill itself.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing is recorded as changing here.

78.content:
Gandharva Ville (also: The City Above the Forest): Gandharva Ville, nicknamed the City Above the Forest, is the main outpost of Sumeru's Forest Rangers, set in the Avidya Forest. Travellers, merchants and adventurers frequent it. It is home to the Forest Watcher Tighnari and his student Collei, and it is where the Traveler recovers after a vision in Chapter III.

Its tone is quiet and caring. The Rangers here help travellers in need, keep watch over the forest's health and treat patients, and the village is where the early threads of Sumeru's Archon Quest begin.

Geography: The village stands above the forest floor in the Avidya Forest; official map text calls it "the city above the forest". Its local specialty is the Kalpalata Lotus, and Shaggy Sumpter Beasts wander near it.

Places: Ashpazi, a Forest Watcher who supervises logistics and is a master chef, serves as the village's vendor; Collei is cared for in the village when her illness flares.

People: Forest Watchers (higher-ranking Rangers) and Rangers include Tighnari (chief officer), Amir (who trains the search and rescue dogs), Shirin (doctor), Iraj, Kamran and Nasrin; Collei, long a trainee, was promoted to official Forest Ranger after the 6.6 crisis. Keon, Farbod and Umm are designated Vanara; Keon is a blind elder who greets travellers by their footsteps. Visitors and workers include researchers Hayyan and Rudaba, adventurer Philby, the merchant Darina and Eremite mercenaries Futuh, Tuman and Yohanan.

Governance: The Forest Rangers run the village. They are civil servants who protect Sumeru's forests, help travellers and preserve the ecosystem, suppress Withering Zones and monitor beast populations.

Culture: The Rangers are devoted to protecting the forest. Locals such as Keon once blessed travellers in the name of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata; since her erasure from Irminsul in Chapter III they credit every blessing to Lesser Lord Kusanali instead. They are wary of the Akademiya's recruiters, as when Tighnari refuses a top-secret project.

History: Little is known of the village's origin. In the story Collei is brought here by Cyno after the Black Fire incident in Mondstadt and becomes Tighnari's trainee. Tighnari's ancestors learned of the Withering and of Irminsul from aranara.

Atmosphere: A quiet, high-up outpost where Rangers in green clothes (higher ranks wear lighter green), search dogs and visiting travellers come and go; Keon counts the Dusk Birds that pass.

Dangers: Withering Zones in the surrounding forest, whose effects only those with elemental power can withstand; Eremites hired by Dottore in Chapter III; hostile wildlife such as Shaggy Sumpter Beasts.

Travel: Gandharva Ville is the Rangers' base in the Avidya Forest; the Traveler also reaches Pardis Dhyai from it, and the road through Dharma Forest leads on to Caravan Ribat and the desert.

Quests: In Chapter III Act I the Traveler wakes here after Haypasia's incense gave them a vision; Collei shows them around on patrol, and Tighnari explains the Withering and Irminsul. Khajeh and his Akademiya retinue visit to recruit Tighnari and are refused. In Act III Collei, barred from expeditions by a worsening Eleazar, is found here, and Tighnari has left for Pardis Dhyai.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Gandharva Ville remains the Forest Rangers' main outpost, with Tighnari and Collei (now an official Forest Ranger) based there.

Eleazar was wiped out after the Chapter III Archon Quest, curing Collei. In 6.6, during the Irminsul crisis, the whole rainforest including the village was evacuated to Caravan Ribat and then Aaru Village, with Tighnari, Collei and the Rangers helping defend the evacuees; after the crisis people returned and Collei was promoted to official Forest Ranger.

79.comment: Gandharva Ville: A Forest of Change and Further Observation
79.content: After passing through the tunnel from Cinnabar Cliff, the Traveler and Paimon follow the scholar Haypasia into a cave, where her incense gives the Traveler a vision of a white tree under a red sky and a woman's voice saying "World... Forget me...". They wake in Gandharva Ville, where Tighnari and Collei treated them. Tighnari calls it a hallucination; suspecting a lie, the Traveler asks Collei and joins her patrol the next day.

80.content: Collei was born with Eleazar, a disease endemic to Sumeru that causes slow, painful death. Dottore had once suppressed her symptoms through experiments that traumatised her and made her avoid touch. In Chronic Illness the Traveler and Tighnari gather medicine ingredients and clear a Withering Zone on a patrol route. After Nahida removes the Greater Lord's presence from Irminsul in the Archon Quest, Eleazar disappears and Collei recovers.

81.content: In Silent Seeker of Knowledge the Traveler and Paimon return to find Sage Khajeh and subordinates trying to recruit Tighnari into a top-secret Akademiya project. Even mention of disappointing his teacher, Sage Naphis, does not move him, and they leave empty-handed. Tighnari then tells the Traveler to meet Rohawi in Sumeru City.

key: The Gaze From a Certain God
82.comment: Gandharva Ville: Chapter III Act III at Gandharva Ville
82.content: On the way to the village the Traveler and Paimon repel an ambush by Eremites hired by Dottore. They find Collei, whose Eleazar has worsened and who is barred from expeditions. Tighnari has uncharacteristically left for Pardis Dhyai on short notice, so they follow him there.

83.content: Keon is a blind elder Vanara in Gandharva Ville who recognises people by their footsteps and says that travellers, merchants and adventurers are frequent. Before the Chapter III climax he worried that Akasha use was growing while fewer Dusk Birds flew from Sumeru City; afterwards he says more birds sing in the forest now the Akasha is shut down, believes things will improve under Lesser Lord Kusanali, and hopes to live to see her restore Sumeru's glory.

84.content:
Garden of Endless Pillars (also: Desert Vivarium): The Garden of Endless Pillars is a one-time domain in the Hypostyle Desert of Sumeru's Great Red Sand, west of the Dune of Carouses. It is the last surviving garden of Tulaytullah, the ancient "city of sapphire", once a palace-like place under thousands of giant pillars. The city is long gone; the garden endures and is now a paradise for fungi.

The domain's in-game text says that priests and the powerful once walked freely beneath the pillars, and that all that remains of the proud city is ruin. The white tree, Irminsul, and the ley lines are credited with keeping the garden alive through the centuries of desert wars.

Geography: A garden of broken pillars in the Hypostyle Desert, west of the Dune of Carouses. Within, ruined terraces are covered with oversized mushrooms and flowering plants. The domain has a single level, called Desert Vivarium; five Pyro monuments around its entrance must be lit in order before it opens. Dendro is recommended, and a Dendro character is needed to complete it.

History: The garden is what is left of Tulaytullah, a city-state said to have risen from the tears of the goddess Nabu Malikata after the fall of her fellow Angels. After King Deshret's civilisation fell, the priest Hermanubis founded the original Temple of Silence there and made it a city of wisdom, with shimmering canals, sapphire-domed buildings and gardens of padisarah and pomegranate. The Temple's departure, wars with Gurabad's kings and later conquest by foreign Khagans ended its prominence; its decline was like that of the other desert kingdoms.

Dangers: Fungi of several kinds: floating and grounded Dendro fungi, whirling Cryo and Electro fungi, and Hydroshrooms. They drift between the pillars and ambush anyone crossing the ruin.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the garden is unchanged: an accessible one-time domain. No later content has altered it.

85.content: Tulaytullah, the City of Sapphire, was a city-state of the Hypostyle Desert whose renown began when Hermanubis founded the original Temple of Silence there. When the Temple's members left after wars, the city lost its defenders and fell, like the other desert kingdoms. Its surviving garden is the Garden of Endless Pillars.

86.content:
Gate of Zulqarnain: The Gate of Zulqarnain is a gate-like ruin and cavern site in Gavireh Lajavard, part of Sumeru's Girdle of the Sands. An Iniquitous Baptist, a boss of the Abyss, is found here, and the underground Subterranean Defile hides one of the Great Songs of Khvarena sought in a world quest. The wiki ties its eight-pointed star motif to Khaenri'ah.

Nothing in canon says who built the Gate or what it was for. Its name echoes the Arabic Dhu al-Qarnayn, "two-horned".

Geography: Located in the Gavireh Lajavard area of the Girdle of the Sands, a region the Adventurers' Guild commission describes as the northern desert. The Gate stands at the surface; the Subterranean Defile is the cave beneath, where the Wenut sleeps.

Dangers: The Iniquitous Baptist, a normal boss of the Abyss family. It uses a combination of Cryo, Electro, Hydro and Pyro, whose mix rotates daily, and has extra limbs from "evolution" through the Abyss's power. Notes elsewhere remark that Abyssal power is little different from elemental items in practice.

Quests: In the world quest series Khvarena of Good and Evil, the Order of Skeptics' sage Nasejuna sends the Traveler to find the Great Songs of Khvarena. The quest As the Khvarena's Light Shows: Dukkha starts at the Gate of Zulqarnain: one Great Song is in the cavern where the petrified Setekh Wenut sleeps. Nasejuna remarks that the song has little effect even near the Wenut, and concludes it affects only things related to the Abyss.

Status as of 7.1: An open ruin and boss site, with no inhabitants beyond the Abyss creature. As of Version 7.1 nothing found changes it.

87.comment: Gate of Zulqarnain: Great Song of Khvarena at the Gate
87.content: The Great Songs of Khvarena hold great power, but only the Pari can obtain the Khvarena's approval and unleash it through a ritual. Three songs are to be gathered; the last lies in ruins elsewhere. The one at the Gate lies in the cave near the Setekh Wenut and is found in the quest Dukkha.

88.content:
Gavireh Lajavard: Gavireh Lajavard is the mountainous western stretch of the Girdle of the Sands, a forbidden-feeling region of Sumeru added in version 3.6. Its subareas include the Gate of Zulqarnain, the Temir Mountains, Tunigi Hollow and the buried Khaenri'ahn factory Hangeh Afrasiyab. Beneath it lie ruins of the lost nation of Khaenri'ah, and above it the Order of Skeptics keep watch.

The Girdle of the Sands is described officially as a forbidden realm beneath the desert where few have set foot, holding the ruins of an ancient civilisation, the legacy of the divine and a hidden lost Darshan. Gavireh Lajavard and the Realm of Farakhkert are the Girdle's two areas.

Geography: Rugged high ground. The Temir Mountains are the main passage between the Desert of Hadramaveth and the rest of the Girdle of the Sands, and the Gate of Zulqarnain stands among them. Tunigi Hollow is a deep hollow that leads down to the Harvisptokhm, and a locked Khaenri'ahn gate lies far below at Hangeh Afrasiyab.

Places: The Gate of Zulqarnain, whose name the wiki traces to Dhu al-Qarnayn, the figure who built a barrier against Gog and Magog. The Temir Mountains. Tunigi Hollow, the epicentre of the Abyssal contamination during the cataclysm. Hangeh Afrasiyab, an abandoned underground Khaenri'ahn factory for processing Azosite. Pyrrho's campsite, southwest of the waypoint into the Temir Mountains, and the Molten Iron Fortress domain.

People: Few live here. The Order of Skeptics hold an outpost behind the Statue of the Seven, where a note orders strict control of mountain passes to ensure a ceremony and plan can be completed. The Pari Sorush joins the Traveler, and the Pari live in the nearby Vourukasha Oasis.

History: Tunigi Hollow was the epicentre of the Abyssal and forbidden-knowledge pollution that spread from Khaenri'ah during the cataclysm. Several gods, including Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and Egeria, came to suppress the defilement seeping from the godless nation below. Hangeh Afrasiyab, a Khaenri'ahn factory for refining Azosite, remains sealed above the lost kingdom.

Dangers: Abyssal and Fatui forces, the Iniquitous Baptist, hilichurls (including Hydro rogues), Thundercraven and Rockfond Rifthound whelps, fungi, and the remnants of Khaenri'ahn defences. Tunigi Hollow's defilement is a danger until it is cleansed.

Travel: The Temir Mountains connect the area to the Desert of Hadramaveth. The Order of Skeptics control the mountain passes. Tunigi Hollow provides the way down to the Harvisptokhm, and after the Rite of Chinvat jumping into it sends the player there.

Quests: The Splendorous Sky That Day, Asipattravana Itihasa, The Hymn of Tir Yazad (Parts 1 and 2), As the Khvarena's Light Shows and its Dukkha chapter, Monumental Study, Pale Fire, Awakening's Real Sound, Lightcall Resonance, The Recollector's Path and Investigate the Fatui Camps Marked by Sosi. These form the Khvarena of Good and Evil storyline, treated in the Vourukasha Oasis entity.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the region is calmer and its worst defilement cleansed, with the Khaenri'ahn ruins still sealed or silent.

The Sign of Apaosha was extinguished in The Hymn of Tir Yazad (Part 2); nothing from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes the area.

89.content: An abandoned underground Khaenri'ahn factory for processing Azosite, with a sealed gate to the lost kingdom within. A Great Song of Khvarena is retrieved here in As the Khvarena's Light Shows by the Traveler, Paimon, Sorush and Nasejuna.

90.content: The epicentre of Abyssal and forbidden-knowledge pollution during the cataclysm; several gods, among them Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and Egeria, came to suppress the defilement. After the Rite of Chinvat, jumping into the hollow takes the player to the Harvisptokhm.

91.content:
Girdle of the Sands: The Girdle of the Sands is a remote desert subregion in the northwest of Sumeru, beyond the Temir Mountains. Here, during the cataclysm 500 years ago, Abyssal monsters poured up through a rift from the ruined kingdom of Khaenri'ah below, and the former Hydro Archon Egeria was slain there fighting them. Her remains became the Amrita, a sea of pure dew in the Vourukasha Oasis, where the Pari, flower-like bird spirits born of the divine bird Simurgh's Khvarena, still stand guard. Its two areas are Gavireh Lajavard and the Realm of Farakhkert.

It is an old war zone that never fully healed, a place of rock, swamps and sealed ruins. Travellers find the Order of Skeptics, a small band of scholars descended from rainforest Akademiya researchers, camped near the Temir Mountains.

Geography: Gavireh Lajavard ("azure desert") holds the Gate of Zulqarnain, the Temir Mountains (the main passage from the Desert of Hadramaveth) and Tunigi Hollow. The Realm of Farakhkert holds the Asipattravana Swamp, the Hills of Barsom, the Samudra Coast (the far northwest border of the Sumeru desert, with sandy beaches and clear blue water) and the Vourukasha Oasis at its heart. After the Mondstadt Prologue's final act, a Teleport Waypoint here, meant to give quick access to Fontaine, can also serve as quick access to the Sumeru desert.

People: The Pari are a sentient form of Khvarena in avian, flower-like bodies, each with a fated duty they carry out alone. Zurvan is the First Pari and elder; Sorush, Mihir and Rashnu are others. The Order of Skeptics, also called Shamaniyya or the Nagarjunites, is a small group of scholars (Pyrrho and Sosi among them) descended from rainforest researchers.

History: Long ago the goddess Nabu Malikata foresaw the cataclysm, made a shard of Khvarena and entrusted it to Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, who shaped it into the divine bird Simurgh. When the cataclysm came, the monsters' horde and the pollution of forbidden knowledge flowed from Khaenri'ah through Tunigi Hollow; Egeria and other gods went to suppress it, and she died there. Her body became the Amrita; Rukkhadevata grew the Harvisptokhm from it, and Simurgh sacrificed herself in the Amrita, shattering into countless Khvarena that became the Pari.

Dangers: Abyssal defilement (purple mist, gray crystals and Defiled Beacons), Abyss Heralds, the Iniquitous Baptist, Consecrated Fanged Beasts and Horned Crocodiles, rifthounds, Fatui skirmishers and hilichurls (including those corrupted by Abyssal energy).

Quests: The Khvarena of Good and Evil world quest series (3.6) unfolds here: The Splendorous Sky That Day, Awakening's Real Sound, Asipattravana Itihasa, As the Khvarena's Light Shows, and The Hymn of Tir Yazad (Parts 1 and 2). The Traveler becomes Sorush's Yasnapati, helps her gather the Great Songs of Khvarena, learns that Nasejuna and Klingsor sought to break the Harvisptokhm's seal and cleanse the Sign of Apaosha, and completes the Rite of Chinvat and Rite of Ab-Zohr.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Sign of Apaosha has vanished and the Harvisptokhm has regrown a glowing blue canopy. The Pari still guard the Oasis, which stays closed to strangers. Nasejuna has fled and the Order of Skeptics has no leader.

No version up to 7.1 adds new areas here; Sorush does appear in the 6.6 Archon Quest, bringing Aranara to the Traveler during Sumeru's Irminsul crisis. Zurvan asked the Traveler to give her greetings to Dainsleif. The Harvisptokhm is purified, but the Abyss's interest in the Great Songs and the open question of the Skeptics' future remain.

92.content: The Pari are avian, flower-like beings descended from Simurgh, created when her Khvarena combined with the Amrita. They are the only sentient form of Khvarena. Each has a fated task to undertake alone; many live only to serve it. They believe their god is Egeria, whose consciousness lies in the Harvisptokhm. They fought in the cataclysm with Khaenri'ahn warriors, a masked sword-wielder and a one-armed sage, and Akademiya scholars. Their human partners are called Yasnapati.

93.comment: Girdle of the Sands: Vourukasha Oasis and the Harvisptokhm
93.content: Vourukasha Oasis holds the Amrita, a sea of pure dew made from the remains of Egeria, the Hydro Archon who ruled Fontaine for about 1,500 years and died at Tunigi Hollow in the cataclysm. Rukkhadevata grew the Harvisptokhm, a giant tree, from the Amrita to anchor Egeria's consciousness and let her absorb the defilement from the rift. Inside lies the lotus Gaokerena, where the Pari god's consciousness slumbers. Before the 3.6 quest the tree was a withered stump under the Sign of Apaosha; afterwards it has a glowing blue canopy.

94.comment: Girdle of the Sands: Order of Skeptics
94.content: The Order of Skeptics, once a branch of the Akademiya, descends from scholars led by the one-armed sage Nagarjuna who came to help the Pari defeat the Abyss. They settled in the Girdle and forged bonds with the Pari. The Akademiya calls them Nagarjunites. After a disastrous Akademiya expedition into Khaenri'ahn ruins and the loss of their archives, they neglected their duty. Members included Pyrrho, Sosi, Aryadeva (who moved to Sumeru City) and Nagahvaya (now in the Temple of Space).

95.comment: Girdle of the Sands: Simurgh and the Great Songs of Khvarena
95.content: Khvarena is an energy created by Nabu Malikata to oppose the cataclysm; it can purify Abyssal energy and forbidden knowledge. Simurgh was a shard of it; when Egeria's Amrita started to be corrupted she flew into the pool and shattered into countless motes. Zurvan fused the strongest Khvarena into five Great Songs. The Sign of Apaosha is a phenomenon in the sky above Tunigi Hollow, a reflection of the Abyss that corrupts the land beneath it.

96.content:
Grand Bazaar: The Grand Bazaar is the market quarter of Sumeru City, a lively, artistic place crowded with merchants selling handmade goods. Its people are mostly ordinary folk who want a steady life rather than scholars or sages. The Zubayr Theater, Nilou's troupe, sits inside it.

It has three entrances from the rest of Sumeru City. It is where everyday Sumeru life, craft, music and dance meet, away from the scholarly world of the Akademiya.

Places: The Zubayr Theater is the Bazaar's best-known landmark, a small theater run by the playwright Sheikh Zubayr. Around it are stalls for woven goods, vases and jars, spices, toys and blankets. Treasures Street, Lambad's Tavern and the Citadel of Regzar belong to other parts of Sumeru City rather than the Bazaar itself.

People: Stallholders and passers-by fill the market: Shevirme (stall vendor), Sulaykha (blanket shop owner), Hushang (toy seller), Jut (spice merchant), Afshin (traveling merchant), Farhad (porter) and the wealthy businessman Bhabha by day. Mercenaries of the Corps of Thirty (Azra, Sahar, Taher) keep order.

Atmosphere: Bustling, colourful and noisy: the Traveler's voice-over line has Paimon marvelling that the residents all seem so talented, selling woven goods, vases and fragrant spices and singing and dancing very well. It feels like a place where anyone might burst into a song or a dance.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Bazaar is an ordinary working market, with no later event recorded in the pages consulted that changes it.

97.comment: Grand Bazaar: Zubayr Theater in the Bazaar
97.content: The Zubayr Theater is housed in a hollow of the great tree and is the stage on which Nilou dances. Its manager, playwright and director is Sheikh Zubayr. See the theater's own entry for detail.

98.content:
Great Hall of Truths (also: Hall of Great Truths): The Great Hall of Truths is a chamber inside the Mausoleum of King Deshret in Sumeru's Hypostyle Desert, joined to the bottomless Duat Hall on its south side. In the quest Dual Evidence the Traveler and Paimon reach it by following the Scarlet Sand Slate, and its giant central device carries them up to Aaru's Shut at the summit.

The slate describes it as the place where those who bring praises before King Deshret, show wisdom and do not fear the darkness may obtain unique gifts. In practice it is the last stage of a trial laid out in imagery of birds, rivers and sacred flame.

Geography: Part of the Mausoleum complex under the Hypostyle Desert. It is connected to Duat Hall at its south side; Duat Hall is entered through an underground waypoint directly south of the Mausoleum and needs the Ferryman's Clearance from the Scarlet Sand Slate. The central section opens onto the way up to Aaru's Shut once Dual Evidence has been completed.

History: In the quest the Scarlet Sand Slate tells the party to prove itself in three ways: pass the river as a falcon, peck three organs, and burn the embers of the sun at three places with feathers. The trial halls Place of Rebirth, Place of Breath and Place of Swallowing each light a sigil on the slate; once all are lit the Great Hall of Truths appears. The Vahumana researcher Soheil had mocked Tirzad's paper on the Mausoleum, and the party's aim is to prove the paper true.

Quests: The hall is the centre of Dual Evidence, the first quest in the world quest series Old Notes and New Friends, begun at Aaru Village after Golden Slumber is done. The quest grants the achievements Walk Like King Deshret's People, The Straight Path and The Path To Enlightenment for the successive stages.

Status as of 7.1: Open to exploration. The cyclone that long crowned the Mausoleum is off for good after Dual Evidence, and Aaru's Shut can be visited through the hall's centre.

Nothing found in the sources up to Version 7.1 changes the hall or reveals more of its original purpose.

99.comment: Great Hall of Truths: Dual Evidence and the Ascent
99.content: Dual Evidence has the Traveler follow the Scarlet Sand Slate through Duat Hall and the three trial halls, then use the Great Hall of Truths to climb to Aaru's Shut. The Mausoleum's long-running cyclone stops for good, the summit is changed, and the party brings back a slate as proof for Soheil.

100.content:
Great Red Sand (also: Deshret Desert): The Great Red Sand, also called the Deshret Desert, is the vast desert of western Sumeru. Once the realm of King Deshret, Lord of Deserts, it is now a sea of dunes dotted with buried temples, ruined cities, oases and hidden machine halls. The Eremite tribes, descendants of his people, wander here, and Aaru Village keeps his memory. Beyond the Wall of Samiel on the east lies the rainforest of the Dharma Forest. Sandstorms, Ruin Golems and the old Jinn legends make it dangerous and rich in secrets.

Its four main areas are the Hypostyle Desert, the Land of Lower Setekh, the Land of Upper Setekh and the Desert of Hadramaveth. The nation's wisdom-seeking scholars have long coveted its ruins, while the desert folk remember it as a lost kingdom.

Geography: Four areas make up the subregion. The Hypostyle Desert holds Khemenu Temple, Sobek Oasis, three named dunes and the Mausoleum of King Deshret. The Land of Lower Setekh holds Aaru Village and Khaj-Nisut; the Land of Upper Setekh holds the Valley of Dahri. The Desert of Hadramaveth, the largest area, stretches west of them and holds the old city of Gurabad, the Tanit Camps and Mt. Damavand. The east is bounded by the Wall of Samiel, with Caravan Ribat at its foot.

People: The Eremites are the desert's mercenaries, descended from the vanished civilisations. They fall into many tribes and factions, each with its own code, bound by stories passed down orally and by dance and sword traditions inherited from Deshret's age. Aaru Village's people and its Guardian, Candace, are spoken of as his descendants; Dehya and Cyno also have ties here.

History: Long ago the desert was the domain of the gods Nabu Malikata, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and King Deshret, the Three Eternal Companion-Gods; Deshret and Nabu Malikata had earlier built the city of Ay-Khanoum together. Nabu Malikata died, and Rukkhadevata left to build a rainforest civilisation while Deshret kept the desert. He pursued a dream paradise through forbidden knowledge until the knowledge ruined his people, brought the Withering and drove him to sacrifice his life. His vassal city Gurabad had already fallen, destroyed by the Jinni Liloupar's revenge.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Great Red Sand has come through the Irminsul crisis of the 6.6 Archon Quest. During it the rainforest's people were evacuated to Caravan Ribat and on to Aaru Village, Jinn sandstorms besieged the desert until the reawakened Jinni Liloupar calmed them, and the Seven Pillars opened Aaru, whose reconfigured system now collects and stores the information Irminsul once held. The Tanit tribe remains destroyed.

Opening Aaru freed Heryshaf, Sobek and Thoth from their imprisonment (Nefer answered Thoth's three questions) and released the countless souls of the Golden Slumber to the ley lines, ending King Deshret's afterlife. Afterwards Thoth and Heryshaf chose to stay at the Temple of Silence for the time being, and Liloupar later faded away at Windrise in Mondstadt after absorbing Collei's god remains. Separately, a 5.0 patch adjusted terrain in the Desert of Hadramaveth, and the 6.5 Temple of Space includes a Desert Pavilion built in the style of the desert temples; neither changes the desert's story.

101.comment: Great Red Sand: King Deshret and the Three Eternal Companion-Gods
101.content: King Deshret, the Lord of Deserts, also called Al-Ahmar and Amun, ruled the desert alongside Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and Nabu Malikata, the Goddess of Flowers, as the Three Eternal Companion-Gods. Each held a different realm: banquet, authority and life. He loved Nabu Malikata. When he pursued forbidden knowledge to defy the Heavenly Principles, Rukkhadevata left; Nabu Malikata ultimately gave her life for the ritual. Mourning, Deshret became the Mourning King, secluded himself, and built the Primal Constructs and the mechanism at Khaj-Nisut in pursuit of an eternal "golden slumber". He is said to have separated his mind from his body, leaving a golden husk in the mausoleum.

102.comment: Great Red Sand: Gurabad and Liloupar
102.content: Gurabad, the "city of brass" or "City of Kings", was a vassal city in the southwest of the Desert of Hadramaveth. A shepherd, Ormazd, united the tribes with the help of Deshret and the Jinni Liloupar, but he grew tyrannical and kept slavery. Liloupar plotted his city's fall across generations. Her daughter Shirin, tricked, served poisoned honey that killed Ormazd and Shirin's siblings; her son Kisra became King Parvezravan, forced Shirin to make mindless Jinn to power machines that replaced slave labour, and faced the Brass Mask rebellion led by his own son, Shiruyeh. Liloupar used Abyssal power and most of the city sank into a chasm; a plague then killed half the survivors.

103.content: Aaru Village is the largest human settlement in the desert, holding Deshret's followers and descendants and Akademiya exiles. It stands as the last embers of his civilisation, guarded by Candace and led by its chief, Uncle Anpu; its Village Keepers are exiled Akademiya scholars. The Old Blind Poet and others settled here to await his return. Caravan Ribat is the checkpoint on the road to the forest.

104.comment: Great Red Sand: Eremite Spirits and Legends
104.content: The Eremites are Sumeru's only authorised mercenary organisation. They hail from the fallen civilisations of the Great Red Sand and are very loosely organised: anyone can join, though traditionally only desert folk could. Rukh Shah is one exception. Some borrow power from fragments of ancient desert spirits that live in their weapons; the spirits wake in danger and, it is said, demand blood. They work all over Teyvat and partner with the Adventurers' Guild.

105.content:
Grove of Dreams: The Grove of Dreams is an underground cavern in Apam Woods, in the Dharma Forest of Sumeru. Arapandu describes it as a place where one may enter dreams.

It connects to the Ruins of Dahri to the west and holds one of the "branch and leaf" energy sources of the Varuna Contraption. Like Vanarana, it exists in a real and a dream version; the Traveler switches between them by playing the Rhythm of the Great Dream on a Vintage Lyre at a Silapna.

Geography: Entered through a stone-littered opening in the ground, reached by following a large tree root north of the Slumbering Roots quest marker. The twisting roots of the great tree make finding anything there hard.

People: Arakunti, one of the Aranara who tend the Varuna Contraption, withdraws here and hides unless Aranara music is played. He speaks cryptically, saying one might be a tree, rain, a dream of Vana or the strings of an instrument.

History: The Grove shelters one component of the Varuna Contraption, the device Greater Lord Rukkhadevata built to bring timely rains. It had gone unmaintained, and part of its restoration is done here.

Quests: Slumbering Roots, part of Varuna Gatha: the Traveler follows Arakunti into the Grove, plays the Rhythm of the Great Dream at Silapna, and in the dream turns three leaves toward the branch.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 unchanged; nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content was found.

106.content:
Gurabad (also: City of Brass, City of Kings): Gurabad, called the City of Kings and the city of brass, was a great ancient city in the southwest of Sumeru's Desert of Hadramaveth. It prospered as King Deshret's favoured vassal, then fell: the shepherd-king Ormazd betrayed the Jinni Liloupar, who took revenge over three generations, ending with much of the city swallowed by a chasm and a plague. Later kings kept trying to restore it. Its ruins are now largely abandoned.

Its downfall is told in the book The Tale of Shiruyeh and Shirin and in the quest Memories of Gurabad. Because holding Gurabad later became a way to claim the whole desert, the ruins are woven into many other stories: Tulaytullah, Ay-Khanoum, Makhaira, Faramarz and the Eremites.

Geography: The ruins lie in the south-west of the Desert of Hadramaveth, in the Great Red Sand. A great gate and a large Ruin Golem of Khaenri'ahn make, identical to the one at Devantaka Mountain, stand among the remains. The Debris of Panjvahe, in the same desert, was a poor district served by a river valley that once irrigated it.

History: A shepherd, Ormazd, won the favour of King Deshret and the Jinni Liloupar and used her blessing to unite the desert peoples, founding Gurabad after Nabu Malikata's death. Liloupar expected him to end slavery; he kept it. Her sense of betrayal made her plot the city's ruin across three generations. She had her daughter by Ormazd, Shirin, bring poisoned honey to a banquet: Ormazd and Shirin's siblings died, Shirin lost her mind, and her husband Kisra (Liloupar's own son, raised as Ormazd's heir and titled Parvez) became king as Parvezravan. He used Jinn-powered machines made by Shirin to replace slave labour, and the resentment of those left jobless fed the "Brass Mask" rebellion of Khorramdin, in truth Parvezravan and Shirin's banished son Shiruyeh. The Great Revolt followed; Liloupar used Abyssal power, turned Parvezravan into a monster and let much of the city fall into the earth. A plague then killed about half the inhabitants.

Status as of 7.1: Gurabad is an abandoned ruin. Some Eremites live in parts of it, and others come on expeditions to hunt for the city's treasures.

The ruins hold the Ruin Golem and relics of several failed revivals. Liloupar's long imprisonment is part of its legacy and appears in the Sumeru Archon Quest King Deshret and the Three Magi, where Memories of Gurabad also explains the city's fall. Nothing found up to Version 7.1 reports a later change to the site.

107.content:
Gurabad's Ruin - Temple of Deshret (also: Temple of Gurabad, Temple of Deshret, Gurabad's Ruin): Gurabad's Ruin - Temple of Deshret is a temple complex on the outskirts of the fallen city of Gurabad, in the canyon country of the Desert of Hadramaveth. It is full of sand-driving machines and sealed rooms, and two hidden chambers on its upper and lower levels hold murals about the shepherd-king Ormazd and the Jinni Liloupar. It is explored in the quest The Temple Where Sand Flows Like Tears.

The Tanit tribe regards the ruins as cursed and taboo. Jeht, who counts as half an outsider, goes in with the Traveler to find a fragment of the Mother of the Jinn.

Geography: A temple with an upper and a lower level, and a giant central device. It lies in Safhe Shatranj, a canyon the Tanit call the Great Rift, in the southwest of the Desert of Hadramaveth; before the quest the area is called The Temples Forsaken and drifts of sand block the way.

Places: The main temple centres on a giant device, which the quest has the party touch more than once as the sand-sealing machines are woken and the sand is made to flow. Opposite the square is a smaller ruin that holds Liloupar's Cell. Two sealed mural rooms, one on each level, are the temple's best known features.

History: Tradition among the desert folk says Gurabad was the work of the shepherd Ormazd, who with King Deshret's grace and Liloupar's help overthrew the tyrant Huvashtra and gathered the desert's wandering tribes. Liloupar later brought ruin on the city across three generations in revenge for his corruption, and King Deshret punished her by splitting her into seven fragments hidden in the Great Red Sand.

Culture: For the Tanit tribe the ruins are bad luck. Their guide Azariq stops short of going deeper than the temple's gate. Jeht quotes the Tanit proverb that the closer the home the more reticent the heart, and Matriarch Babel's maxim that true gold has deep roots in soil and spring.

Quests: The Temple Where Sand Flows Like Tears is the second part of the world quest series The Dirge of Bilqis. The Murals of Gurabad, an unofficially titled hidden exploration objective, becomes available once The Dirge of Bilqis is finished; it requires finding six Mysterious Stone Slates, three per door, and awards two Precious Chests and the achievement The Nameless City's Past.

Status as of 7.1: Accessible and cleared of sand. Nothing found up to Version 7.1 reveals later change here.

108.comment: Gurabad's Ruin - Temple of Deshret: The Murals of Gurabad
108.content: After finishing The Dirge of Bilqis, the Traveler can find slates I to III to open the upper-level door and slates IV to VI to open the lower-level door of the temple. The murals show Ormazd, Ormazd with Liloupar and the defeated tyrant Huvashtra. A tablet in the lower room gives Ormazd's account, in which Deshret's grace let him unseat Huvashtra, the Jinni came to help, and he promised his kingdom to Liloupar and the king alike.

109.content:
Hangeh Afrasiyab (also: Forge of the Abandoned Foundry, Gate of Everlasting Mourning): Hangeh Afrasiyab is an abandoned underground factory of the lost kingdom of Khaenri'ah, hidden under Gavireh Lajavard in Sumeru's Girdle of the Sands. It once processed Azosite, an energy block drawn from ley lines, and deep inside is a sealed gate to the lost nation itself. In the quest As the Khvarena's Light Shows it holds the last Great Song of Khvarena, and Nasejuna reveals he has been using the party.

Dahri is an archaic Sumeru name for Khaenri'ah, so the quest calls this an underground Dahrian factory. By Nasejuna's reading of the records it belonged to the Schwanenritter, the knight order that fought the monsters of the cataclysm.

Geography: Two map levels, upper and lower, in Gavireh Lajavard. The main hall is the energy control hub, with relays sealed in Gray Crystals, a furnace for smelting Azosite, an elevator to the deepest level and a control room above. Mourning Flowers and Trishiraite are local specialties; the Gate of Everlasting Mourning viewpoint overlooks the sealed gate.

History: Azosite was made here by extracting pure elemental energy from ley lines and smelting it into Energy Blocks. A mutilated set of notes says the royal workshop Gnade had gone out of use and this was probably the last workshop with a full Azosite-powered system. Nasejuna, citing records, says it was owned by the Schwanenritter, as was the proving ground at Madinat al-Nuhas, and that they resisted the monsters that came from below in the cataclysm 500 years ago.

Quests: As the Khvarena's Light Shows (Khvarena of Good and Evil, part 2) leads the Traveler, Paimon, Sorush and Nasejuna here to seek the fifth Great Song of Khvarena. Nasejuna opens doors, links circuits with Farrwicks to power three relays and then the central control device, and rides the elevator down with them.

Status as of 7.1: Abandoned. Some machinery still runs and the main gate toward Khaenri'ah is sealed. Nothing found up to Version 7.1 changes this.

110.comment: Hangeh Afrasiyab: Gate of Everlasting Mourning
110.content: A grand gate leading to the world beneath the soil, sealed tight. Its viewpoint text adds that the once prosperous kingdom behind it has long since turned to rubble.

111.content:
Harvisptokhm (also: God of the Pari, Mother Tree of All Seeds): The Harvisptokhm is the giant tree in the middle of Vourukasha Oasis in Sumeru, the Pari's homeland, and serves as the God of the Pari. It grew from the remains of Egeria, the former Hydro Archon, and keeps her consciousness tied to the mortal world while suppressing an Abyssal rift.

Its interior can be entered through a hole at Tunigi Hollow or from the top of its stump. Inside lies a giant lotus, the Gaokerena, in which the God of the Pari's consciousness slumbers.

Geography: Stands at the centre of Vourukasha Oasis, in the Realm of Farakhkert of the Girdle of the Sands. Tunigi Hollow, the old site of the Abyssal rift, opens into it. Around it lies the Amrita, a sea of pure dew made from Egeria's remains.

People: The Pari are the oasis's guardians and regard it as their god. Elder Zurvan sealed the Oasis with the Great Songs of Khvarena after an Abyss attack and admits only heroes bonded with Pari and pilgrims who come to worship Egeria. Sorush, Mihir and Rashnu are Pari in the quest line.

History: During the cataclysm, gods including Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and Egeria went to Tunigi Hollow to suppress the Abyssal defilement from Khaenri'ah below. Egeria was slain in the battle and her body became Amrita. Rukkhadevata grew the Harvisptokhm from it to anchor her consciousness, so it could absorb the defilement from the rift and keep the seal.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the defilement has been cleansed and the seal holds; the tree is a living, restored sacred site. Nothing found in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content changes it.

112.content: The giant lotus inside the Harvisptokhm, where the God of the Pari's consciousness is said to slumber. In The Hymn of Tir Yazad the Traveler defends the Flower of Sanctity there against Abyssal creatures while the power of Amrita lends help.

113.comment: Harvisptokhm: Egeria's Remains and the Amrita
113.content: Egeria was the Hydro Archon and God of Justice who ruled Fontaine until 500 years ago, killed at Tunigi Hollow during the cataclysm. Her body became the Amrita, from which the tree was grown; Focalors succeeded her.

114.content:
Hills of Barsom (also: Barsom): The Hills of Barsom lie just north of Asipattravana Swamp in the Realm of Farakhkert, in Sumeru's Girdle of the Sands. They are home to the Barsom, a huge pine with pink foliage, and to its familiar, the Pari Rashnu, who sleeps there.

The hills were the setting of the Order of Skeptics' old musical ritual with the Pari and are the start of the world quest "Awakening's Real Sound" (3.6), part of the Khvarena of Good and Evil series.

Geography: A rise of ground dominated by the Barsom tree, a towering pine with pink foliage. The area sits just north of Asipattravana Swamp, and the Samudra Coast and a cave by the water lie close by.

People: Rashnu, a Pari called the Familiar of the Barsom, lives in and around the tree, usually asleep. Nasejuna, the Order of Skeptics' Nasuraia (Vijnanapati), brings the Traveler to the hills and cares about the Order's traditions; Sorush, the young Pari who calls the Traveler her Yasnapati, comes to wake Rashnu and take her to the Vourukasha Oasis.

History: By the Order of Skeptics' account, their predecessors, after helping the Pari quell the disaster of the cataclysm, befriended them. Barsom's familiar liked music, so the Skeptics made the Kory Drums; to make the bond ("Laupa") official, five drums had to be gathered and played to scores. The drums were later lost and Barsom's familiar stopped answering them.

Quests: "Awakening's Real Sound" begins here (3.6). Julien's "An Artist Adrift" also starts nearby, at a cave between the Samudra Coast and Asipattravana Swamp, once "The Splendorous Sky That Day" is complete.

Atmosphere: Quiet and sleepy. The giant pink pine towers over the hills, and the Pari who dwells in it dislikes noise; her only stated complaint is the drumming.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Rashnu has left her post to join Sorush at the Vourukasha Oasis, though the Barsom remains.

The Kory Drums have been recovered and played once; the Order of Skeptics' version of the ritual has been corrected, but Nasejuna's unanswered questions about the Skeptics' traditions are left for Rashnu to answer "later, perhaps".

115.comment: Hills of Barsom: Kory Drums and the Skeptics' Ritual
115.content: Mysterious drums said to symbolise the union between the Order of Skeptics and the Pari. There are five, one per element (Rupa, Samjna, Sankhara, Vedana, Vijnana), each with a score that must be played in order. The scores are carved in stone and survived the sandstorms; the drums themselves were lost until the Traveler found them. In truth Rashnu scattered them because they were noisy.

116.content: A Pari known as the Familiar of the Barsom. Sleepy, honest and uninterested in "human business". She answers Sorush, whom she recognises, agrees to go with her to the Vourukasha Oasis, and says that sleeping is also a duty. Her Zoroastrian-derived name refers to the yazata of justice, according to the wiki.

117.content:
House of Daena: The House of Daena is the great library at the centre of the Sumeru Akademiya in Sumeru City, the largest library in all of Teyvat. It was once reckoned the repository of all knowledge in the world because of its unmatched collection, but the Akasha System has since taken that role. It still stands as a symbol of Sumeru, the Nation of Wisdom.

Officially only students and teachers of the Akademiya may borrow its books. It is run by a Grand Conservator, who is responsible for acquiring new material and maintaining the existing collection.

Places: An elevated platform in the middle of the library carries a lift. After the events of the Archon Quest "Jnagarbha Day" it can rise to the Grand Sage's office or descend to the confinement room.

People: The librarian Katayoun and the matra Shohre work here, with students and researchers such as Hunayn, Sanad, Gregor, Jafar and Nargess. After the Archon Quest the mahamata Panah is found here.

Governance: Run as part of the Akademiya under a Grand Conservator; only its students and teachers may borrow books.

History: Once the world's bank of knowledge, it was superseded by the Akasha System, but the old library remains in use.

Atmosphere: Vast, hushed and scholarly, an old stack of shelves and reading rooms where researchers work by day and night; a symbol of Sumeru's reverence for learning.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the library stands as it did at the close of the 3.0 Archon Quest; no later change is recorded in the pages consulted.

118.content:
Hypostyle Desert: The Hypostyle Desert is the central part of Sumeru's Great Red Sand, the land of King Deshret's ruined civilisation. It contains the giant Mausoleum of King Deshret, the underground Khemenu Temple and the resting place of Sobek Oasis. The ancient city-state of Tulaytullah once stood here.

The name is an architectural term for a hall whose roof rests on rows of pillars, fitting the area's pillared temple ruins. The Golden Slumber quest series (3.1) runs through it.

Geography: A vast field of dunes and oases with a few plateaus. On a plateau north-east of the Sobek Oasis waypoint stands a stone tablet whose carved words promise that the golden sandstorm and burning sun will exorcise the darkness on behalf of the reader, guiding a spirit that perished here back to the Orchard of Pairidaeza. The Garden of Endless Pillars, a one-time domain, lies west of the Dune of Carouses.

Places: The Mausoleum of King Deshret, a golden husk left by the king, where his intelligence is not held. Khemenu Temple, an underground temple east of the Mausoleum. Sobek Oasis, a rest stop. The site of Tulaytullah, now at the Garden of Endless Pillars. The Altar of Mirages, which may be where Ay-Khanoum's remains lie.

People: The Eremites roam the area, and the Tighnarians were once associated with Tulaytullah. The followers of King Deshret live mostly at Aaru Village in the Land of Lower Setekh, not here. Travelling adventurers sometimes rest at Sobek Oasis, as one of Cyno's character stories notes.

History: Tulaytullah, the City of Sapphire, rose to prominence in the desert after King Deshret's civilisation fell. The priest Hermanubis founded the original Temple of Silence there and made it a city of wisdom, and the Temple kept the knowledge that survived the king's fall. After wars between city-states and Eremite tribes, the Temple's members left, and the city declined like the other desert kingdoms.

Dangers: Primal Constructs (Repulsors, Prospectors) in the ruins, Fatui and Eremite groups, scorpions and desert beasts, sunstroke, thirst, and the Mausoleum's old defences. The Garden of Endless Pillars domain has fungi.

Travel: Teleport waypoints are unlocked by stepping through Khemenu Temple and the Mausoleum. Travellers rest at Sobek Oasis. The Scarlet Sand Slate opens many of the temples and chambers.

Quests: Golden Slumber (3.1): An Introduction to Indoor Archaeology, The Secret of Al-Ahmar and Dreams Beneath the Searing Sand lead through Khemenu Temple and the Mausoleum to Khaj-Nisut. Others tied here include Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana, A Tower Unto Wisdom and Folly, Headlong Into the Sands, Darkness Looming and Invisible Barrier.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the desert is open and the Mausoleum's cyclone is gone.

Nothing from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes the area.

119.content: An ancient city-state of the Hypostyle Desert, once a city of wisdom founded around the Temple of Silence by the priest Hermanubis. It declined during the wars among desert city-states. Its refugees helped found Aaru Village.

120.content: A city built for the Jinn by King Deshret and Nabu Malikata, whose name means Moon Maiden in the Jinn's ancient language. Now in ruins, likely in the Hypostyle Desert; the Altar of Mirages may mark its remains.

121.content:
Kalimi Exchange (also: Kalimi stock exchange): The Kalimi Exchange is Sumeru City's stock exchange and marketplace, on Treasures Street. One can buy futures contracts here, and a bulletin board beside the building posts goods for sale. The Mahamata Barmak, a researcher with an economics degree, monitors it for illegal or fraudulent practice. A man who calls himself a millionaire, Hatim, stands outside during the day.

In Port Ormos, the Wikala Funduq trade supervisor Dilawar tells casual traders to "try your luck" at the Exchange, while warning that profit does not come easily.

People: Barmak is a Mahamata, an Akademiya official, posted at the Exchange. He welcomes "all law-abiding businessmen", says illegal trade is strictly prohibited, and says that as an economics researcher no speculation gets past him. In his private thoughts he is irritated by cocky youngsters who think they can get away with anything on his watch. Hatim is a self-proclaimed millionaire seen outside by day and inside Puspa Cafe at night. He calls the Exchange a place where people's strength, courage and insight are tested, and complains that its forecasters are amateurs.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Exchange is open and unchanged.

122.content:
Khaj-Nisut (also: Eye of the Sands, King Deshret's throne room): Khaj-Nisut ("Eye of the Sands" on the map before the Golden Slumber quests) is the throne temple of King Deshret, also called Al-Ahmar, buried in the Great Red Sand of Sumeru's desert. It is invisible until a visitor passes three trials, and the temple is built to recognise who is acknowledged: the scarlet slate that a visitor carries opens its doors, and its mechanisms test clearance. Inside, an immense empty throne sits at the top of a descent through lower halls. In the Golden Slumber quests the Eremite Samail was tricked onto the throne, entered the "Golden Slumber" that King Deshret's followers believe in, and Jebrael followed him in to stop him as the temple sealed behind them.

The name is Egyptian-derived for "appearance of the king", and the Chinese name uses a term for the manifestation of the sacred. The Scarlet Sand Slate calls it the sacred realm that all King Deshret's people aspired to reach, and warns that whoever acquires Al-Ahmar's wisdom loses their bodily form and cannot tell of it. The surrounding ruins are also the City of Gold domain, which the domain text describes as a stronghold once defended by seven battlements that crumbled overnight when King Deshret fell.

Geography: Khaj-Nisut lies in the Land of Lower Setekh, part of the Great Red Sand, in Sumeru's desert. An oasis in front of it is a resting place for travellers. The temple does not exist on the map or to the eye until the visitor has passed the three trials set around it and operated a Plinth of the Secret Rites; then it manifests. Inside it is a descent, not a climb: a lower floor, further halls below it, then a lift that carries visitors up to the throne room under the dome of Khaj-Nisut.

Places: Entrance gateway and oasis: the oasis outside is where travellers refresh themselves before paying tribute. Lower floor and descent: halls with mechanisms (Plinths of the Secret Rites, a central device that must be set in action in three steps). Throne room: the throne of Al-Ahmar on the upper floor, beside a statue of Heryshaf (as pictured on the wiki).

People: Samail of the Thutmose, an Eremite faction that wants King Deshret's lost power, and Jebrael, once his partner as one of the "twin blades of Thutmose" and now a father, reach the throne in the story. Jeht (Jebrael's daughter), the Akademiya researcher Tirzad, the Traveler and Paimon enter with Benben, a small Primal Construct that responds to the ruins. Nobody lives in Khaj-Nisut. The only residents are the Primal Constructs and mechanisms of King Deshret's age and, during the quest, Samail's Eremite mercenaries and Fatui Skirmishers.

History: Khaj-Nisut belonged to the civilisation of King Deshret, the Lord of Deserts, in the age before and during the Archon War. In the Golden Slumber quests (3.1) it is rediscovered: first the Mausoleum, then, after a series of trials, the temple itself. The throne is empty, and the "wisdom" of Al-Ahmar that texts promised there is not an object but a prayer.

Quests: Golden Slumber (World Quest series, 3.1), especially The Secret of Al-Ahmar and Dreams Beneath the Searing Sand. The follow-up series Old Notes and New Friends begins with Dual Evidence, which grants the Ferryman's Clearance for Duat Hall and the Great Hall of Truths in the Mausoleum.

Dangers: Primal Constructs and the building itself. In the quest, after Samail enters the Slumber, the temple turns hostile and the visitors have to flee through the lower floors while a "sea of consciousness" pursues them; if it touches a visitor the escape restarts in the game's time trial. Outside, Samail's Eremites and Fatui Skirmishers patrol the ruins during the quest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the throne is empty and the temple is sealed after the Golden Slumber events. Jebrael and Samail never returned in body; Jeht kept her father's axe and went looking for the Tanit. In 6.6, when the Seven Pillars opened Aaru, the souls trapped in the Golden Slumber, Jebrael's among them, were released to the ley lines, and Jebrael spoke briefly with Jeht before departing.

No later canon through 7.1 changes the building itself, but the Golden Slumber that its prayer opened no longer exists as a refuge for souls. The City of Gold domain (3.3) remains in the surrounding ruins.

123.comment: Khaj-Nisut: Dreams Beneath the Searing Sand
123.content: In the last chapter of the Golden Slumber, Jebrael and Jeht, the researcher Tirzad, the Traveler and Paimon travel to the oasis for Khaj-Nisut while the Eremite Samail's men attack the camp. A coded letter says Al-Ahmar's throne shows itself to those who pass three trials. After the trials Khaj-Nisut manifests; the party activates its mechanisms, rides the lift to the throne room and finds the throne empty. Samail arrives holding Jeht and demands the prayer needed to sit on the throne.

124.content:
Khemenu Temple (also: Temple of Secret Rites): Khemenu Temple is a buried temple in the Hypostyle Desert of Sumeru's Great Red Sand, underground to the east of King Deshret's Mausoleum. It is not the largest of the desert's temples but it is linked to the people: the Scarlet Sand Slate says all would enter and bow their heads to praise Deshret's wisdom. Its murals depict his reign.

The temple is explored in An Introduction to Indoor Archaeology, the second part of Golden Slumber, by the scholar Tirzad's team with the Traveler. It appears on the map once the quest is done.

Geography: Four map levels: the Entrance Hall, an Underground Area, the Underground Depths and a Chamber of Secrets. The slate tells a visitor to leave Abdju Road and walk toward the sunset along the axis. People painted images on the shrine walls with plant juice and ore powder, and sand does not cover them as it does footprints.

Places: Inside is a mural of a sun and an eye above seven pillars and many small figures. Behind it a passage opens upward when Tirzad bumps into the wall. The temple also holds a vessel, a boat, in a dry room, and mechanisms using fans, torches and an elevator.

History: The slate calls Khemenu Temple modest in size but close to ordinary people, a place where all entered and praised Deshret. The temple belongs to the realm of King Deshret, whose civilisation is gone; generations of Vahumana researchers have studied the desert's ruins.

Quests: In An Introduction to Indoor Archaeology Tirzad's team (Jeht, her father Jebrael and Benben) camps at an oasis and enters the temple. Benben opens the first door by itself. The party lights Primal Torches to open further doors, reaches a mural, and a sliding wall reveals a rising path to the next stage, The Secret of Al-Ahmar.

Status as of 7.1: Open. Nothing found up to Version 7.1 changes the temple or answers the questions about its murals.

125.comment: Khemenu Temple: Benben and the Temple Doors
125.content: Benben, a strange three-cornered machine, earlier made the stone slate light up in Golden Slumber, and in the temple opens Khemenu Temple's first door by itself, with Jeht guessing it is drawn to the doors' triangular shape. Tirzad's professional scorn for Benben is a running joke.

126.content:
Lamb-Devourer Rock: Lamb-Devourer Rock is a desert rock formation in the Land of Upper Setekh, in the Great Red Sand of Sumeru. It conceals the secret base of the Thutmose, a group of Eremites.

The base is reached in the world quest Hidden Mercenaries, where the Traveler follows Soheil's old notes about a place where Thutmose would appear and vanish.

Geography: A rock outcrop in the Land of Upper Setekh, with a hidden door that opens to a password-triggered device. The base lies behind it.

People: The Thutmose are Eremites who are devout believers of King Deshret. Seeking the secret of Al-Ahmar, they have gathered knowledge and collaborators from many sources, from Sumeru researchers to the Fatui. Jebrael and Samail were once called the twin blades of Thutmose. This is background from the Eremites' profile, not from the quest.

Quests: Hidden Mercenaries, in the Old Notes and New Friends chapter (part of Soheil's Wish), begins with Aaru Village. Steps: approach the rock, enter the secret base, look for valuables, hand slates to Soheil.

Dangers: Armed Eremites patrol the area; the quest uses stealth rather than direct combat.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no change to the base was found.

127.content:
Lambad's Tavern (also: Lambad Tavern): Lambad's Tavern is the main tavern and restaurant of Sumeru City, close to the lively Treasures Street. Its owner Lambad says he was a legendary sailor who sailed far and wide; the map description notes it is hard to tell how exaggerated that is, but the food makes the cuisine part of the claim believable. It sells food, ingredients and recipes.

Its signature dish is the Lambad Fish Roll, which Lambad says he devised in his youth by combining grilled fish he tasted in Mondstadt, Liyue and Inazuma with Sumeru's pitas.

Places: A ground-floor bar and dining room with an upstairs section. A noticeboard outside advertises a daily special and the line that a wonderful day starts with a drink.

People: Lambad runs it. By day the researcher Jafar sits here; by night come the Corps of Thirty mercenary Hakan, the Eremite mercenary Lemta and, upstairs, the researchers Khaldun and Yavanani, the international student Gregor and the boat captain Shams.

Quests: No quest is set mainly here; it appears in the background of Kaveh's history with Alhaitham.

Atmosphere: Warm and talkative, smelling of grilled fish and fresh bread, with Lambad ready to tell a sailing tale.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tavern is open as before; the pages consulted record no later change. Players who reach Reputation Rank 4 in Sumeru get a 10% discount there.

128.content:
Land of Grounded Dreams: The Land of Grounded Dreams is the deepest part of Old Vanarana in the Lost Nursery, in Sumeru. It is the battlefield where the last war against Marana ended and where the Traveler defeats Marana's Avatar in the Aranyaka.

It is unlocked in the quest For All Children Who Long for Life, the third part of Nursery of Lost Dreams. After Marana's Avatar falls, Arama plants themselves here and becomes the new Ashvattha Tree.

Geography: A cavern reached from the deepest part of Old Vanarana, after the earlier seal and nursery caves. It holds a small pool from which Marana's Avatar rises, and withering growths scattered around it.

People: Arama guides the Traveler here, saying the Withering has fully corroded the old place and that they can now resist Marana. Aramuhukunda, according to Arama, had turned into a Vasara Tree on this spot to suppress Marana's Avatar. Arakavi, Arapacati, Arapandu and Arana also appear in the quest.

History: Arama says this is where the last war ended: Marana's Avatar was crushed and imprisoned with four seals. The Vasara Tree Aramuhukunda became was meant to hold it down.

Quests: For All Children Who Long for Life: follow Arama, destroy the tumors of the Withering in turn, defeat Marana's Avatar and its final form, then play the Rhythm of the Great Dream. Co-op is disabled for it.

Dangers: Marana's Avatar and rifthounds, with Decay from the Withering.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the avatar is defeated and the new Ashvattha Tree grows from Arama; no later changes found.

129.comment: Land of Grounded Dreams: Marana's Avatar
129.content: Marana's Avatar is the body Marana took by corroding the Vasara Tree in the Land of Grounded Dreams. The Traveler and Arama destroy the spirit containers (tumors of the Withering) to damage it, and then defeat it so the new Ashvattha Tree can be born.

130.content:
Land of Lower Setekh: The Land of Lower Setekh is the part of Sumeru's Great Red Sand where most people of the desert live. Its centre is Aaru Village, the largest human settlement in the desert, home to the followers and descendants of King Deshret and to scholars exiled from the Akademiya. It also holds Khaj-Nisut, King Deshret's throne-room temple, Abdju Pit, the abandoned hospital Dar al-Shifa and the hidden base of the real Temple of Silence.

Setekh echoes the Egyptian god Set, associated with deserts and storms. The area's official viewpoints are titled The Barren Land Where Sand Dances and Verdant Fields' Vantage Point.

Geography: Dunes and oases south of the Wall of Samiel and Caravan Ribat, with Aaru Village at its heart. Abdju Pit is a deep sinkhole at the sands' edge, Khaj-Nisut lies in ruins hidden under the sand, and Thamud Oasis is where the city of Saleh once stood. The Temple of Silence's real base is an underground temple near Thamud Oasis.

Places: Aaru Village, around an old fortress. Khaj-Nisut, once called the Eye of the Sands, the King's throne-room temple. Abdju Pit. Dar al-Shifa, a ruined hospital for Eleazar patients. The Temple of Silence, an underground temple. Thamud Oasis.

People: Aaru Village's people are followers and descendants of King Deshret together with exiled Akademiya scholars. Candace, whose companion story supplies one account of the village's origins, is associated with it; the Eremites, the Temple of Silence's members (including Cyno and, as its appointed leader, Sethos) and Kshahrewar Village Keepers all appear here.

Governance: Aaru's founders swore off the rule of kings, and the old fortress now serves as the Village Chief's House. The Temple of Silence, which still exists as an independent body here, has begun re-establishing relations with the Akademiya after the events of Oathkeeper.

Culture: The founders named the village Aaru after the "ancient dream of the gods" and preserve the embers of Deshret's civilisation while awaiting the return of Al-Ahmar.

History: After King Deshret's death his civilisation broke into warring city-states, and refugees eventually left the desert to build Aaru. The founders were led by a blind poet of Tulaytullah. Candace's account is that the earliest inhabitants were survivors of the city of Akhtamun.

Dangers: Sandstorms, ancient guardian constructs in the pit and temple, Eremite groups, the Fatui, and monsters such as spinocrocodiles and red vultures in the oases.

Travel: The route from the rainforest passes Caravan Ribat and the Wall of Samiel, then crosses the dunes to Aaru Village. Aaru Village is the base for expeditions elsewhere in the Great Red Sand.

Quests: Golden Slumber (3.1): Lost in the Sands, An Introduction to Indoor Archaeology, The Secret of Al-Ahmar and Dreams Beneath the Searing Sand. Also in this area: Cry From the Eleazar Hospital, Desert Bloom, Dual Evidence, Hidden Mercenaries, Sage of Sages, The Exile (Sprouting and Blooming), A Gifted Rose series, Warehousing Business and others (titles only).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Aaru Village and the surrounding ruins are open, and the Temple of Silence is again cooperating with the Akademiya.

Nothing from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes the area.

131.comment: Land of Lower Setekh: Aaru Village
131.content: The largest human settlement in the desert, home to followers and descendants of King Deshret and exiled Akademiya scholars. It is built around a Gurabad-era border fort and gets its water from a stepwell.

132.comment: Land of Lower Setekh: Dar al-Shifa
132.content: A now-abandoned hospital that specialised in treating Eleazar. Old notes suggest one doctor used patients as test subjects for dangerous treatments.

133.comment: Land of Lower Setekh: Temple of Silence base
133.content: An organisation keeping knowledge from King Deshret's era. The Akademiya office of that name is a remnant; the real Temple operates underground near Thamud Oasis.

134.content:
Land of Upper Setekh: The Land of Upper Setekh is a desert region in Sumeru's Great Red Sand, named because it lies in the direction of the sun at noon. Its landmark is the Valley of Dahri, where a giant Khaenri'ahn Ruin Golem sits among Akademiya research notes, and it also holds Lamb-Devourer Rock, the secret base of the Eremite tribe Thutmose.

"Setekh" is the Egyptian name of the god Set, associated with deserts, storms, disorder and foreigners. The region's world-quest series is thin: the only quest under its category is Afratu's Dilemma.

Geography: A rocky desert area with its own Statue of the Seven. A cavern north of the statue and a spot northeast of it hold parts of the Ruin Golem, with Akademiya reports left on them. The Valley of Dahri is a wind-eroded valley, and its viewpoint is titled The Giant of the Wind-Eroded Valley.

Places: The Valley of Dahri, with its Ruin Golem. Lamb-Devourer Rock, a Thutmose hideout reached in Hidden Mercenaries. The area's Statue of the Seven stands beside the cavern with the Ruin Golem's parts.

People: Eremites of the Thutmose tribe hide at Lamb-Devourer Rock; a character named Afratu appears in the world quest, and its first step is to talk to a researcher. Hilichurls (called Majuj by desert people) roam the valley.

History: Akademiya reports found at the Ruin Golem record the team studying the machine, medical reports on the Majuj and on Eleazar sufferers, and an order from the Temple of Silence that all machines from Khaenri'ah be sealed in the format of the Revelatory Monument. Suda's Flow is the sages' name for a perturbation of elemental veins used as a seal.

Dangers: Ruin Guards, Mitachurls, fungi, the golem itself in the quest, and Eremite hideouts. Desert exposure is the general risk.

Travel: The region is part of the Great Red Sand and is reached overland from its other lands; the Statue of the Seven is the local waypoint.

Quests: Afratu's Dilemma (3.1) starts at the Valley of Dahri: the Traveler helps a researcher enter the Ruin Golem and breaks the Suda's Flow seals. Hidden Mercenaries (part of Old Notes and New Friends) leads to Lamb-Devourer Rock, where the Traveler enters Thutmose's base, finds valuables and hands slates to Soheil.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the region is an open desert area with its Ruin Golem still immobile.

Nothing from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes it.

135.comment: Land of Upper Setekh: Valley of Dahri
135.content: A wind-eroded valley with a giant Ruin Golem. Akademiya investigators left reports on the machine, medical notes on the Majuj and on Eleazar sufferers, and a hidden note from Zandik about the Khaenri'ahn machine and elemental flows.

136.comment: Land of Upper Setekh: Lamb-Devourer Rock
136.content: The secret base of the Eremite tribe Thutmose, found during the world quest Hidden Mercenaries.

137.content:
Liloupar's Cell (also: Liloupar's Gaol, Jinni's prison): Liloupar's Cell is a ruined prison in Safhe Shatranj, in the Desert of Hadramaveth, where the most dominant fragment of the Jinni Liloupar was kept. Its viewpoint calls it a prison that has become an oasis: a green spot with a big tree and a river. In The Temple Where Sand Flows Like Tears the Traveler and Jeht find a bottle here, and when it is touched the plants wither and Liloupar's voice speaks from it.

Liloupar is the Jinni who destroyed Gurabad in revenge across three generations. King Deshret split her into seven fragments and had divine sages hide them in the Great Red Sand; this cell held the strongest one.

Geography: A small ruin opposite the square of the Gurabad temple, in the canyon the Tanit call the Great Rift. Before the bottle is touched it is a lush spot with a big tree beside a river. A viewpoint here is named Liloupar's Gaol. Afterward its look changes and the oasis is withered.

People: Liloupar speaks from the bottle as the Mother of the Jinn, a title she mocks. She is proud, theatrical and sharp-tongued, and calls Jeht a sand-licking lackey before warming to her.
