Geography: Sumeru borders Liyue to the east (the Dharma Forest is reached directly from The Chasm), Natlan lies beyond the western edge of its desert, and the far desert lies on the road toward Fontaine. The ruins of Khaenri'ah lie directly beneath it. It has three subregions: the Dharma Forest, the rainforest of the north and east where Sumeru City stands; the Great Red Sand (also called the Deshret Desert), King Deshret's old realm; and the remote Girdle of the Sands beyond it.

Government: The Dendro Archon is head of state, but the Sumeru Akademiya runs daily affairs. It has six Darshans (schools), each led by a Sage; one of them is also Grand Sage. The current Grand Sage is Naphis (Amurta), Tighnari's old teacher, who is famous for his temper and integrity. The other sages are Baladhuri (Vahumana), Alkindi (Spantamad), Firnas (Kshahrewar), Shakir (Rtawahist) and Rushd (Haravatat). The Matra, led by General Mahamatra Cyno, punish academic crimes.

Religion: Sumeru reveres the Dendro Archon as the God of Wisdom. Under the old sages she was a distant, little-respected figure locked away in the Sanctuary of Surasthana; only a few devotees such as Dunyarzad and Nilou honoured her. Many desert people instead revered the ancient King Deshret, sometimes called Al-Ahmar, and some Eremite groups still await his return. Since Chapter III the Akademiya and the people openly honour Nahida, and the Sabzeruz Festival marks her birthday.

History: Sumeru was shaped by three god-kings, the Dendro Archon of the forest, King Deshret of the desert and Nabu Malikata, the Goddess of Flowers. After Nabu Malikata died, Deshret turned to forbidden knowledge and brought madness, scales and the Withering onto his land. He died ending the catastrophe, and his civilisation broke apart into rival city-states. In the cataclysm 500 years ago, forbidden knowledge contaminated Irminsul, and Lesser Lord Kusanali was born as the new Dendro Archon. The sages confined her for five centuries. In Chapter III they also tried to build an artificial god with the Fatui Harbinger Dottore, but the Traveler and Nahida's allies defeated the plot.

Customs: Learning shapes daily life: seniority depends on academic progress rather than age, and thesis defences are notoriously gruelling. Before Chapter III, Sumeru adults famously did not dream, which the sages praised as rational, and art was seen as useless. People dream again now and the arts are recovering, though talking about art still kills a conversation. The great festivals are the Sabzeruz Festival and the Akademiya Extravaganza.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Sumeru is at peace and rebuilding after the Irminsul crisis of 6.6. Nahida has recovered and governs openly with Grand Sage Naphis and the Akademiya. Irminsul has been burned away, and Aaru now stores the world's records in its place. The Archon Quest has moved on to Snezhnaya (Chapter VII). At the end of 7.1 Sumeru's Celestial Nail began, like every other Nail, to cast a strange light into the sky.

Dottore is dead. The Fatui still hold the Electro and Dendro Gnoses. The Pyro Gnosis disappeared in the fire. Thoth and Heryshaf of the Seven Pillars are staying at the Temple of Silence. Collei is now a full Forest Ranger and has been freed of her god remains. Alhaitham and Kaveh have repaired their damaged home. After the Nails began to glow in 7.1, Candace, Dehya and Dehya's mercenaries camped near Mt. Damavand in the Desert of Hadramaveth to keep watch.

210.comment: Sumeru: Sumeru City and the Divine Tree
210.content: Sumeru City, the "City of Wisdom", is built up the trunk and branches of the Divine Tree in Avidya Forest. The docks are at the bottom. The lower and middle tiers hold the Grand Bazaar with the Zubayr Theater, Treasures Street, Lambad's Tavern and the Bimarstan. Higher up is the Akademiya campus with its library, the House of Daena. The Sanctuary of Surasthana, Nahida's treetop palace, sits at the very top. The Corps of Thirty is based at the Citadel of Regzar.

211.comment: Sumeru: The Rainforest and the Aranara
211.content: The Dharma Forest is a damp, layered rainforest of giant trees, mushrooms and rivers. Its areas are Avidya Forest (Sumeru City, Gandharva Ville), Lokapala Jungle (Bayda Harbor, Mawtiyima Forest, Chatrakam Cave), Ardravi Valley (Port Ormos, Vimara Village, Devantaka Mountain), Ashavan Realm (Caravan Ribat, Pardis Dhyai, Apam Woods), Vissudha Field, Vanarana and the Lost Nursery. The Forest Rangers (Vanara) work out of Gandharva Ville, where Tighnari is Forest Watcher. Pardis Dhyai is Amurta's botanical research station. The Aranara are shy, plantlike forest spirits who love memories and songs and can shape dreams. They live in hidden Vanarana and are usually seen only by children. They feared adult humans ("Nara") after the cataclysm took away people's dreams.

212.comment: Sumeru: The Desert and King Deshret
212.content: The Great Red Sand was King Deshret's realm. Its areas are the Hypostyle Desert, the Lands of Upper and Lower Setekh (Valley of Dahri, Aaru Village, Khaj-Nisut) and the Desert of Hadramaveth. His giant pyramid, the Mausoleum of King Deshret, rises over the Hypostyle Desert, and the ruins of Khaj-Nisut lie in the Land of Lower Setekh. He ruled through his Seven Pillars and the Jinn, defeated many gods, and with Nabu Malikata's illicit celestial help began building Aaru, an artificial afterlife. After her death he succumbed to forbidden knowledge. The Dendro Archon helped contain the disaster and was shrunk to a child's size by the effort, and Deshret gave his life to end it. Ay-Khanoum, the City of Amphitheaters the three god-kings built together, lies in ruins, and later ruined cities like Gurabad and Tulaytullah record centuries of vassal kings, betrayals and wars.

213.comment: Sumeru: The Sumeru Akademiya and the Six Darshans
213.content: The Akademiya is thousands of years old and takes students from all over Teyvat. Its Six Darshans each have a specialty and a uniform colour: Amurta studies biology (green), Rtawahist illuminationism (blue), Spantamad elementalism (red), Haravatat semiotics (black), Vahumana aetiology (yellow) and Kshahrewar technology (white). Their Sages form the governing council, and one of them serves as Grand Sage. Former members include Lisa, Signora and Dottore. Students rise from Driyosh (travelling scholars) to Dastur (two accepted theses) and Herbad, and graduating after thirty is common.

214.content: The Akasha was a mind-linking network, worn as a leaf-shaped Akasha Terminal over the left ear, that gave users knowledge according to their clearance. It ran on the Dendro Gnosis and was secretly powered by its users' harvested dreams. The sages used it to monitor people, predict their movements and spread propaganda. Nahida, the "First Akasha Terminal", shut it down after Chapter III and gave her Dendro Gnosis to Dottore.

215.comment: Sumeru: The Sages' Conspiracy and the Sabzeruz Samsara
215.content: In Chapter III, Grand Sage Azar and three other sages, disappointed in their "childish" god, joined Dottore to make a new God of Wisdom from the puppet Scaramouche, using the Electro Gnosis. They imprisoned the sages Naphis and Baladhuri, who objected. They also trapped Sumeru in a repeating dream of the Sabzeruz Festival to harvest people's minds through the Akasha, and gathered "divine knowledge" from maddened scholars. The Traveler, Nahida, Nilou, Dehya, Alhaitham, Cyno, Tighnari and the desert fighters of Rahman and Candace's village broke the loop and freed Nahida on Jnagarbha Day. Then Nahida and the Traveler defeated Scaramouche's mech, Shouki no Kami.

216.content: In the cataclysm the first Dendro Archon, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, stayed behind to guard Irminsul and was contaminated with it by forbidden knowledge. Because she could not erase herself, she made Lesser Lord Kusanali from the purest branch of Irminsul to be her reincarnation. In Chapter III Act V her lingering consciousness asked to be removed, and Nahida purged her from Irminsul. The contamination cleared, the people of Sumeru could dream again and Eleazar vanished, but every memory of Rukkhadevata disappeared. The Traveler, who is not recorded in Irminsul, is the only one who remembers her.

217.content: "Eremites" is a blanket name for the desert's many clans and mercenary bands, which are proud, quarrelsome and often hired out across Teyvat. They are Sumeru's only authorised mercenaries. Some draw elemental power from ancient desert spirits bound in their weapons. The Corps of Thirty, with green scarves instead of the usual red, polices Sumeru City. Other bands range from Dehya's Blazing Beasts to Deshret zealots such as Ayn Al-Ahmar.

218.content: The Withering is a blight born of forbidden knowledge that drains land and life and turns forest into desert. The Aranara call it Marana. Its human form, Eleazar, slowly covers victims in dark scales and was once incurable. When Rukkhadevata was purged from Irminsul, the Withering stopped spreading and Eleazar was cured, but existing Withering Zones remain dangerous and the Forest Rangers still clear them.

219.content:
Sumeru City (also: City of Wisdom, Sumeru Akademiya city): Sumeru City is the capital of Sumeru and is known across Teyvat as the "City of Wisdom". It is built on the Divine Tree, a colossal tree in Avidya Forest, and falls under the Sumeru Akademiya, the nation's great school and government. Ordinary life, markets and taverns sit near the foot of the tree, the Akademiya occupies its middle, and at the very top rests the Sanctuary of Surasthana, the palace of the Dendro Archon Lesser Lord Kusanali (Nahida).

Height in the city doubles as social rank: the lower levels are for the common folk, and promotion or higher study is spoken of as "moving up". It is where the central events of Sumeru's Archon Quests unfolded: the Akademiya's god-making plot and, much later, the Irminsul crisis.

Geography: The city is built on the Divine Tree, which carries the Akademiya and everything below it. The Grand Bazaar and everyday buildings stand at the base, the Akademiya in the middle, the Sanctuary of Surasthana at the top. The city lies in Avidya Forest, within Dharma Forest, and a river runs from it to Port Ormos.

Places: Grand Bazaar: a lively, artistic market, home to the Zubayr Theater (Nilou's troupe). Treasures Street: the liveliest street, with the Puspa Cafe, the Adventurers' Guild branch and the Citadel of Regzar of the Corps of Thirty. The Akademiya: the main building of the Sumeru Akademiya, with the House of Daena library at its heart. Sanctuary of Surasthana: the palace at the top. Lambad's Tavern: Sumeru's main restaurant, run by Lambad. Bimarstan: the city's medical institution.

People: Residents include Akademiya students and researchers, the Matra under General Mahamatra Cyno, Corps of Thirty mercenaries, merchants, farmers, dockworkers and performers. Nahida lives at the Sanctuary, and Naphis leads the Akademiya as Grand Sage as of 7.1. Kaveh (an architect), Alhaitham (a scribe) and Nilou (a dancer at the Zubayr Theater) live and work in the city; the Forest Rangers Tighnari and Collei visit often.

Governance: The Akademiya runs the city and nation day to day. Six Darshans (schools: Haravatat, Vahumana, Kshahrewar, Amurta, Rtawahist and Spantamad) are each led by a sage, and the Grand Sage leads them all. The Matra enforce order. Its rules rest on three virtues (Admonition, Ingenuity, Praxis) and six banned fields of research; breaking them can bring expulsion or imprisonment.

Culture: Learning is the city's pride and its pressure: a degree is notoriously long and stressful to earn, and theses are the hardest hurdle. Under the old sages the arts were marginalised; once Nahida took her place, performance, books and music returned.

History: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's rainforest civilisation built the city on the Divine Tree. Five hundred years ago forbidden knowledge corrupted Irminsul and Rukkhadevata, and Lesser Lord Kusanali, her successor, was kept by the sages in the Sanctuary. In Chapter III the sages and the Fatui Harbinger Dottore built an artificial god; Nahida was freed and Rukkhadevata was erased from Irminsul at her own request.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Sumeru City is inhabited again after the evacuation of the Irminsul crisis (6.6). Nahida lives in the Sanctuary of Surasthana, free; Naphis leads the Akademiya as Grand Sage.

Irminsul no longer exists in its old form: it was burned and its storage function was taken over by the reconfigured Aaru, with no lasting damage reported. Dottore died in the burning. The Pyro Gnosis that Nahida used then disappeared without trace. A letter from Pulcinella of the Fatui apologised for the trouble Dottore caused and said relief supplies had been sent; Nahida and Naphis agreed to keep watch on what Snezhnaya does. No later crisis in the city is shown through 7.1.

220.content: The Divine Tree is the tree on which Sumeru City is built; it holds up the Akademiya. A student named Yasmin jokes that its years exceed all the rice grains in all the pilaf of Port Ormos. Amurta students record the condition of its roots as a preventative measure. The bottom is the common area with the Grand Bazaar, the middle the Akademiya, and the top the Sanctuary of Surasthana.

221.content: The treetop palace above the Akademiya is the home of the Dendro Archon, Lesser Lord Kusanali. For about five hundred years it was also her prison, as the sages kept her confined within; no one but the sages saw her for centuries. A map description updated after the Archon Quest says that for centuries the light of wisdom shone out from here to illuminate Sumeru. Surasthana is Sanskrit-derived and can mean a temple or residence of a god.

222.comment: Sumeru City: The Akademiya and House of Daena
222.content: The Akademiya is the main building of the Sumeru Akademiya, built into the Divine Tree; its library, the House of Daena, lies at its heart, and the Grand Sage's office is above it. Students and researchers of every Darshan study here, and the Matra keep order.

223.comment: Sumeru City: Grand Bazaar and Zubayr Theater
223.content: The Grand Bazaar is the lively, artistic heart of everyday Sumeru City, with three entrances and many stalls of handmade goods. The Zubayr Theater, within it, is managed by Sheikh Zubayr and associated with Nilou's troupe.

224.comment: Sumeru City: Treasures Street and Puspa Cafe
224.content: Treasures Street is the liveliest street in Sumeru City. It holds the Puspa Cafe, shops, the local Adventurers' Guild branch (Branch Master Kamal, receptionist Katheryne) and the Citadel of Regzar, where the Corps of Thirty are based under their Parchamdar, Rukh Shah. Padisarah can be gathered there.

225.content: Sumeru's main restaurant, near Treasures Street. Its owner, Lambad, claims to be a legendary sailor who sailed far and wide; it is hard to tell how much he exaggerates, but the food at least supports the claim to know many cuisines. Kaveh redesigned the booth seating on the second floor as thanks to Lambad, who gave him a seat and free drinks when he was nearly penniless; he spent over a fortnight drinking there. The Traveler and Paimon ate there after the Irminsul crisis.

226.content:
Tanit Camps (also: Tanit Camp, Tanit Encampment, Tanit Tribe camp): The Tanit Camps are the tent settlement of the Tanit, an old Eremite tribe, on the southern border of the Desert of Hadramaveth in Sumeru. They were the home of Matriarch Babel and, for a time, of Jeht, the Traveler's friend. After the events of the world quest series Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters..., the camps are empty: the tribe is gone and the Vahumana Dastur Tanjiyy is the only person living there.

The camps are the Tanit's most recent settlement. The tribe prized words and learning but refused to trust the Akasha, so its tents hold many books that were smuggled out of the Akademiya's library. Visitors who arrive after the tribe's fall find ash, abandoned tents and supplies still in place.

Geography: The camps lie in the Great Red Sand, on the southern border of the Desert of Hadramaveth. They are a cluster of tents around the Matriarch's tent, with water on the western side and a bridge leading to further tents to the north. Wadi Al-Majuj, where the final quest of the Her Foes series begins, is nearby.

People: While the tribe lived here, the NPCs at the camp were the Matriarch Babel, Jeht (with her companion Benben), the mercenary guards Mendas and Hugeweh, the farmer Yuften, the tent-holders Aderfi and Masseira, and the Falcon Tadhla. After Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters... only Tanjiyy, a Vahumana Dastur from the Akademiya, remains. He came to give educational assistance to the Tanit under a deal that Setaria had made and found the camp deserted.

Culture: The Tanit are matrilineal and revere the Goddess of Flowers. They value words and knowledge but distrust the Akasha, so they educate themselves on long walks across the desert and with books smuggled out of the Akademiya. They trade crocodile products, spices and essential oils to Sumeru's markets and hunt Wenut for spices.

History: The Tanit are said to be the oldest tribe of the Desert of Hadramaveth, with many branches, and the camps are their latest settlement. The camps entered the story in Version 3.4 with The Dirge of Bilqis, in which Jeht brought the Traveler and Paimon to meet Babel. Babel secretly meant to seize the Eternal Oasis and its Jinni, Liloupar, and, after the Traveler and Jeht discovered the Orchard of Pairidaeza, ordered the Traveler killed. When the Traveler worked out the truth and told Jeht, Jeht turned on the tribe; the confrontation at the camp left Babel dead and the tribe destroyed.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the camp is abandoned. Babel is dead and the Tanit are gone; only the Vahumana Dastur Tanjiyy stays, studying what happened.

Jeht left with Benben and no longer belongs to the tribe. No later story, including Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya, returns to the camps.

227.comment: Tanit Camps: The Fall of the Tanit
227.content: Babel's betrayal is the tribe's last chapter: she tried to turn the Traveler's friendship with Jeht into a weapon, then ordered the Traveler's death to control the Jinni Liloupar. Jeht refused, killed Babel, and the tribe fell. Babel had already sent members to warn the other tribes of Jeht's supposed treachery.

228.comment: Tanit Camps: Tanjiyy at the Camps
228.content: Tanjiyy, a Vahumana Dastur, came to the camps for educational assistance and found them deserted. He is friendly, treats the Tanit's fate as history worth reconstructing, and offers the Traveler a card game with decks he found in the tents. He does not know the real cause of the tribe's fall.

229.content:
Temir Mountains: The Temir Mountains are a range in Gavireh Lajavard, in Sumeru's Girdle of the Sands. They are the main passage between the Desert of Hadramaveth and the rest of the Girdle. Legend says the range was formed from molten metal, and the desert folk treat it as the border of the red desert.

The wiki lists the mountains as the base of the Order of Skeptics, the scholars who split from the Akademiya and made friends with the Pari. They were added in version 3.6.

Geography: A mountain belt that serves as the primary passage between the Desert of Hadramaveth and the rest of the Girdle of the Sands.

History: Trishiraite's description recalls the old Sumeru legend of Dahri, an underground kingdom said to have fallen to the dark disaster of the cataclysm after straying from the true path. Mourning Flowers are said to bloom on ancient battlefields, watered by the blood of heroes who died in that war.

Dangers: Fatui camps, marked by Sosi in Monumental Study, and the wider hazards of Gavireh Lajavard, whose boss is the Iniquitous Baptist.

Quests: "Monumental Study" (3.6) starts here once the first step of "As the Khvarena's Light Shows" is done, and Fravashi Tree quests in the western mountains let the Traveler wake residual Pari. Both belong to the Girdle of the Sands and Khvarena of Good and Evil content.

Atmosphere: A border range at the edge of the red desert, known in legend as molten metal turned to stone.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing is recorded as changing here beyond the events of the 3.6 quests.

230.comment: Temir Mountains: Temir Mountains in Desert Lore
230.content: Loading screens call it a legendary mountain range said to be formed from molten metal, which desert folk regard as the border of the red desert. A Skeptic note on controlling mountain passes shows how important the road is.

231.content:
Temple of Silence (also: Temple of Silence base): The Temple of Silence is the underground base of the organisation of the same name, in the Land of Lower Setekh near Thamud Oasis. Its map description says it keeps silent vigil over all that is ancient. It guards knowledge that survives from the age of King Deshret, and it is now led by Sethos, with Cyno as its de jure leader.

Players unlock it in Cyno's story quest Oathkeeper, in the part "Footprints Sunken Beneath the Sands", after which its entrance reveals itself when approached. It has a square and an inner temple; the Akademiya's office of the same name is only a front.

Places: An entrance leads into a square and then, through an inner door, the temple itself. Inside are a great hall, a ceremonial hall, an east hall, the room of its former head Bamoun, a statue of Hermanubis and a mural of the Bennu.

People: Members shown here include Asenath, Betresa, Charmian, Djer, Intef and Khensa. Sethos leads it; Bamoun, its former head, has died.

Governance: Tradition says the Temple follows the person who holds the most Ba Fragments (pieces of Hermanubis' spirit). After the duel in Oathkeeper Cyno held both, so he is formally leader, but as General Mahamatra he handed the running of the Temple to Sethos, who pledged to open its knowledge to those he and Lesser Lord Kusanali judge worthy.

History: Hermanubis and his followers founded the Temple after King Deshret's death and settled in Tulaytullah as keepers of Deshret's surviving knowledge. When the king of Gurabad besieged the city and Tulaytullah's rulers betrayed the Temple, Hermanubis shattered his spirit into Ba Fragments and gave them to his followers, who drove the army off but were then shunned. They left for the rainforest, and about 400 years ago they raised a large underground temple near Thamud Oasis.

Atmosphere: Silent, ancient and solemn, a hushed underground sanctuary of statues, murals and guarded halls.

Dangers: The Temple's trials are fought against guardians (Grounded Geoshrooms and Hydroshrooms, and Primal Construct Reshapers) during the duel with Sethos.

Quests: Oathkeeper (Lupus Aureus Chapter Act II): The Mysterious Letter, After Repose, Footprints Sunken Beneath the Sands, Sage of Sages, The Dead Past is the Living Present. These are a major spoiler for Cyno and Sethos.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Temple is active under Sethos and is rebuilding ties with the Akademiya.

232.content:
Thamud Oasis: Thamud Oasis is an oasis in the Land of Lower Setekh in Sumeru's Great Red Sand. It is where Saleh, the Electrum City of Warriors, once stood. Its Viewpoint text calls oases like it gems adorning the sea of sand.

Saleh was home to the golden-eyed Thamudians and was known for seven walls. The kingdom was short-lived, was drawn into the wars between desert kingdoms and was destroyed; today there is little sign of it. The oasis still gives caravans and wanderers springs and plants.

Geography: A green oasis of springs and plants amid the sand of Lower Setekh. Exploration objects here include Dendroculi, Dendrogranum puzzles and a Four-Leaf Sigil.

History: Saleh existed from the time of King Deshret's civilisation and became known as one of the Cities of the Seven Towers. By Parvezravan's reign inscriptions record it paying annual tribute to Gurabad as King Deshret's primary vassal kingdom.

Dangers: Hilichurls of several kinds, a Wooden Shieldwall Mitachurl, fungi and Winged Dendroshrooms, and desert wildlife such as Desert Sumpter Beasts, Red Vultures and Spinocrocodiles.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is a quiet oasis with no city; Saleh survives only in texts and inscriptions.

233.comment: Thamud Oasis: Saleh, the Electrum City of Warriors
233.content: Saleh was an ancient city-state around Thamud Oasis, home to the golden-eyed Thamudians, with seven walls. It paid tribute to Gurabad under Parvezravan and later fell amid the wars of the desert kingdoms.

234.content:
The Akademiya (also: Akademiya building, Akademiya headquarters): The Akademiya is the main building of the Sumeru Akademiya, the prestigious institute of learning and governing body of Sumeru. It is built into the middle of the Divine Tree that carries Sumeru City, above the Grand Bazaar and below the Sanctuary of Surasthana, and holds the House of Daena library at its heart. Scholars, students and officials of the Six Darshans work here. For centuries it was ruled by six sages whose control of knowledge, through the Akasha System, went far beyond teaching.

Under the sages the Akademiya regulated information and secretly collaborated with the Fatui to create a false god. After the plan was stopped in Chapter III Act V (3.2), four of the six sages were removed.

Geography: The Akademiya sits in the middle of the Divine Tree, between the Grand Bazaar and ordinary buildings at the bottom and the Sanctuary of Surasthana at the very top. Its doors open on their own as visitors approach. Inside, paths lead up the tree through places such as Razan Garden, and the House of Daena stands at the centre.

Places: House of Daena: the largest library in Teyvat, described on the map as once the bank of all the world's knowledge, now overshadowed by the Akasha System but still a symbol of Sumeru. Razan Garden: a serene garden up the tree with gazebos and Padisarah, entered from the Akademiya's doors; its name is Persian for "vines" and the Chinese name means a quiet garden.

People: The Six Great Sages head the Akademiya, one for each Darshan, and one of them is the Grand Sage. The Mahamata are civil administrators and the Matra enforce discipline.

Governance: Sumeru's day-to-day affairs are run from the Akademiya. It is divided into six Darshans, each led by a sage, and the Grand Sage is the central leader among them. Its rules rest on three virtues and six sins.

Culture: The Akademiya admits students who pass its entrance exams, children included at schooling age. Degrees are famously long and stressful, with the thesis defence the hardest hurdle.

History: The Akademiya was founded by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata with its first Darshans, and was already prestigious by the cataclysm five hundred years ago. After her death, the sages, disappointed with the new god Kusanali's lack of obvious wisdom, locked her in the Sanctuary of Surasthana, took control of the Akasha System, and ran the nation themselves.

Atmosphere: A scholarly place where wisdom is also pressure: students in the colours of different Darshans pass by, researchers worry about theses, and mercenaries of the Corps of Thirty keep order. Under the sages it was watchful and controlling over information; after Chapter III it is a looser, less certain institution.

Dangers: The risks are social and informational: the Matra punish forbidden research and Canned Knowledge, the Akasha once shaped what people were allowed to know, and entry to certain places, such as the Sanctuary, was restricted.

Travel: The Akademiya is reached by climbing the Divine Tree from the Grand Bazaar. Doors lead up to Razan Garden and on to the Sanctuary of Surasthana.

Quests: Chapter III of the Archon Quests: Dreams, Emptiness, Deception (3.1) and Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises (3.2), especially Jnagarbha Day.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Akademiya continues as Sumeru's centre of learning and administration under reformed leadership. The sages who planned the false god were removed after 3.2; Naphis is Grand Sage, with Baladhuri, Alkindi, Firnas, Shakir and Rushd as the other sages (as shown in 6.6). Nahida halted the Akasha after Chapter III; during the 6.6 Irminsul crisis it was briefly restarted so the allies could overload Irminsul, and it is not shown back in everyday use. The sages' history of controlling information still shapes habits.

235.content: The largest library in Teyvat, at the heart of the Akademiya. Run by a Grand Conservator who procures and maintains the collection; the previous holder retired, and Rifaet and Vikram were the candidates. Shatir calls Lisa "Mondstadt's Grand Conservator" and says she would have been his first choice had she stayed. Daena is a Zoroastrian term for insight and revelation.

236.content: A calm garden on the path up the Divine Tree, reached by the Akademiya's left or right doors, with gazebos and Padisarah. Researchers and students such as Darya, Farghani, Homayun, Makhfi, Muganna, Qushji, Arina and Armin are found here. The Akademiya Public Message Board stands in the garden.

237.comment: The Akademiya: Grand Sage's office and the confinement room
237.content: Above the House of Daena sits the Grand Sage's office, with the Grand Sage's console, through which restricted commands are executed; on Jnagarbha Day the sages load research and decrees into Knowledge Capsules for entry into the Akasha. Below it is the confinement room, a sealed chamber close to the Sanctuary where Azar jails the Traveler. From there the Traveler wakes Nahida's consciousness with a modified Akasha Terminal.

238.content: Amurta (biology, green) is the Darshan of Tighnari and Naphis and runs the Bimarstan and Pardis Dhyai. Rtawahist (illuminationism, blue) was Azar's. Spantamad (elementalism, red) was Cyno's and Cyrus's. Haravatat (semiotics, black) was Khajeh's. Vahumana (aetiology, yellow) is Baladhuri's. Kshahrewar (technology, white) is Firnas's per the wiki. The Chinese names give each a descriptive name and a phonetic name; the English uses the phonetic ones.

239.comment: The Akademiya: Virtues and sins of the Akademiya
239.content: The three virtues are Admonition, Ingenuity and Praxis; the six sins are listed in the governance section. They form the basis of the Akademiya's rules, to which the sages have added new rules and amendments ever since. Researching sinful topics can result in expulsion or imprisonment.

240.comment: The Akademiya: The sages' false god scheme
240.content: Four of the six sages, led by Grand Sage Azar, agreed with Il Dottore to build a replacement god. They harvested divine knowledge from crazed scholars at a secret facility, used the Akasha to run a dream samsara, and spread false claims of King Deshret's return. Naphis and Baladhuri opposed and were locked up. Scaramouche, delivered by Dottore, was modified as the vessel.

241.comment: The Akademiya: The Akademiya after Chapter III
241.content: After the victory Azar and the three sages who joined him were removed, Naphis and Baladhuri were released and four new sages were to be chosen under Nahida's supervision. Alhaitham was offered Grand Sage, refused and served as Acting Grand Sage before resigning to return as Scribe, leaving the Akademiya briefly without a clear leader. By the 6.6 Archon Quest (A Divergence Leading to Oneself) Naphis is Grand Sage and introduces the new sages Alkindi (Spantamad), Firnas (Kshahrewar), Shakir (Rtawahist) and Rushd (Haravatat), alongside Baladhuri (Vahumana); when he was appointed is not shown.

242.content:
The Dune of Carouses (also: Dune of Carouses): The Dune of Carouses is a dune in the Hypostyle Desert of Sumeru's Great Red Sand. It is home to the Tomb of Carouses, a cone-shaped ruin that Soheil, an Akademiya researcher in Aaru Village, calls "a miniature version of the Mausoleum of King Deshret".

The tomb is the setting of the 3.1 world quest "Desert's Remembrance", part of "Soheil's Wish" in the quest chain "Old Notes and New Friends".

Geography: A dune area with the Tomb of Carouses, a pyramid-like ruin that echoes the shape of the Mausoleum of King Deshret on a smaller scale. Soheil found the same mysterious barrier keeping him out here as at his earlier ruins.

History: Soheil's notes (days 32 to 46 of a youthful expedition) recall the day he reached the dune: "We have arrived at The Dune of Carouses." He named the cone-shaped ruin the Tomb of Carouses "for now", found it much smaller than the Mausoleum and tried to imagine how Deshret enslaved his people to build such a structure, and was turned away by the same mysterious power that blocked him elsewhere.

People: Soheil Usaibia, an Akademiya researcher found in Aaru Village, sends the Traveler on his behalf; he says he and Hulwani must patrol the area each day because young researchers keep trying to worm their way into the desert. The Eremites of Thutmose are fanatics of Deshret who once attacked his team.

Dangers: Hilichurls of several kinds (including Dendro Samachurls and shield and shooter variants), Stretchy Geo Fungi, and, inside the tomb, Primal Construct Reshapers and floating Hydro and Anemo fungi.

Atmosphere: A dune of the red desert with a small cone-shaped tomb that once turned scholars away at a barrier.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tomb can be entered and its slate can be given to Soheil for study; nothing else is recorded as changing.

243.comment: The Dune of Carouses: Tomb of Carouses
243.content: A cone-shaped ruin on the Dune of Carouses, a smaller echo of the Mausoleum of King Deshret. Soheil named it. A hidden barrier once kept explorers out. Inside are Primal mechanisms and a stone slate recording its history (the Record of the Tomb of Carouses).

244.comment: The Dune of Carouses: Garden of Endless Pillars
244.content: A one-time Dendro domain west of the dune, in the Hypostyle Desert. It is the surviving garden of the "city of sapphire" Tulaytullah, once dominated by thousands of giant pillars. The white tree and ley lines preserved it after the fall of the desert kingdom, and it is now a home for fungi.

245.content:
The Dune of Elusion: The Dune of Elusion is a subarea of the Hypostyle Desert in Sumeru, one of the ruins of King Deshret's civilisation. It contains the boss Algorithm of Semi-Intransient Matrix of Overseer Network.

Exploration here includes a Mysterious Mural and a Four-Leaf Sigil. The ruins south of the dune are one of the places where Primal Constructs must be defeated for the hidden exploration objective The Dead End and the Glinting Architects, which requires the quest Dual Evidence.

Geography: A desert hill with ruined structures belonging to the vanished civilisation of King Deshret, in the Hypostyle Desert of the Great Red Sand. The southernmost ruins of the Hypostyle Desert lie south of the dune.

Dangers: The Algorithm of Semi-Intransient Matrix of Overseer Network, a boss, guards the site; ruin machines called Primal Constructs are found in the ruins to its south.

Quests: The Dead End and the Glinting Architects (an unofficial wiki name for a hidden exploration objective, available after Dual Evidence).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is an explorable ruin, with nothing in the sources about later changes.

246.comment: The Dune of Elusion: Algorithm of Semi-Intransient Matrix of Overseer Network
246.content: This boss, a construct of the ancient desert civilisation, is found at The Dune of Elusion. See its own entry for its nature.

247.content:
The Dune of Magma: The Dune of Magma is a subarea of the Hypostyle Desert in Sumeru, a remnant of King Deshret's civilisation. It connects to the underground Rock Cavern Area at the southwest of the Mausoleum of King Deshret.

Its ruins are full of puzzle machinery: Scarlet Sand Slate puzzles (full clearance needs Clearance Level 3), a Plinth of the Secret Rites, Primal Barriers, Primal Embers, Sconces and Torches, Large Fan Blades, Verity Cells, Forged Primal Light with a Replicator Keystone, a Sacred Seal, a torch puzzle and a Time Trial Challenge.

Geography: Ruins in the red sands of the Hypostyle Desert, linked by passage to the Mausoleum's southwest rock cavern.

Dangers: Only fungi are listed as common enemies; the main hazards are the ruins' mechanisms.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is an explorable ruin, with no later changes recorded in the sources.

248.comment: The Dune of Magma: Scarlet Sand Slate puzzles
248.content: Scarlet Sand Slate is a gadget used to solve some puzzles in these ruins; completing all of them requires Clearance Level 3.

249.content:
The Mausoleum of King Deshret (also: King Deshret's Mausoleum, Mausoleum of King Deshret): The Mausoleum of King Deshret is the huge pyramid in the Hypostyle Desert of Sumeru's Great Red Sand that has long been taken for the tomb of King Deshret (Al-Ahmar), the Lord of Deserts. For years a great cyclone turned on its summit and researchers never learned why. In the Golden Slumber quests the Traveler, Paimon and Tirzad's expedition find the way in through a mural passage in Khemenu Temple and discover that the pyramid is only one corner of a far larger palace: a mausoleum with an empty sarcophagus, an underworld-like Duat Hall, a Great Hall of Truths and, at its highest point, Aaru's Shut.

The Scarlet Sand Slate describes it as the place where King Deshret left a golden husk while his intelligence lies elsewhere, with many more temples beneath it. After Dual Evidence the cyclone is permanently gone and the summit is open.

Geography: Rises from the Hypostyle Desert in the Great Red Sand. Three levels are mapped: Main Hall, Middle Level and Lower Level. Opet Hall is an underground chamber just north; Duat Hall is reached by an underground waypoint directly south of the Mausoleum; the Great Hall of Truths connects to Duat Hall's south side; Aaru's Shut is the highest point.

Places: Entrance and Main Hall: giant doors, guardian statues and a sarcophagus chamber. Opet Hall: where blessings were said to reach the throne directly. Duat Hall: the bottomless hall, named after the Egyptian realm of the dead, where the guilty or disrespectful meet their destiny and those who pass the trials fly across an invisible river. Great Hall of Truths: where, by the slate, the wise and unafraid who bring praises to the king obtain unique gifts. Aaru's Shut: the summit.

People: Nobody lives there. In the quests the expedition of the Akademiya researcher Tirzad, with the desert guide Jebrael and his daughter Jeht, Benben (a small Primal Construct that is evidently connected to the ruins), the Traveler and Paimon enter first. Fatui forces and Eremites, including Samail, "the Twin Blades of Thutmose", are also working in the ruins. The Vahumana researcher Soheil of the Usaibia family, who explored the desert in his youth and never found Khemenu Temple or Khaj-Nisut, later learns of the interior through Dual Evidence.

History: The building belongs to King Deshret's civilisation. Little is dated: the Record of Aaru's Shut, a stone slate left near the summit, is the fragment of a diary by someone who says Al-Ahmar made them the architect of Aaru, a project meant to protect the people after a disaster that killed the writer's father; the writer's mother blamed Al-Ahmar for the calamity in Gurabad, which the writer rejects. The writer hopes Aaru will encompass the desert, restore Gurabad and carry out Al-Ahmar's ambition, and the record breaks off when they hear a loud explosion.

Quests: Golden Slumber (3.1), especially The Secret of Al-Ahmar: the party enters through a mural passage in Khemenu Temple, rides an elevator and reaches the Mausoleum, fights Primal Constructs, lights four Primal Torches to open a sarcophagus that proves empty, reaches the highest floor, falls into what seems to be a trap that separates the party, defeats Samail and the Fatui, and then pushes deeper into Opet Hall. Old Notes and New Friends (3.1): Dual Evidence and Soheil's Wish.

Dangers: Primal Constructs (Repulsors, Prospectors and guardians), traps that separate a party, mechanisms that need clearance, Fatui Skirmishers and Eremites in places, and Duat Hall's bottomless drop. Before Dual Evidence, the summit's cyclone made the pyramid unclimbable.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Mausoleum is open to those with the slate. The cyclone is off, the summit changed, and Aaru's Shut is a permanent destination through the Great Hall of Truths.

Soheil studied the Record and counts it as a major find. In the 6.6 Archon Quest the Mausoleum and Aaru's Shut became the allies' working base during the Irminsul crisis: the Seven Pillars agreed to open Aaru, and the reconfigured Aaru has since taken over Irminsul's role of collecting and storing information. No later change to the site is shown through 7.1.

250.comment: The Mausoleum of King Deshret: Aaru's Shut and the Record
250.content: Aaru's Shut is the highest point of the Mausoleum. The slate's description says it should have been paradise on earth and the crown jewel of the desert but now looks very different. The word Shut in the name is, according to the wiki, from the Egyptian word for shadow. At the summit the Traveler defeats a guardian construct and finds a chest with the Record of Aaru's Shut.

251.comment: The Mausoleum of King Deshret: The Great Hall of Truths and Duat Hall
251.content: Duat Hall needs Ferryman's Clearance, granted when Dual Evidence starts. It is a bottomless hall, linked to the trial places of Rebirth, Breath and Swallowing. Visitors who pass reach the Great Hall of Truths, where a giant device and four plinths open a path. According to the slate, those who bring praises before the king, who are wise and who do not fear the dark may obtain unique gifts here. A portal beyond the plinths leads to a second giant device; once its three Primal Torches (the "embers of the sun") are lit, the device lifts the party to the summit.

252.content:
The Orchard of Pairidaeza (also: Eternal Oasis, Orchard of Pairidaeza, Paradise of Eternal Peace): The Orchard of Pairidaeza, or Eternal Oasis, is a hidden garden beneath Mt. Damavand in the Desert of Hadramaveth, Sumeru. King Deshret built it on a divine nail as a cemetery and memorial for the Goddess of Flowers, preserving a single moment forever: animals, trees and even the water are frozen in place. It can only be entered through Deshret's Glass Goblet above it.

Desert tribes tell of it as a paradise where the slumbering goddess is guarded by Ferigees, the last mother of the Jinn. When the Traveler, Jeht and the Jinni Liloupar reach it in The Dirge of Bilqis, Liloupar finds that the goddess is not there.

Geography: Beneath the Goblet, the oasis is a still, bright garden of trees and a lake. Everything is fixed in place, including the water, which can be walked on. A central island holds three chairs, one for each of Sumeru's three god-kings, with abbreviated names written in Deshret Script. A withered Irminsul-like tree stands beside the island, which the wiki reads as showing that a Celestial Nail fell on Mt. Damavand.

History: In a time only the Jinn could recall, King Deshret built a cemetery for his beloved, the Goddess of Flowers. With gems under the deep sands as a power source and the Jinn's help, he made an eternal oasis. Later tribes spread legends of it as ever-flourishing, ruled by the slumbering goddess and guarded by Ferigees. The Tanit, Uzza, Shimti and other matriarchal tribes call themselves Daughters of the Flower Goddess and seek the oasis for its endless knowledge.

Accounts: Three views of the place exist side by side. The tribes believe in a living paradise with a sleeping goddess. Ferigees believed the goddess lay in the oasis and defended it for that reason. Liloupar, after seeing it, concluded the goddess is gone and that the Lord of the Sands lied to the Jinn. The artifact text calls it a cemetery and argues that eternity is no paradise.

Status as of 7.1: In The Eternal Dream, Ever Lush the equilibrium device that kept the oasis still was broken as the party entered, and the Jinni Liloupar says the oasis is destined to be buried by the sands in time. Jeht left her father's axe and her mother's notes beside a tree there.

Liloupar says the Goddess of Flowers is not there and feels no hatred, only emptiness. Jeht, a member of the Tanit tribe, finds calm in the place. Babel, the Tanit matriarch, is told of the oasis afterwards. After the Akasha Pulses quest, one throne bears Rukkhadevata's name in Deshret Script, according to the wiki (version 3.6 or later).

253.comment: The Orchard of Pairidaeza: Ferigees and the Glass Goblet
253.content: Ferigees, a Jinni who served Nabu Malikata and later King Deshret, guarded the oasis from a machine atop Deshret's Glass Goblet. She called Liloupar a traitor who had brought Gurabad down with honeyed words, refused her entry, and was destroyed when the Traveler fought her mechanical defenders. Her last words say the empty tomb will crumble. Desert legends call her the last mother of the Jinn, a gate guardian who blesses every mortal who comes to her.

254.comment: The Orchard of Pairidaeza: Jeht at the Oasis
254.content: Jeht came seeking the place her parents had spoken of. At the center of the oasis she set down her mother's notes and her father's axe beside a tree, which can be found there later. She said she might return after her adventures to lie down beside her parents' memory. Her mother's notes contain a lullaby of the eternal oasis written for her daughter.

255.content:
The Palace of Alcazarzaray (also: Palace of Alcazarzaray, Alcazarzaray): Dori asked only that it be large and extravagant, so Kaveh had almost full creative freedom. The Archive shows a purple garden before the palace where flowers dance and warblers sing. Visitors find the palace staffed by a butler, merchants and students, and people praise its architect while many do not know who owns it.

Geography: The palace stands in the Dharma Forest area of Lokapala Jungle, in the depths of the woods, just north of Sumeru City according to Dori's wiki page. A purple garden lies before it. The wiki lists Padisarah and Nilotpala Lotus as local specialties and a Four-Leaf Sigil, Auspicious Branch, Dendro Elemental Monument and bouncy mushrooms nearby.

People: Dori, the owner, appears only intermittently; her butler Goshtasb says the Lord is not in and promises to introduce visitors when she returns. Other open-world figures at the palace include Gaston (a trainee reporter of The Steambird who travelled from Fontaine to interview the owner), the merchants Rajavi and Zhila, the student Sasani, and Ehsan, Mandana, Shaghayeh and Soltani. Kaveh, the architect, does not live there but still owes Dori for it.

History: At some point after getting rich, Dori had Kaveh build it. Kaveh gave the project everything. Near the end of construction the Withering spread in the night, destroying the worksite and leaving it beyond saving. Dori did not want to continue, but Kaveh had already invested too much and knew how rare such an opportunity was, so he took a loan from her and rebuilt it, leaving him in massive debt (Kaveh's fourth character story).

Quests: - The Price of a Wish (Hangout Event: Kaveh, Act I, The Pendulum of Weal and Woe, 3.7) begins here: Kaveh and the Traveler meet Dori after failing to find a sponsor for his education-and-culture project. She finally agrees to fund the project, which is aimed at giving the desert's children books, and gets Kaveh to waive his commission and shoulder the project.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the palace is still owned by Dori and open to visitors, and no later canon changes it.

256.comment: The Palace of Alcazarzaray: Kaveh and the palace
256.content: Kaveh, the Akademiya-trained architect known as the Light of Kshahrewar, designed the palace for Dori. He calls it his best work. The project cost him far more than it earned him, and he lives with Alhaitham because of it. Character details belong in character.kaveh.

257.comment: The Palace of Alcazarzaray: Dori's staff and visitors
257.content: Goshtasb, the butler, defers everything to the Lord and says Dori will be in later. Gaston, a young reporter from The Steambird, wants a scoop and is certain that the owner must be someone very important. Staff call Dori Lord, and her formal title is Lord Sangemah Bay.

258.content:
The Rain's End: The Rain's End is a location in Apam Woods, in Sumeru's Dharma Forest. It is where the Traveler first gains access to the Varuna Contraption, the Aranara-tended device that sustains the rain cycle of the forest.

It unlocks during the Varuna Gatha world quests, at the end of A Prayer for Rain on the Fecund Land. Its viewpoint text says there is no rain here, yet it is the birthplace of rain, and that the purification of the Vana rains begins and ends here.

Geography: Underground in Apam Woods, in the Ashavan Realm. The southernmost contraption is found here, and it unlocks the others.

People: The Aranara Arapandu, Aranakula, Arabalika and Arakunti repair the contraption in the quest series. Its original makers are long dead, and the Nara Varuna, who once fixed it when it went wrong, is nowhere to be seen.

History: The Varuna Contraption was a device made by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata to summon timely rains in a stretch of desert, according to the original Chinese text of an item description. The English text omits this detail.

Quests: Varuna Gatha, including Memory of Stone, Irate Iron Chunk and Slumbering Roots, then A Prayer for Rain on the Fecund Land. Completing the series lets the Traveler change the weather in Apam Woods; this is a gameplay mechanic.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the contraption works and Apam Woods keeps its rain cycle; no later changes were found.

259.content: The Varuna Contraption controls the Varunastra, a huge pillar of water that creates the rain cycle nourishing the once-desert forest of Apam Woods. By default the weather alternates between sunny and rainy on a twelve-hour cycle, which the Traveler can override (gameplay mechanic).

260.content:
The Sands of Al-Azif (also: Sands of Al-Azif, Moonblue Canals): The Sands of Al-Azif are a comparatively flat part of the Desert of Hadramaveth in Sumeru's Great Red Sand. Wenut, the huge eyeless sand-worms of the desert, roam the surface, and the Wenut Tunnels run in the earth beneath. The City of the Deceased, a one-time domain, lies within.

The area came with the desert in version 3.4. Its viewpoint, the Moonblue Canals, preserves a desert tale that three canals once met here and watered fertile fields and rich gardens; nothing of that age remains.

Geography: One of the flatter, more open stretches of the desert, with the Wenut Tunnels, a system of caverns, below it. On the surface, Wenut rise from the sand to strike at travellers.

Places: The Wenut Tunnels (the caverns of the Wenut), the City of the Deceased domain, and the Moonblue Canals viewpoint site.

History: Canon gives the sands no dated history. The Moonblue Canals viewpoint relays an old desert tale: this was where three canals met, feeding fields and gardens, but only the faded shade of that dream remains.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the sands are an open, permanent part of the Desert of Hadramaveth.

No change to the area is recorded after version 3.4.

261.comment: The Sands of Al-Azif: City of the Deceased
261.content: A one-time domain in the Sands of Al-Azif (the wiki lists the Wenut Tunnels as its point of interest). Its single level, Suspiration of the Deceased, is a walk through winding corridors with fungi, slimes and hilichurls, and Dendro and Anemo are recommended. Its blurb: the halls of death do not welcome the deluge of living things.

262.comment: The Sands of Al-Azif: The Moonblue Canals
262.content: Viewpoint in the Sands of Al-Azif. Ancient desert tales say this was where three canals met and nourished fertile fields and rich gardens, but only the dulled shades of a dream remain.

263.content:
The Sands of Three Canals (also: Sands of Three Canals, Land of Three Canals): The Sands of Three Canals are an elevated part of the Desert of Hadramaveth in Sumeru, north of Mt. Damavand. Desert folk still keep the name of a lost river and the green gardens that once lay here. The Fane of Panjvahe, a one-time domain, stands in it.

The area was added in version 3.4. Today the only thing the old river carries is grinding gravel.

Geography: High ground in the Great Red Sand, north of Mt. Damavand, around which sandstorms never cease.

Places: The Fane of Panjvahe, a lonesome hall where ancient mechanisms (Primal Constructs) and desert bandits (Eremites) patrol. It is a one-time domain with a single level, Fading Rumination.

History: Loading-screen text recalls a beautiful river, navy as a moonlit night, that once flowed here in an age of songsters and flowers, marble colonnades and glazed domes. Desert people still cherish the green and blue memory and the name Three Canals; the river now carries only grinding gravel.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the sands are an open, permanent subarea of the desert.

No change to the area is recorded after version 3.4.

264.comment: The Sands of Three Canals: Fane of Panjvahe
264.content: One-time domain in the Sands of Three Canals. The game says that when travellers step into this lonesome hall, the ancient mechanisms and desert bandits patrolling it emerge from the shadows to punish the reckless. Enemies are Primal Constructs and Eremites (Desert Clearwater, Daythunder, Crossbow and Galehunter types).

265.content:
Thinkers' Theater (also: Thinkers Theater): The Thinkers' Theater is the theatre area of the Veluriyam Mirage, the bottle-domain from the limited-time Version 3.8 event Secret Summer Paradise. Zosimos, a stage-director replica, puts on plays at its central theatre. A troupe of seven Hydro Eidolons that speaks as one voice, Daiya, stages three shows around the grounds. It was event-only.

The area unlocks with the Act III quest Treehouse Theater: Candlelit Shadows Dancing, and the world quest series Daiya's Three-Day Reverie starts here. A hidden Broadcasting Station above the central theatre opens after all three plays are completed.

Geography: Points of interest: the Central Theater (Zosimos' stage), the Director's Treehouse (where he builds props and writes scripts), an Ancient Castle in the north (always night once Petrifying Gaze is started), a Skycastle in the south, and the Broadcasting Station over the theatre. The area includes Waverider Waypoints, Dendrograna and Choo-Choo Cart track.

People: Zosimos is a moustached, Fontaine-dressed stage director, a Hydro Eidolon replica of a real prop designer who dreamed of directing. Daiya is the shared voice of seven Hydro Eidolons (Director-in-Chief, Engineer, Fake Playwright, Food Manager, Harum-Scarum, Hustler and Loafer), who talk through a device with a prerecorded vocabulary made by Zosimos and Idyia.

Quests: In Treehouse Theater: Candlelit Shadows Dancing, the Traveler, Klee, Kaeya and Kokomi find Zosimos in his treehouse. He holds the last component of the central hub and will give it up only after they perform his script about a thief and a mage. Klee, Kaeya and Kokomi act while the Traveler works backstage. Afterwards he gives them a bottle-lamp component and lets Klee and Kaeya keep their costumes.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 canon, the Thinkers' Theater is part of a time-limited area from Version 3.8; no later story returns to it.

After the event Zosimos says he has finally seen his own show, got useful feedback, and means to become a true director.

266.content: Zosimos is a Hydro Eidolon replica of a Fontaine-dressed prop designer who dreamed of directing. He is warm, grateful and open to criticism from Paimon and Idyia. His own story is a play about a thief and a mage. He calls the Hydro Eidolons dependable partners and says the outdoor stages cannot run without them.

267.comment: Thinkers' Theater: Daiya, the Seven Players
267.content: Daiya is the shared name of seven Hydro Eidolons that speak through a prerecorded-word device: Director-in-Chief (leader), Engineer, Fake Playwright, Food Manager, Harum-Scarum, Hustler and Loafer. They narrate and stage the three plays of Daiya's Three-Day Reverie.

268.content:
Tomb of Carouses (also: Lesser Mausoleum of King Deshret): The Tomb of Carouses is a small cone-shaped ruin in the Dune of Carouses, in the Great Red Sand of Sumeru's Hypostyle Desert. It looks like a scaled-down copy of the Mausoleum of King Deshret. Nobody in canon says who built it.

It is a point of interest rather than a settlement: a sealed tomb with a puzzle mechanism and a modest hoard. The scholar Soheil named it in his old expedition notes, and the Traveler later returns to it on his behalf.

Geography: The tomb stands on the Dune of Carouses within the Great Red Sand, part of the Land of Lower Setekh. The dune and its surroundings hold hilichurls and fungi, and scarabs can be gathered nearby. The tomb is a cone-shaped structure, far smaller than the Mausoleum of King Deshret.

Places: Inside, a mechanism called a Prism of Khaj-Nisut must be activated, as in the larger Mausoleum. Doing so changes its colour but opens nothing by itself; a second switch has to be found, after which a passage is heard opening deeper in. A chest at the end holds a stone slate.

History: Its origin is unknown. When Soheil's archaeology team reached it on day 45 of his expedition, they found it shut by the same mysterious power that had kept them out of the Transparent Ruins, and he gave it its name provisionally. The next day his team was attacked by Eremites calling themselves Thutmose, led by two young men, one of whom (Samail) wanted them dead while the other (Jebrael) let them go.

Atmosphere: A hushed, wind-scoured sandstone cone, quiet apart from the hum of old mechanisms. It feels like a sibling of the great Mausoleum, with fewer rooms and less treasure.

Dangers: A Primal Construct: Reshaper is listed as an elite enemy at the site, and fungi and hilichurls roam the surrounding dune. Elsewhere in the desert, Eremite groups may be encountered.

Quests: Desert's Remembrance, a world quest in the Old Notes and New Friends chain that follows Soheil's Wish. The Traveler searches the tomb and brings what is found back to Soheil.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tomb is unchanged and open to explore. No later story involves it.

key: Record of the Tomb of Carouses
The Sheep the Bird and the Crocodile
269.comment: Tomb of Carouses: Record of the Tomb of Carouses
269.content: A stone slate found in the tomb's chest, described as a record left by a lost civilisation. It carries a fable, The Sheep, the Bird, and the Crocodile. A sheep chief sends seven lambs to find fresh pasture; a bird, for its own reasons, sends them far north; a crocodile there pities them and escorts them home. The bird, ashamed, joins them, and on meeting the chief the crocodile devours the sheep and weeps afterwards. The moral: do not trust the meek, the wise, or those who shed tears.

270.content:
Towers of Betrayal (also: Tower of Betrayal): Those in the Hypostyle Desert, Land of Lower Setekh and Land of Upper Setekh stand on the surface but must be opened from within through the desert's cave networks. Those in the Desert of Hadramaveth are partly or fully buried and are entered at the main entrance. Each has a ground-level room with a blue crystal, and some have a basement reached by an elevator. A recorded memory of the priest Kasala, shown in Secret of the Scorching Desert, speaks of temples built by King Deshret's priests and filled with Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's power of life.

Geography: Towers stand in the Hypostyle Desert (northwest of the Mausoleum of King Deshret), the Land of Lower Setekh (south of Abdju Pit), the Land of Upper Setekh (west of the Valley of Dahri), and in the Desert of Hadramaveth (northwest of Khaj-Nisut, northwest of Safhe Shatranj, in Debris of Panjvahe, and in Wadi Al-Majuj).

History: Desert tradition, quoted in the Archive, holds that the obelisks have stood since King Deshret died and shame the desert kings who broke faith with him. The Archive adds that they may be older than those short-lived kingdoms, and the real story is lost.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the towers still stand, three can be reactivated by the Traveler, and no later canon changes their meaning.

271.content:
Treasures Street: Treasures Street is the liveliest street in Sumeru City, one of the city's named districts alongside the Grand Bazaar and the Akademiya. It is a busy commercial strip with vendors, an Adventurers' Guild branch, Puspa Café and the Citadel of Regzar among its listed places. Its local specialty is padisarah.

Mercenaries of the Corps of Thirty, students, researchers and shopkeepers all pass through it.

Places: Places tied to the street include Puspa Café and the Citadel of Regzar, where Rukh Shah and other Corps of Thirty members are listed. Barmak, Mahamata at the Exchange, is on the roster, as are the Adventurers' Guild branch staff Kamal (branch master) and Katheryne (receptionist).

People: Listed street figures include Barmak, Hatim (a self-proclaimed millionaire), Mawyo (a self-described freelancer), Kimiya (a student), Mansur (a researcher), and the mercenaries Farid and Hakan of the Corps of Thirty.

Governance: No governing body is named for the street itself. The Exchange's Mahamata, a tax officer and Corps of Thirty mercenaries work in or near it, within the Akademiya's jurisdiction over the city.

Culture: Trade and talk: sweets and padisarah, jewelry and smithing, haggling, card games and storytelling in the café, and colourful characters boasting of wealth or freelance work.

Atmosphere: Lively and crowded, with a different mix of people by day and night: a hairdresser and a freelancer by day, a tax officer and café regulars after dark.

Dangers: No dangers are described in canon.

Travel: Treasures Street lies within Sumeru City, listed with the Grand Bazaar and the Akademiya as one of its districts. The wiki lists padisarah as its only local specialty.

Status as of 7.1: Still the city's busiest street as of 7.1, as far as the sources show.

272.content:
Tree of Dreams (also: Araja's Tree of Dreams): The Tree of Dreams is a mystic, seemingly sentient tree growing in the heart of the forest at Vanarana in Sumeru. After the cataclysm, the Aranara chief Araja turned his original body into it, so that only in its dream could the Aranara sustain a Vanarana large enough for them all.

Players unlock it with the world quest Trees and Dreams after The World of Aranara. In the Dream State it turns from green to luminous purple. Offering Dendro Sigils here raises Vanarana's Favor for rewards.

Geography: Stands at the centre of Vanarana in the Dharma Forest. It looks different in the real and dream worlds: green and leafy in one, luminescent purple in the other. It is marked on the map only after it is first visited.

People: Araja, the Aranara village chief, is the tree. His physical body can no longer move, but his mind remains intact and can manifest a body inside the dream. Over about 500 years he has lost many old memories, but he remembers taking part in the last Festival Utsava and being close to Araji, Arapacati and Aramuhukunda.

History: When the original Vanarana was destroyed by the Withering in the calamity, Araja sacrificed his physical form and became the Tree of Dreams. This created the dream Vanarana, where the Aranara live in peace away from Sumeru's devastation and the harmful Nara.

Quests: Trees and Dreams, a dialogue-free world quest, only shows the Traveler where the tree is. The quest begins after the Traveler speaks with Araja during The World of Aranara.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tree is alive and the dream Vanarana is maintained. Nothing found in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content changes it.

273.content: An offering system at the tree, levelled by giving Dendro Sigils in groups of 35. Before version 3.6 the maximum level was capped at 20, 30 and 40 in versions 3.0, 3.1-3.3 and 3.4-3.5. This is a gameplay mechanic.

274.content:
Tulaytullah (also: City of Sapphire, Tulaytullah Tighnarians): Tulaytullah, the "City of Sapphire", was an ancient desert city-state in what is now the Hypostyle Desert of Sumeru. After King Deshret's civilisation fell, the priest Hermanubis brought the Tighnarians there and founded the original Temple of Silence, and the city became famed for wisdom, canals, sapphire domes and gardens. Wars among the desert kingdoms ended its glory. Only its garden is still preserved, in the Garden of Endless Pillars.

Its story is told in fragments: weapon and artifact texts, obelisk inscriptions in the Mausoleum of King Deshret, the Temple of Silence's own history, and a few quests. Legend says the city arose from the tears of Nabu Malikata after the fall of her fellow Angels. Refugees from Tulaytullah helped found Aaru Village and spread across Sumeru; some Eremite tribes and some desert-born people still trace their descent to it.

Geography: The city stood at the site of today's Garden of Endless Pillars in the Hypostyle Desert, part of the Great Red Sand. Accounts describe a lattice of shimmering canals, buildings with sapphire domes and lush emerald gardens full of padisarah flowers and pomegranates.

People: Tulaytullah was home to the Tulaytullah Tighnarians, priests who had come with Hermanubis, and in later ages to an elite of nobles and scholars. Its better-known figures in the sources are King Humayun, the young noble Goudarz (later called Saleb Dowleh), the queen regent Makhaira, her lover Xiphos, the prince Faramarz and a blind poet who later led refugees to Aaru Village.

History: After King Deshret sacrificed himself and his civilisation splintered, Hermanubis led the Tighnarians to Tulaytullah and set up the original Temple of Silence, which kept the knowledge that survived and held remnants of forbidden knowledge at bay. A little over a hundred years after Deshret's death war reached the desert. A Gurabad king besieged the city and demanded the Temple be handed over; the city's elite sided with him and blamed the Temple's knowledge for corruption. Hermanubis, his strength spent, broke himself into pieces and passed his power to his followers, who defeated the invaders but frightened the citizens. The Temple of Silence and the Tighnarians then left for the rainforest, and Tulaytullah fell into the wider wars.

Status as of 7.1: Tulaytullah is long gone. Its remembered gardens are all that remains, preserved in the Garden of Endless Pillars. It cannot be visited as a city.

Its descendants live on across Sumeru, and Aaru Village was founded by refugees from Tulaytullah and other failing desert kingdoms. As of Version 7.1 nothing found changes this.

275.comment: Tulaytullah: Hermanubis and the Temple of Silence
275.content: Hermanubis was a Tighnarian priest who brought followers to Tulaytullah and, according to Thoth, took in many who had nowhere else to go. The Temple of Silence he founded there kept the surviving knowledge of Deshret's civilisation and, through his power, kept forbidden knowledge at bay. The Tighnarians themselves came from a place called Tighnar and had left it to serve Deshret before his death. When the city turned on the Temple, the Tighnarians withdrew to the rainforest.

276.content:
Tunigi Hollow: Tunigi Hollow is a subarea of Gavireh Lajavard in Sumeru's Girdle of the Sands, long a great breach carved by the Abyss. Five hundred years ago, in the cataclysm, gods fought Abyssal monsters here, and the Archon Egeria was slain. The Harvisptokhm, a tree grown from her remains, seals it.

Added in version 3.6, it is the site of the Hymn of Tir Yazad quests (Khvarena of Good and Evil). A path can be opened from the Hollow into the Harvisptokhm by the Rite of Chinvat.

Geography: A hollow, ringed by trees whose hollows hold the Great Songs of Khvarena, in Gavireh Lajavard. Gray crystal and Fravashi Trees dot it. After the Rite of Chinvat, jumping into the Hollow sends the player to the Harvisptokhm instead.

History: During the cataclysm, the Abyss spewed monsters and forbidden-knowledge pollution from here. Several gods ventured to suppress it, including Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and Egeria, the old Hydro Archon.

Places: The Harvisptokhm in the Vourukasha Oasis, reached through a hole at the Hollow or at its stump. Its heart, the Gaokerena, holds the Flower of Sanctity.

Culture: The Pari treat the Harvisptokhm as their god. The Order of Skeptics once kept its seal through ritual, but lost its connection to the Pari and let the defilement build up.

Dangers: Hilichurls, Fatui Skirmishers, rifthounds (some Thundercraven, some Rockfond), fungi, and a Consecrated Fanged Beast after the Hymn's second part. Abyssal defilement in the Hollow and tree.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Hollow is cleansed, with the Sign of Apaosha sealed and a clean path into the Harvisptokhm.

Before the quests the Hollow was a great breach, with its pathway blocked and the Harvisptokhm near collapse.

277.content: A rite of the Pari performed at Tunigi Hollow with the Great Songs of Khvarena. In the Hymn of Tir Yazad (Part 1), Sorush, with Mihir and Rashnu, uses it to open a pathway into the Harvisptokhm, linking the Hollow with the Sign in the sky, which loading screens call unexplained.

278.content:
Valley of Dahri: The Valley of Dahri is a wind-eroded valley in the Land of Upper Setekh, in Sumeru's Great Red Sand. A huge, sealed Ruin Golem, a war machine from Khaenri'ah (called Dahri in old Sumeru), lies in it. Scattered Akademiya research notes tell of the desert's strange hilichurl-like creatures and the Abyss.

The Valley and its golem feature in the world quest Afratu's Dilemma, added in version 3.1, in which the Traveler silences the machine's autonomous guns.

Geography: Open wind-carved country in the Land of Upper Setekh, so named because the land lies toward the sun at noon. A cavern north of the area's Statue of The Seven leads into a Ruin Golem part, and the golem itself towers over the valley.

Places: The Ruin Golem, and the cavern and arm passages through which one enters it, past a seal of three Suda's Flow clusters. Inside lie the cockpit and old orders written by the machine's former crew.

People: No settlement. In Afratu's Dilemma the Vahumana Mahamata Afratu, on temporary assignment, asks adventurers to deal with the golem because the Eremites she commissioned from the Citadel of Regzar have been slow to arrive.

History: The golem's old orders are the main record of its past. They name a Knight Commander Hadura, honoured as Sentinel of the Golden Hall for stalling the beasts, under Marshal Regent Anfortas. Sealed orders tell the crew to abandon the machine for the Marshal's machine and to leave the wounded with supplies in a safe place, with the promise to return for them.

Dangers: Before the quest, the golem fires beams indiscriminately at anything living near it. Inside: Ruin Guards, fungi, Dendro Samachurls, and Wooden Shieldwall Mitachurls.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the golem lies silent in its valley, its autonomous guns off after Afratu's Dilemma.

Afratu reported the anomaly to the Akademiya, and expects the other sealed golems to show problems if ley lines are the cause.

279.content: World quest in the Valley of Dahri. The Traveler and Paimon find the Mahamata Afratu worried about a Ruin Golem that has begun to attack. They bait it into blasting the entrance open, break the three Suda's Flow seals, and switch off its autonomous targeting from the cockpit. Vines inside suggest a ley line cause to Afratu, who passes the report to the Akademiya.

280.content:
Vanarana (also: Mahavanaranapna, Vanarana of Great Dreams, Vanarana village, Aranara village): Vanarana is the secret home of the Aranara, the small plant-like forest spirits of Sumeru's Dharma Forest. It exists twice: as a quiet clearing in the real forest, and as Mahavanaranapna ("Vanarana of Great Dreams"), a dream version where the Aranara actually live, with houses, a stage, a stall and gardens. Adults normally never find it; children and trusted friends can.

The two versions are linked by the Tree of Dreams, the elder Araja, who anchors the dream to the real world. A visitor switches between them by playing the Aranara's "Rhythm of the Great Dream" on a lyre beside a Silapna by the central pond. The village is warm, a little childlike and sentimental, and built around memories, songs and shared meals.

Geography: Vanarana lies in the Dharma Forest of Sumeru, in the rainforest north of the desert. The wiki treats an "area" (the surroundings, including a southern stretch not touched by the dream) and a "village" proper, centred on a pond. A small garden cave at the west end grows Viparyas. In the dream version the lighting is dreamlike, a Statue of The Seven stands there, and the Tree of Dreams glows violet instead of green.

Places: Notable spots: the central pond; the Silapna east of it that toggles dream and reality; Araja's house; a festival stage; the stall of Aramani, the Aranara vendor; the nursery garden at the west end; and the Tree of Dreams in its cave.

People: The residents are Aranara, each with a name beginning "Ara-" and each with a personal tune. Araja is the elder and village chief; Arama is the first villager to befriend the Traveler and sets them tasks to win the others' trust; Arana is a gentle Aranara tied to Rana in Vimara Village. Others include Arakavi, Arapacati, Aramani, Arakara, Aranakula, Arapandu, Aranakin and Aragaru. In total more than two dozen are named in the village.

History: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata created the Aranara after she left the desert to make the Dharma Forest. They first lived in Old Vanarana and befriended humans. When the Cataclysm struck they fought the invaders from the Abyss, then withdrew, set up a new Vanarana and hid it within a dream anchored by the Tree of Dreams.

Travel: Humans cannot normally find the way. In the world's story, a visitor plays the five-note Rhythm of the Great Dream on a lyre in front of the strange arch to enter, and again at the Silapna to move between real and dream Vanarana. The Traveler borrowed a Mondstadt-style lyre from Amadhiah in Vimara Village.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Vanarana is at peace, with the Aranara safe in the dream village and the threat from Marana's Avatar ended.

Old Vanarana began to recover after Marana's Avatar was destroyed; Arama is now an Ashvattha Tree. Arana and Rana have set off on a journey together.

281.comment: Vanarana: Tree of Dreams and Araja
281.content: The Tree of Dreams grows in a cave at the heart of Vanarana and seems sentient. Per the wiki, Araja turned his original body into the tree after the Cataclysm so he could sustain a dream large enough for the other Aranara. His body cannot move, but his mind can manifest a body inside the dream. At Festival Utsava he reveals that he cannot leave the dream because he is the Tree of Dreams. Over about 500 years he has lost many memories.

282.content: The Aranara's festival, held in the dream Vanarana during Aranyaka. The Traveler and Paimon collect a flower from each Aranara as a token of friendship, everyone plays the Rhythm of the Great Dream on the stage, and Arama weaves the flowers into a garland for the Traveler. It is a permanent quest and not a limited-time event.

283.comment: Vanarana: Old Vanarana and Marana's Avatar
283.content: Old Vanarana was the Aranara's home for hundreds of years before the Cataclysm. Afterwards they sealed Marana's Avatar deep inside with four layers of seals, including three Inscriptions of Remembrance by Aramaha, Arayama and Araji, who became Vasara Trees. Corruption still leaked, until the Traveler and Arama broke the seals, entered the Land of Grounded Dreams and destroyed the Avatar in Aranyaka Part III. Old Vanarana then began to heal.

284.content: A small garden in a cave at the west end, tended by Aranakula and Arakara, who grow "happy Viparyas". The name is unofficial wiki usage. After the quest The Viparyas of Vanarana the 13 Viparyas can be harvested; in the real clearing the plants are Sweet Flowers instead.

285.content:
Vanarana Nursery: Vanarana Nursery is an unofficial name for a small garden in a cave at the west end of Vanarana in Sumeru. The Aranara Arakara and Aranakula tend it, working hard to grow happy Viparyas.

Arakara is always there; Aranakula returns after the Traveler helps restore the Varuna Contraption in A Prayer for Rain on the Fecund Land (this timing is flagged as unverified). In the real Vanarana, Varsha can be found at the nursery after Giving Flowers.

Geography: A cave garden on the western edge of Vanarana. It looks different in the dream version, with blooming Viparyas, and the real version, with Sweet Flowers.

People: Arakara and Aranakula, Aranara gardeners. Varsha visits the nursery in the real Vanarana after Giving Flowers.

Quests: The Viparyas of Vanarana and Giving Flowers, both world quests.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no change was found.

286.content:
Veluriyam Mirage (also: Bottleland): The Veluriyam Mirage, nicknamed Bottleland, is a pocket world inside a wondrous glass bottle, said to lie hidden in Sumeru's desert. It appears only in the limited-time 3.8 event Secret Summer Paradise. Its caretaker is Idyia, an Oceanid who fled Fontaine, and the place is built to grant visitors a quiet respite and their heart's desires.

The invitation came through Klee's mother Alice, who sent Klee a letter and a "Magic Invite". Klee, Kaeya, the Traveler and Paimon arrive, meet Collei, Eula and Sangonomiya Kokomi already inside, and find the Mirage's central hub broken. The party gathers three missing parts to start it again; the deeper reveal is that the town's residents are Hydro Eidolon copies of earlier guests.

Geography: Inside the bottle is a humid, green and watery pocket world, a striking contrast with the desert outside. The official loading text calls it a beautiful, quiet domain where special Hydro life-forms live. Game-wise it is a limited-time area rather than an actual Domain, although the story calls it one. The main hub is the Silver Bottle Courtyard, with a giant wheel, the Central Hub, above it; the Overgrown Valley holds a cavern with a painter's hidden mural.

Places: Key places: the Silver Bottle Courtyard (arrival point); the fairground and its big tent run by Maymunah, a Spantamad scholar; Zosimos's treehouse theatre; the cart area; the Overgrown Valley; and the Central Hub with the Ferris-wheel ride that works again at the end.

People: Idyia is the Oceanid caretaker, called "Aunty Desert" by Klee and "Mud Fairy" by Paimon, a wish-granting fairy of local legend. Maymunah runs the fairground; Zosimos is a stage director; Lessig, a visitor from the Lawrence Clan, came to the Mirage to try to restore his family's honour and caused the breakdown by accident. Eula came after hearing a Lawrence Clan cousin had gone to Sumeru, Collei helped guide the group, and Kokomi came looking for the lost Shinrou Casket.

History: Idyia fled Fontaine after the old waters grew full of pain and hatred (she speaks of Oceanids fleeing, and mentions Rhodeia, who has since settled in Qingce Village in Liyue), and collapsed in the desert. According to the wiki's profile, Alice met her and granted her wish for a place away from everyone by giving her this bottle. Over time travelers found it, their wishes were granted, and they left gifts that powered the Mirage and were copied by Hydro Eidolons.
